items.body_text:
There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed.
About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.
On Sunday, seven armed groups from around the country, including the TPLF, announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, aimed at deposing the government in Addis Ababa. Then, on Wednesday, the TPLF seized control of three airports from federal police. The state-owned carrier, Ethiopian Airlines, said it had suspended flights to the region “due to the current situation”.
The TPLF also launched attacks into Afar and Amhara. A humanitarian source in Afar told Agence France-Presse there were heavy artillery attacks by the group on Thursday as they attempted to take control of the town of Yallo, near the Tigrayan border.
Flights to the historic Ethiopian town of Lalibela were also suspended on Thursday because of nearby fighting, while people in Tigray stocked up on food and cash, with one resident telling Reuters that people there feared they could face siege conditions similar to those during the previous war.
A resident of Adigrat, a city close to the Eritrean border, described panic-buying and shops emptying. “Food shortages are worsening as market shelves sit empty … Essential medicines remain scarce and astronomically expensive,” he told Reuters. “Daily survival has become a constant calculation.”
The TPLF’s vice-president, Amanuel Assefa, told AFP: “We are in the situation of full-blown war now.” He confirmed Tigrayan forces were fighting alongside local armed groups in Afar and Amhara.
The group took control of Abala, also on the Tigray-Afar border, on Wednesday, a foreign security source based in Ethiopia told AFP, while a TPLF source said they had seized several other towns in Afar. The foreign security source also said there was fighting around the Amhara town of Weldiya – one of the few routes to the capital.
In its first public comments on the fighting, Ethiopia’s army said on Thursday it had foiled the attacks and killed, wounded or captured more than 500 enemy fighters.
Analysts say the TPLF has support from Ethiopia’s neighbour and historic adversary Eritrea, which fears landlocked Ethiopia is planning to invade its territory to gain access to the Red Sea. The TPLF’s Assefa told AFP “we have no information about Eritrea’s plan”. Asked if they would request Eritrean intervention, he said: “Not yet.”
The current fighting reflects shifting dynamics from the civil war, when Eritrea and Fano, an insurgent group that is now part of the new alliance, both fought with the government against the Tigrayans.
Speaking at the UN general assembly on Wednesday, the Ethiopian president, Taye Atske-Selassie Amde, decried “the forces of destruction and mayhem” and “interference in our internal affairs by adversarial elements”. He said Ethiopia had exercised “immense restraint” and made progress with its neighbours.
Abiy’s spokesperson, Billene Seyoum, said members of the alliance had been collaborating for a while with the financial backing of Eritrea. Eritrea has repeatedly denied similar accusations.
The TPLF ruled Ethiopia from 1991 to 2018 before being sidelined by the rise of Abiy, eventually triggering the civil war.
The renewed fighting marks the most serious challenge yet to the 2022 Pretoria agreement, which ended the civil war and maintained an uneasy calm until late last year, when clashes resumed.

items.title: Girl, 3, found dead at Surrey home
items.summary: Police believe girl’s death occurred in a ‘family setting’ and arrest a 31-year-old man on suspicion of murder
items.body_text:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a three-year-old girl was found dead at a home in Surrey.
Police were called to an address on Pyrcroft Road in Chertsey at 5.40pm on Thursday following reports of safety concerns.
Officers found the girl dead at the scene and arrested a 31-year-old man.
Surrey Police said the man was taken to hospital with a serious injury and would be taken into custody after receiving medical treatment.
The force’s Major Crime Team, which is leading the investigation, described the girl’s death as a “tragic incident” believed to have occurred “within a family setting”. Police are not considering additional suspects.
In a statement, a senior investigating officer from Surrey Police’s Major Crime Team said: “This is a tragic incident, and our officers are working hard to build a picture of what happened.
“We have made an arrest in connection with this incident and at this stage, we are not looking to identify anyone else in connection with our investigation. We have no reason to believe there is any risk to the public.
“There is a significant police presence in Pyrcroft Road and this will remain over the coming days.
“We appreciate that the incident itself, as well as the significant police presence, will be concerning for local residents and we would like to thank them for their co-operation as we conduct our investigation.”

items.title: Counter-terror police investigating ‘Iran-backed firebombing’
items.summary: Four vehicles set on fire outside London synagogue in ‘anti-Semitic hate incident’
items.body_text:
Sir Keir Starmer, who said earlier this month that the war in Iran was being used to divide Muslims and Jewish people, condemned the “deeply shocking” attack.
The Prime Minister, who met Jewish community leaders in Downing Street on Monday morning, said: “The idea that we live in a society where people should feel they need to hide their identity or their religion is, frankly, abhorrent.
“Anti-Semitism is an old hatred, but it requires constant vigilance to overcome it.”
But Suella Braverman, the Reform UK education spokesman, blamed the attacks on “years of weak leadership” by Labour and the Conservatives, who she accused of failing to tackle Islamism and anti-Israel marches.
She told The Telegraph: “All we get are warm words, ‘I’m shocked and I’m upset’, by prime ministers, whether it’s Starmer or Sunak, but nothing changes.
“Jews are leaving the country because they don’t feel safe here. They feel safer in Israel, a war zone, than they do in London at the moment.”
Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, warned that Britain had an “open door to potential enemies” with the current migration crisis.
“The horrible attack on volunteer ambulances is part of a rising tide of hate against Jewish communities in Britain,” he said.
“As I write, more undocumented young men are crossing the Channel. Many will be from Iran – we have an open door to potential enemies.”

items.summary: Murder investigation under way as police arrest four people over incident in Northampton

A man has died and a teenage boy is in a critical condition after a double stabbing at a skate park in Northampton.
Northamptonshire Police launched a murder investigation after the pair were stabbed during an altercation at the park in Ringway, in the Briar Hill area, at 3.45pm on Wednesday.
The man, in his 20s, was pronounced dead at the scene, while the teenage boy suffered life-threatening injuries. He has been taken to hospital, where he is in a critical condition.
Four people – two teenage boys, a man and a woman – were arrested over the incident and remain in police custody.
The public has been urged to avoid the area. A police cordon was in place at the park, and several roads were shut.

Burnham faces Labour conference civil war: Rayner stands by 'drive-by shooting' on immigration plans, Left accuses PM of 'ghosting' - and Chancellor admits he might need to find billions for fuel bailout
- See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Andy Burnham is facing a difficult Labour conference today with ministers clashing on migration and accusations that he has 'ghosted' the Left of the party.
The PM is in Liverpool for his first gathering since ousting Keir Starmer - but there is mounting evidence that the same bitter infighting will blight his leadership.
Tensions have flared after Angela Rayner doubled down on her criticism of Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's 'un-British' plans to make it harder for migrants to gain permanent residence in the UK.
Ms Rayner insisted this morning that there were 'no splits' and pointed out that Mr Burnham wanted ministers to 'do politics differently' by speaking out. 'We're not having an argument about immigration, we're having a conversation – a national conversation,' she told Sky News.
But the Housing Secretary's intervention has been described by MPs as a 'drive-by shooting'.
Meanwhile, Left-wingers have been openly sniping at Mr Burnham's approach. Clive Lewis - once such a fervent ally suggested he could stand down so the former Manchester mayor could re-enter the Commons - said the PM had 'left his allies behind' on entering No10 and behaved 'terribly'.
Veteran campaigner Neal Lawson, previously tipped to advise Mr Burnham in No10, accused him of 'jettisoning' plans for wealth taxes and rent controls, and downgrading a nationalisation push.
The internal warring comes against an increasingly bleak backdrop for the Government, with the Middle East crisis wreaking havoc on the public finances.
Chancellor John Healey admitted in an interview today that he might need to act on fuel duty, which is scheduled to rise at a time when drivers are facing rocketing prices at the pumps.
However, with markets alarmed at UK borrowing levels that would require him to find billions of pounds more from other tax rises or spending cuts - the latter of which would meet stern resistance from Labour MPs.
Ahead of his first Budget on October 28, Mr Healey also signalled he understands concerns about an exodus of rich individuals from the UK, saying he wanted people to stay to create jobs and wealth.
In other developments at Labour conference today:
- Mr Burnham insisted he 'won't leave office' without having 'grasped this nettle' of social care reform, after the death of his Alzheimer's-hit father Roy;
- The PM raised fresh doubts about Heathrow airport expansion, just weeks after his Chancellor backed it;
- A megapoll has renewed speculation about a snap election, showing Labour would be the biggest party and potentially able to form a coalition;
- Tories have warned that a new help to buy scheme offering state loans to first-time purchasers will heap more pressure on the country's finances and only push up house prices;
- Ms Rayner has announced local leaders will get stronger powers to seize empty and derelict homes so they can be brought back into use;
- Speculation continues to swirl about a snap election despite Mr Burnham declaring the idea 'dead';

Dramatic pictures have shown terror police arresting five men and a bomb disposal robot sweeping three vans after a suspected explosives plot at RAF Fairford.
Police were alerted to the plot early this morning after a heroic resident called 999 to report men 'acting suspiciously' around the white vans.
The group was arrested and filmed sitting on the road shirtless while handcuffed, indicating officers may also have suspected they were wearing suicide vests.
Viable incendiary devices and chemicals were found inside one of the vans, police said as they arrested the men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act.
A bomb disposal robot from the Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team was later seen moving between the three parked vans. Two vans' rear doors were open and what appeared to be large black barrels could be seen scattered outside.
RAF Fairford, in Gloucestershire, is the US Air Force's command outpost for operations from Europe and has been used for American strikes on Iranian missile sites that have been attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
The base was the subject of a warning from Iran's Revolutionary Guard in July, with the regime warning Britain not to allow US bombers to fly from the base.
Counter-terrorism police are understood to be leading the investigation into the incident amid suspicions a potential attack may have been foiled.

items.title: Garvaghy Road LIVE: PM calls for ‘calm on all sides’ as thousands block Orange Order march
items.summary: Protesters are now beginning to blockade Garvaghy Road following the late night court ruling that will allow an Orange Order parade to go ahead this morning in Belfast
items.body_text:
Garvaghy Road LIVE: PM calls for ‘calm on all sides’ as thousands block Orange Order march
Protesters are now beginning to blockade Garvaghy Road following the late night court ruling that will allow an Orange Order parade to go ahead this morning in Belfast
Thousands of protesters have blocked Garvaghy Road in Belfast in a bid to prevent a contentious Orange Order parade from passing through the predominantly nationalist area.
The protest has delayed the march, which had been due to begin at 8am after an overnight High Court ruling upheld permission for 35 Orangemen to take part.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appealed for “calm on all sides”, while police have repeatedly warned protesters they could face arrest for taking part in an unnotified parade.
The Orange Order members due to march remain at nearby Drumcree Church, with PSNI Chief Constable Jon Boutcher urging everyone to remain calm and peaceful as officers manage the situation.
The Drumcree parade has been banned since 1998 and was associated with violent clashes during the Troubles. The Orange Order has unsuccessfully sought permission for more than a quarter of a century to complete its traditional route along Garvaghy Road.
This is an ongoing news event. Keep up to date with our live blog below.
DUP MP Carla Lockhart calls Garvaghy Road protest 'unlawful'
Stood outside Drumcree parish church, Lockhart said: "The folks in the hall behind you have had a seismic win in the courts – for 28 years they have been denied their rights on this very hill.
“They have been here 52 weeks over the past 28 years in a dignified and peaceful manner.”
She added: “It’s time for Sinn Féin to take leadership and to ensure that the unlawful protest that is currently happening on the Garvaghy Road is dealt with, that they listen to the police and remove themselves from it, and allow the parade, which has obviously been determined in law and permitted to go down the road, down the road.”
PSNI negotiators on the scene
Orange Order member outside Drumcree Parochial Hall
Liam Kelly calls to 'dial down rhetoric' and for 'calm heads'
The Chair of the Police Federation for Northern Ireland has spoken out.
Liam Kelly said: “Our officers will police the out-workings of this Judgement without fear or favour. Their job will be to maintain the rule of law and see that there is full compliance with the Parades Commission determination. I remind those who disagree with or oppose the decision and procession that they, too, must comply with the law and, so, I would appeal to anyone who wishes to protest to do so in a lawful, measured and ultimately peaceful manner.
“Unfortunately, over the last 24 hours there has been a raft of unhelpful commentary in both mainstream media and social media platforms. I would particularly appeal to our politicians and community/civic representatives to dial down the rhetoric and work constructively to calm heads to help ensure that our officers can safely carry out their duties.
“Our officers want the policing deployment to be a safe environment for them and all who take opposing viewpoints. For that to happen we need to see calm heads and full compliance with the law.”
Carla Lockhart MP says 'the law is on our side'
In a post on Facebook, the MP has said: "Urgent message from Drumcree - Please Share.
"We have been made aware of false information that ‘bands’ and loyalists are converging in response to the illegal blockade set up by Republican activists on the Garvaghy Road.
"This is completely false.
"We believe this is deliberate misinformation being pushed by nefarious Republican sources in an attempt to goad young people into a confrontation.
"Do not fall for misinformation or react.
"The law is on our side and we are upholding it peacefully.
"We are still standing with the 35 brethren for a peaceful resolution and upholding of the determination for Portadown Orange District LOL 1 to complete their parade."
Protests - in pictures
Northern Ireland Secretary statemen

items.title: Labour conference: Watch live as Andy Burnham issues stark warning on future of NHS
items.summary: Attending his first conference as leader, the new Prime Minister will set out his stall just hours after saying he is more determined than ever to fix the broken social care system after the death of his beloved father
items.body_text:
Labour conference: Watch live as Andy Burnham issues stark warning on future of NHS
Attending his first conference as leader, the new Prime Minister will set out his stall just hours after saying he is more determined than ever to fix the broken social care system after the death of his beloved father
Andy Burnham is setting out his vision for Britain on Sunday as Labour party conference in Liverpool begins - but he began the day warning that the NHS needed saving.
Attending his first conference as leader, the new Prime Minister joined the party faithful just hours after saying he is more determined than ever to fix the broken social care system after the death of his beloved father.
The Prime Minister said it was painful to see the same failures that impacted his grandmother 25 years ago when his dad Roy needed care as he battled Alzheimer’s disease. Mr Burnham’s dad, who had been living in a care home, died earlier this month aged 86. And Mr Burnham warned adult social care "will in the end break the NHS" unless it is fixed, as he appeared on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg before conference resumed today in Liverpool.
It comes as Mr Burnham confirmed plans to help people to buy their first home with a deposit of just 2.5%, ahead of his big speech to Labour Party conference next week. The “Your First Home” scheme is designed to help young people who would struggle to afford a deposit to get on the housing ladder.
Meanwhile a fresh poll boosted party spirits. The MRP poll from More in Common shows Labour is now projected to be the largest party - albeit in a hung parliament - with 250 seats and 73 short of a majority, a major uptick from the last sounding carried out in July.
Follow along live below....
Key Events
When are next speakers due on Labour conference main stage?
The next speakers are due on the Labour conference main stage later this afternoon.
They include:
2pm - Louise Haigh
2:10pm - Douglas Alexander
2:20pm - Michael Marra
2:30pm - Stephen Kinnock
2:40pm - Ken Skates
3:15pm - Pat McFadden
Labour minister reveals anger from voters on small boats
A Labour minister has said she faces anger from voters all the time about small boats - despite a sharp fall in crossings.
Jo White told a fringe event in Liverpool that progress is being made and Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is pushing forward measures to remove incentives.
But the Home Office minister conceded that the message is not cutting through.

items.title: Benidorm Bianca Dyke star has famous actor dad in real life and fans will be floored
items.summary: Bianca Dyke appeared in series six of ITV's Benidorm - but who is the actress' real-life soap star father?
items.body_text:
Benidorm Bianca Dyke star has famous actor dad in real life and fans will be floored
Bianca Dyke appeared in series six of ITV's Benidorm - but who is the actress' real-life soap star father?
Benidorm fans will be stunned to find out that Bianca Dyke star Bel Powley is not the only famous member in her family.
Bel joined the cast of the ITV sitcom back in 2014, with the rest of the Dyke family: dad Clive (Perry Benson), mum Tonya (Hannah Waddingham) and brother Tiger (Danny Walters).
During their stint on the show, the family became firm favourites and famously had a rivalry with the Garveys who were also stopping at the Solana resort.
As for Bianca, she turned her attention to fellow holiday-goer Martin Weedon (Nicholas Burns), thinking he was a wealthy businessman, only to end things after realising he wasn’t.
Benidorm was not actress Bel’s first time on the screen. She shot to fame playing Daisy Millar in CBBC’s M.I. High from 2007 to 2008. Her other acting credits include the TV series Everything I Know about Love and the 2015 coming-of-age film The Diary of a Teenage Girl.
She also played Claire Conway in The Morning Show from 2019 to 2025 and is currently portraying Petunia Dursley in the upcoming new Harry Potter television series.
In real life though, Bel is the daughter of actor Mark Powley, who is best known for playing P.C Melvin in police drama The Bill from 1987 to 1990. He’s also appeared in several soaps including Coronation Street in 2001 as Rob Lucas and Emmerdale in 1999 playing Liam Hammond.
Talking about her childhood, Bel told Hollywood Authentic: “I never even really wanted to be an actor. I was really academic. But my dad’s an actor [Mark Powley], and my mum’s a casting director [Janis Jaffa]. So it was always kind of in the family.
“I went to a Saturday drama group called Youngblood Theatre Company, which was all improvisation-based, where I met a lot of my mates. A casting director came in once to cast a CBBC show called M.I. High about child spies, and I got the job.”
She added: “So I basically ended up being a child actor, to my parents’ dismay, because they thought I was going to be the first academic of the family. I ended up following in my dad’s footsteps.”
Bel is also married to fellow actor Douglas Booth. Douglas has starred in the likes of Great Expectations, Romeo and Juliet and ITV’s recent cop drama The Blame, alongside Michelle Keegan.
Douglas and Bel first met at a chemistry read audition over 10 years ago. Three years later in 2016, they worked together on the film Mary Shelley and a romance quickly blossomed.
Going from strength to strength Douglas proposed to Bel in July 2021 on Primrose Hill in London. Then in October 2023, Douglas and Bel made things official by getting married at Petersham Nurseries in Richmond.
“I woke up in the morning, and I was like, ‘I just want to do it all over again, right now’,” Bel told Hollywood Authentic before sharing: “I think in 10 years’ time, we’ll get married again.”
Benidorm is available to watch on ITVX.

At least 17 dead in mass shooting at bar in South Africa, police say
Police said eight men armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols entered the bar and began shooting at the patrons

At least 17 people have been killed in a mass shooting at a bar in South Africa's Gauteng, police said.
The South African Police Service said authorities have launched a manhunt to find eight armed men following the deadly shooting late on Saturday at a tavern in Wedela township southwest of Johannesburg.
The suspects, armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols, entered the bar and began shooting at customers around 9.30pm local time, police said.
All 17 people, including four women, were shot and killed at the bar and declared dead at the scene by the ambulance service, police said.
The suspects allegedly targeted the tavern, opening fire on customers drinking outside and then moving inside to continue shooting, the police said.
Police said the suspects searched some victims and stole their mobile phones before fleeing the scene in two vehicles. Two other vehicles were also set ablaze during the shooting, police added.
Police said the motive behind the shooting was unknown. Fifteen others suffered gunshot wounds and were rushed to hospital for treatment.
No arrests have been made, the police said in a statement.
Soldiers from the national army and police pathologists arrived in the township, where two burnt vehicles could be seen. The tavern where the shooting happened had a sign that read "No weapons allowed" below its trading hours.
In a separate incident overnight, South African police said gunmen killed 10 people and wounded 11 more at an entertainment venue in Lwandle in Cape Town at 1.46am local time.
Five people died at the scene, while five others succumbed to their injuries at the hospital, police said. At least 11 others were undergoing medical treatment on Sunday afternoon.
“Detectives are hard at work in search of a perpetrators of the shooting incident, with no arrests yet,” the police said.
South Africa has a long history of mass shootings at bars and unlicensed taverns known as shebeens, which are linked to gang rivalries, extortion, or disputes tied to illegal liquor sales.
"South Africa has a serious illegal firearms problem, and firearms are frequently used by organised criminal groups as well as in gang-related and other violent crimes," said crime expert Yusuf Abramjee.
"Every mass shooting should therefore trigger more than an investigation into the immediate perpetrators," he told Reuters. "Authorities need to look at the wider networks behind the violence."
Last week, at least 12 people were killed, and two others suffered injuries in a shooting at a house in KwaMakhutha in southeastern KwaZulu-Natal Province.
Three armed men opened fire on 13 men and a woman believed to be pregnant when they were reportedly having a party inside the house.
The woman and 10 other men died at the scene, while one person succumbed to their injuries later at the hospital. Police have not ruled out gang rivalry as a possible motive.
These are the latest in a series of mass shootings in South Africa recently, including one in June when multiple shooters killed 12 people in a poor neighbourhood in Johannesburg that police linked to criminal gangs.
Two mass shootings two weeks apart in December last year killed 21 people. They were also carried out by multiple gunmen.
South Africa has extremely high rates of violent crime, with official police statistics recording 5,427 homicides in the latest three-month period between April and June at an average of nearly 60 homicides a day.

China and US announce AI safety channel even as Trump claims ‘super intelligence’ needs no guardrails
Xi Jinping reportedly told his US counterpart that AI must be harnessed ‘for good’, despite Trump calling safety fears a hoax
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Join today
Already a member? Log in
The US and China agreed to set up a channel for handling artificial intelligence (AI)-related incidents, according to an announcement at the end of their three-day summit, even though president Donald Trump has claimed the technology doesn’t need any new guardrails.
Xi Jinping's first visit to the White House produced no major breakthroughs, but experts say it provided them an opportunity to nurture cooperation and set up working groups that could prevent problems from escalating.
The White House on Saturday said both sides would set up a communication mechanism for AI-related incidents, to discuss related risks and benefits, with further AI-specific talks scheduled for November.
During their summit, Mr Xi reportedly told Mr Trump that both nations can and must develop and manage AI “for good”, in contrast to the American president’s stance that safety fears over the technology are “a hoax”.
Mr Xi told Mr Trump: “Both China and the United States are leading nations in artificial intelligence. [We must] ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the wellbeing of the people.”
AI bosses in recent weeks have sounded alarm over the potential of the technology to threaten the future of the human race. Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI maker ChatGPT, said the world was right to be afraid of AI, and the warnings have led to new calls for regulation of the technology.
Two researchers from Anthropic, the company behind the advanced AI assistant Claude, also warned this month that the rapidly progressing technology could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future.
It prompted the UN human rights chief to ask AI companies to rein in development of the technology, cautioning that the world was “on the cusp of irreversible change" that could affect generations of humanity.
But at the UN General Assembly last Tuesday, Mr Trump dismissed calls for stricter controls, branding the warnings “a hoax”.
“During this visit, we will also discuss pressing issues concerning security, technology, and 'super-intelligence’,” Mr Trump said ahead of Mr Xi's arrival in Washington.
Analysts have cautioned that the two countries’ intense competition in the AI field is likely to reduce either side’s willingness to limit the technology beyond symbolic agreements.
Mr Trump claims Mr Xi had agreed with his push to rebrand AI as “super intelligence". He has instructed government departments to use the term in posts and documents.
The US president has also rebuffed calls for Congress to place new regulations on AI, saying: “The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades.”
Several executives from AI and technology companies attended the Trump-Xi state dinner on Thursday evening, including Mr Altman, Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman, Tesla boss Elon Musk and Amazon chief Jeff Bezos.

items.body_text:
Two giant pandas head to Atlanta zoo from China after Trump-Xi agreement
The pandas set off for Atlanta on Sunday morning
- Bookmark
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Join today
Already a member? Log in
A pair of giant pandas departed from Chengdu in south-west China early on Sunday morning, travelling to their new home in Atlanta under a joint agreement between the Chinese and American governments.
While attending a three-day summit in Washington with US president Donald Trump, Chinese president Xi Jinping stated that the bears would arrive in Atlanta over the coming days.
The temporary transfer of the pandas to the zoo was among the few concrete outcomes to emerge from the state visit, which produced public displays of goodwill between the leaders but failed to settle long-standing diplomatic differences between the two nations.
Atlanta said goodbye to its final pandas in 2024, leaving its zoo without any of the animals. A fresh arrangement was initially announced back in April, though specific dates were not released.
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are the adult pandas assigned to Zoo Atlanta for a period of 10 years as part of the deal. Both animals were born in 2020 and cared for at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding. Ping Ping, a male, possesses distinct dark black circles around his eyes, while Fu Shuang, a female, features a slightly protruding forehead, according to the Xinhua News Agency.
Beijing has long employed pandas as instruments of global diplomacy, loaning the bears as a sign of goodwill while allowing contracts to lapse when international relations become strained.
Xi described the loan programme as a demonstration of "friendship between the Chinese and Americans."
Earlier this week, Trump met UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham for the first time, with talks taking place on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
In a largely warm shared press conference, the president praised Burnham as a “natural business person” and the former mayor of Greater Manchester said he had “established a good connection” with Trump.
The prime minister said that the pair had “taken that further today” as they discussed trade, energy and immigration among other topics during their 40-minute meeting.
Trump told reporters: “I think right now, based on my relationship with your prime minister, Andy, I think we’re doing very well.”

items.title: England have two glaring weaknesses Thomas Tuchel desperately needs to fix
items.summary: The question is, can he do it?
items.body_text:
Thomas Tuchel was burning again, eyes full of aggression and fire, knowing that any claims he might have for English supremacy at Wembley would meet with raised eyebrows and a roll of the eyes.
Thus did a 3-2 defeat to Spain reframe impressions. What might have been cause for trumpets and drums became a night of fawning over the world champions.
We learned nothing new about Spain, a fully developed unit, replete with next level talent, supported by a bench just as good, and a mentality made of iron. We did, however, learn much about England, an evolving team that drew from Tuchel the view that he had seen in moments the best football of his reign.
This was far removed from the overwhelmed, low esteem England of two years ago when Spain rattled through Gareth Southgate’s lame apologists in the European Championships final.
Tuchel identified two critical differences between these teams at Wembley, England’s susceptibility to unforced errors that gifted Spain two goals and a want of the kind of composure and ruthlessness Spain showed within sight of goal.
This meant Tuchel was explaining away a narrow loss when he felt he could have been celebrating victory.
“The top transition goal we scored [Anthony Gordon] was an amazing goal, and we could have created more,” Tuchel said.
“The effort against the ball is also identity. The effort against the ball and the bravery and courage to have the high ball wins was outstanding.
“I think we had 12 or 15 more ball wins in the opponent’s half than Spain today. But we couldn’t convert enough into chances and goals, because otherwise we would have won the match.”
Apart from a 15-minute spell after the equaliser, when Spain hit that familiar, poetic meter, England were, in the argot of the football pundit, “at it”.
There was a welcome absence of doubt, of deference. They cancelled Spain’s eminence by refusing to acknowledge it.
The result was a rousing, joined-up demonstration of super expressive Englishness, powered by England’s own Hispanophiles Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon. Spain were never far away, but they were properly discomfited and suffered a little of the anxiety they routinely evince in others.
What stood out was the confidence of England, recovering from an awful Mark Guehi error in the second minute to establish a degree of command. Nico O’Reilly, who would offer gift No 2 on the hour to complete the momentum shift after Harry Kane’s missed penalty, raced forward with real spite. His counterpart on the right, Jarell Quansah, made light of Nico Williams with his rendition of a Venus fly trap.
Elliot Anderson enjoyed sole occupancy at the base of midfield to deny Dani Olmo room to operate and Myles Lewis-Skelly proved a nimble contrast to the more one-dimensional, hard running of Declan Rice. This gave England real presence in the middle of the park, forming a fluid connection with Bellingham.
Had Kane been at his best to put England 3-1 up from the spot, it might have put a welcome sock in all those crowing inevitably, “yeah, but you knew how it would end. Same old England.”
	
Read more
Tuchel knew it was coming, reacting tetchily to reporters framing the outcome in that way.
“The start was terrible,” he admitted. “It makes it so, so difficult to be behind against this kind of team. The reaction was very, very good.
“After 10 or 12 minutes, I think we were the better team. We still made two or three big mistakes and conceded big chances, but overall we were better.
“We dominated at home in the first half. We created, scored two goals and I think it was our best 15 minutes after the whistle. Unfortunately, we couldn’t convert the penalty, which maybe would have been the decisive moment, because I think then Spain would have maybe, for the first time, believed that their long run of unbeaten games ends here.”
Tuchel gets another chance to make his point in Prague, where England must demonstrate the same appetite against lesser opposition. November’s return with Spain will tell

items.title: Even in Trump’s home state, Maga is turning on him
items.summary: The loss of Florida - seat of his unofficial court at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach - would be an extraordinary and humiliating loss for the US President
items.body_text:
If there is one state in the US that Republicans had thought was entirely safe terrain for them in November’s midterm elections, it was the Sunshine State of Florida.
At the start of this year, Democrats gave no thought to the possibility of flipping the state and turning it blue. After all, their Republican opponents currently control 20 of Florida’s 28 seats in the House of Representatives, both seats in the US Senate, and the Governor’s Mansion. Democratic Party grandees had sensibly written it off.
But suddenly, such is the American public’s disquiet over Donald Trump’s stewardship of the nation and the economic crisis that his war on Iran has ignited that even Florida is in play.
Shorts
With fewer than 40 days left in the midterm campaign, last week Byron Donalds, the Republican Party’s candidate to succeed Ron DeSantis as Florida’s governor, suddenly removed virtually every reference to Trump from his campaign website. Donalds, a former congressman who is so close to Trump that in November 2023 he was considered one of the top candidates to serve as vice president in a second administration, is now running from his political mentor as fast as his legs can carry him.
Endorsed by Trump, Donalds had proudly emblazoned the President’s backing of him on all his campaign communications for months. Now, voters visiting Donalds’ website are hard-pressed to find the candidate making any mention of the President at all.
The Miami Herald found that at least eight references to the President were removed from the site, including one that said Donald’s first priority as governor would be to “Enact the Trump Agenda”. Instead, he is now vowing to take on the issue of “affordability”, a word that Trump claims that Democrats have concocted to describe economic travails that he insists do not exist.
Congresswoman María Elvira Salazar is another Florida Republican who suddenly realises her desire to return to Washington may hinge on a rejection of Trump. “Mr President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far”, she thundered in a campaign advertisement released this month.
The ad eviscerates Trump’s policy of mass deportations, observing that in July 50 per cent of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainees had no criminal convictions or pending charges, despite the President’s insistence that he is removing “the worst of the worst” from US soil. “Be careful what your advisers are telling you about immigration policy,” warns Salazar. “The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today,” she says, reflecting the growing hostility to Trump among Latino voters that she is encountering on Miami doorsteps.
Under normal circumstances, Salazar would be a shoo-in to return to office. She won her district by 20 points two years ago, has risen to the position of assistant Republican whip in the House, and earned Trump’s endorsement for re-election as early as February.
“SHE WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN”, he gushed on Truth Social.
Now, she may feel doubly let down by him. In addition to the drag his policies are placing on her re-election efforts, over the weekend Trump amplified far-too-late efforts to ditch “backstabber” Salazar as the Republican Party’s candidate in her district, signifying his displeasure with her disloyalty.
In battleground states across the country, Republican candidates now find themselves with a choice: stand by Trump and lose or make an 11th-hour effort to salvage their campaigns by breaking with him.
In Michigan, the Republicans’ Senate candidate Mike Rogers has dropped his long-standing support for the Iran war, urging Trump to end it as soon as possible. Other candidates making similar demands include Tom Tiffany, the Republican nominee for governor of Wisconsin (“we should be exiting Iran… it’s time to move on”), Senator Jon Husted seeking re-election in Ohio (“the war needs to come to an end as soon as possible”), and Iowa Republican Ashley Hinson seeking a re

items.title: ‘Stuff of nightmares’: UK cuts aid to UN’s Gaza food operations by 78%
items.summary: The revelation risks reigniting left-wing anger at Labour’s approach to Gaza
items.body_text:
Britain has cut funding for the UN’s food operations in Gaza by 78 per cent, undermining a promise by ministers to protect aid to the Palestinian territory.
The UK’s annual contribution to the World Food Programme (WFP) Palestine fell from $18m (£13.6m) in 2024 to $9.3m (£7m) last year and just $4m (£3m) this year, The i Paper has learned.
The organisation has said the funding shortfall will mean it has to cut the number of people it can feed in Gaza from 1.1 million to 600,000.
Shorts
In March, the then foreign secretary Yvette Cooper told the Commons: “We are fully protecting our allocation to Palestine.”
The Foreign Office insisted that this was still the case, and that its overall aid budget for Palestine remained at £127m. An £88m package of support for healthcare, clean water, sanitation and other essential services for people in Gaza and the West Bank was announced last Thursday.
But MPs on the international development committee have called the cuts to the UN agency “appalling” and said they were the “stuff of nightmares”.
The revelation risks reigniting left-wing anger at Labour’s approach to Gaza as it attempts to hold off the challenge of Green leader Zack Polanski in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election.
Britain’s overall aid budget has been squeezed in recent years. The previous Tory government cut spending on development from 0.7 per cent of GDP to 0.5 per cent in 2021, before Sir Keir Starmer reduced it further to 0.3 per cent, which takes effect next year. Programmes are already being scaled back.
The Foreign Office will continue to support the WFP and funding allocations are kept under review, The i Paper understands.
Gaza situation is ‘extremely fragile’
A World Food Programme spokesperson said: “The situation is Gaza remains critical and extremely fragile. At a time when WFP should be scaling up assistance to reach more people, we are being forced to make difficult decisions, prioritising the most vulnerable while cutting assistance to others despite widespread needs.
“Humanitarian assistance is still a lifeline and without it, people could slip back into catastrophic levels of hunger faced last year.”
The UN agency said that by October the WFP would be reaching around 45 per cent fewer people overall, while also reducing both cash and food volumes.
If current levels of humanitarian assistance in Gaza are not sustained, up to 90 per cent of the population will face high levels of acute food insecurity by the end of the year, the WFP said.
The Foreign Office has insisted the aid package announced last week will support hundreds of thousands of Palestinians.
The money, announced by Miliband at the UN in New York, includes support for medical consultations, rehabilitation for children with blast injuries, safe water provision and mental health services. But it is not new funding and is part of the overall aid budget to Palestine of £127m, which it said was protected this year.
In a written statement to the Commons in March, Cooper said the Government remained “committed to providing lifesaving assistance to Palestinians in Gaza” and was seeking to limit the impact of aid cuts on humanitarian crises across the Middle East.
Monica Harding, a Liberal Democrat MP on the international development committee, said it was “appalling” that the World Food Programme expects to cut the number of people it can feed in Gaza.
“The Government cannot truly speak of their commitment to the Palestinian people while these cuts remain in place,” she said.
‘The numbers are stark’
Concerns over the cuts to WFP Palestine were raised by Harding and her fellow committee member James Naish, a Labour MP, at a hearing with aid minister Kirsty McNeill earlier this month.
Naish told The i Paper: “The numbers are stark – 1.4 million people in Gaza facing acute food insecurity by December, at a time when UK funding to the World Food Programme has fallen sharply since 2024.”

items.title: Where the road became a destination: Iran’s historical caravanserais
items.summary: TEHRAN - For centuries, crossing Iran was as much a test of endurance as it was a journey of discovery. Merchants moved goods between distant markets, pilgrims traveled toward sacred places, and ordinary travelers followed routes across deserts, mountains and plains. Between these long stretches of road stood caravanserais, places where a journey could pause, animals could be rested, goods could be protected and strangers could share food, stories and news.
items.body_text:
Where the road became a destination: Iran’s historical caravanserais
TEHRAN - For centuries, crossing Iran was as much a test of endurance as it was a journey of discovery. Merchants moved goods between distant markets, pilgrims traveled toward sacred places, and ordinary travelers followed routes across deserts, mountains and plains. Between these long stretches of road stood caravanserais, places where a journey could pause, animals could be rested, goods could be protected and strangers could share food, stories and news.
Today, many of these historical roadside inns offer a different kind of journey. They are destinations in their own right, allowing visitors to step into the infrastructure of travel that shaped Iran long before motorways, railways and airports.
The importance of these buildings was formally recognized in 2023, when UNESCO inscribed The Persian Caravanserai on the World Heritage List. The serial property comprises 54 caravanserais selected from the country’s much larger network of centuries-old examples.
Together, they represent far more than individual buildings: they form a testimony of the roads, trade, pilgrimage, architecture and human encounters that connected different parts of the Iranian soil and the wider region.
For travelers today, this network offers an unusual way of experiencing the ancient country. Rather than visiting heritage only in the form of palaces, mosques or ancient cities, visitors can follow the roads between them and discover the places where earlier generations stopped along the way.
Glimpses of an architecture that was shaped by the road
Though, there are many differences and similarities between those caravanserais countrywide, there is no single architectural formula for an Iranian caravanserai.
Their designs evolved according to geography, climate, available building materials, security requirements and the character of the routes on which they stood. The UN cultural body describes the 54 selected caravanserais as demonstrating a wide range of architectural styles and adaptations to different climatic conditions across thousands of kilometers.
Yet many share a recognizable shape and design. A traveler approaching a caravanserai would often first encounter a substantial entrance, sometimes marked by a monumental portal. Beyond it was a central courtyard around which rooms and service spaces were arranged. The courtyard provided an organized space for people, animals and goods, while the surrounding rooms offered shelter.
The design was practical but rarely devoid of architectural ambition. Brickwork, vaults, domes, arches, geometric patterns and carefully proportioned courtyards could transform what was essentially roadside infrastructure into an impressive architectural ensemble.
In desert areas, thick walls and enclosed courtyards helped moderate the harsh climate. Elsewhere, local materials and construction traditions produced different forms. The result is a remarkable architectural map of Iran: buildings responding to the same basic human need while reflecting very different landscapes.
UNESCO’s documentation notes that the location and setting of each caravanserai were decisive in shaping its design, particularly in relation to climate, water availability and defensive requirements.
This is one reason that visiting a caravanserai can be more revealing than looking at photographs of one. Sometimes, the relationship between building and landscape becomes part of the experience.
A caravanserai in a desert does not tell the same story as one near a mountain pass or a historic urban center. The surrounding terrain, the distance from other settlements and the availability of water help explain why the building was constructed where it stands.
More than roadside inns
The word “caravanserai” can easily create an image of merchants stopping overnight with their camels. That picture is not wrong, but it is incomplete.

items.title: DOE steps up efforts to restore Persian yellow deer population
items.summary: TEHRAN – The Department of Environment (DOE) is carrying out research, conservation, and breeding programs aimed at restoring the population of Persian yellow deer in designated natural habitats and wildlife breeding centers across the country.
items.body_text:
DOE steps up efforts to restore Persian yellow deer population
TEHRAN – The Department of Environment (DOE) is carrying out research, conservation, and breeding programs aimed at restoring the population of Persian yellow deer in designated natural habitats and wildlife breeding centers across the country.
Conservation efforts to recover the threatened species are being pursued through two complementary approaches: in-situ conservation in its natural habitats and ex-situ conservation in managed settings, IRNA quoted Mohammad Nosrati, an official with the DOE, as saying.
To conserve the animal in its natural habitat, the feasibility study for the reintroduction of Persian fallow deer in chosen habitats in Fars and Yazd provinces is placed on the agenda to be conducted.
As part of the plan to reinforce the number of Persian yellow deer and enhance its restoration, DOE has allocated funding for monitoring and assessing the population of the species introduced into Ilam, Khuzestan, Fars and Yazd provinces. The effort aims to study the population dynamics, identify threats, evaluate habitat desirability, and assess the conservation status of the species, he added.
Referring to the conservation measures being conducted outside the natural habitat, Nosrati said the DOE is organizing fallow deer breeding centers at different sites such as Azadi, Arsanjan, Miankotal, Dasht-e Naz, Rashkan, Bagh-e Shadi, Mahour Dasht-Yafteh, Karun Agro-Industry, and Fandoqlu, where population management, the translocation of Persian deer to natural habitats, and the assessment of the species’ genetic purity are put on the agenda.
According to the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List, the Iranian yellow deer is categorized as an endangered species.
Almost half a century ago, it was thought that the yellow deer species was extinct in the world. However, about 50 years ago, four yellow deer were observed in Dez and Karkheh forests, the primary habitats of the Persian yellow deer. They were released in different regions of Iran for better reproduction.
Thanks to the effective implementation of the conservation program, the number of Persian yellow deer has risen from 5 in the Iranian year 1398 (2019 – 2020), to 19 this year.
Genetic map for endangered species being developed
The DOE is developing a genetic map of endangered wildlife species to increase their chance of survival, create a breeding plan, manage their population, and address the risks facing them in their natural habitats.
Effective conservation of endangered species is almost unattainable without a precise understanding of population genetics. To this end, genetic and molecular studies of key wildlife species in the country have been put on the agenda, ensuring that management decisions are based on accurate scientific data, IRNA quoted the head of the National Museum of Natural History and Genetic Resources, Leila Ezzeddinlou, as saying.
Preserving genetic diversity within and between populations, preventing declines in effective population size, avoiding inbreeding and genetic erosion, conserving genes adapted to diverse environmental conditions, and providing genetic resources for species restoration, propagation, and introduction or reintroduction programs are among primary objectives of these studies, she added.
Referring to three research agreements signed between the DOE, the College of Agricultural and Natural Resources of the University of Tehran, and Gorgan University, the official said that as part of the cooperation, a project is underway to investigate the genomic diversity and phylogeny of Levant viper and Latifi’s viper populations, employing conservation and therapeutic approaches based on genomic markers.
Moreover, the development of genetic profiles and maps for the Asiatic cheetahs, black bear, and Persian yellow deer, as keystone and threatened species, has kicked off.

items.title: Board of directors of Iranian committee of ICC elected
items.summary: TEHRAN- The election of the Board of Directors of the Iranian Committee of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) was held concurrently with the meeting of the Council of this committee at the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture (ICCIMA).
items.body_text:
Board of directors of Iranian committee of ICC elected
TEHRAN- The election of the Board of Directors of the Iranian Committee of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) was held concurrently with the meeting of the Council of this committee at the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture (ICCIMA).
The Council meeting of the Iranian Committee of ICC was chaired by Samad Hassanzadeh, President of the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture, and with the attendance of Abolfazl Roghani Golpayegani, Secretary General of the Iran Chamber, Ahmad Pour-Fallah, the Chairman of Iran-Italy Joint Chamber of Commerce, and 23 of the 24 members of this Council.
At the beginning of the meeting, Samad Hassanzadeh, President of the Iran Chamber, while appreciating the efforts and successes of the Iranian Committee of ICC and its Secretary General, referred to the economic conditions prevailing in the country and the role of private-sector economic actors in ensuring market security.
Hassanzadeh emphasized the effective role of this committee in developing the international relations of economic actors and chambers of commerce and in enhancing these interactions, and referred to the planning ahead for the Iranian Committee of ICC.
Then, Mohammad Khazaei, while appreciating the effective and comprehensive support of the President and Board of Directors of the Iranian Committee during the past three-year term, considered these supports among the important factors in achieving the recent accomplishments of the Iranian Committee of ICC.
Khazaei also presented a report on the most important measures and activities of the first six months of the current Iranian calendar year, the negotiations and interactions conducted with ICC presidents and affiliated bodies, and the agreements reached.
Later in the meeting, given the completion of the three-year term of the Board of Directors of the Iranian Committee of ICC, the Council meeting entered the process of electing the new Board of Directors.
EF/MA

items.title: Iran International establishes scholarship in memory of presenter Farahnaz Espad
items.summary: Iran International has established an annual postgraduate scholarship in memory of Farahnaz Espad, one of the channel’s first presenters, who died in August after eight years with the channel.
items.body_text:
The one voice that could settle what Tehran wants from the diplomacy under way in New York has not been heard at all. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has said nothing publicly about the contacts with Washington, the attacks on his foreign minister, or the speech itself.
He did not receive the president before the trip. And this is the first UN General Assembly in 37 years at which his father was not Iran's supreme leader.
What changed, and what did not
Before the speech, the hardline press was hostile to the trip itself. Kayhan warned that "New York is not a place for smiles and negotiations" and that the General Assembly should be turned into "a court for US crimes." Fars, affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards, wrote that Pezeshkian should not have gone at all.
Moderates pushed the other way: the daily Etemad recalled the meetings Iranian presidents failed to hold with Bill Clinton in 2000 and Barack Obama in 2013, and the reformist Mehdi Karroubi urged Pezeshkian to meet Donald Trump.
Pezeshkian did neither. After Trump used the UN podium to threaten to "annihilate" Iran, the president said he had rewritten his speech. He held up photographs of children killed in the strike on a school in Minab in the war's first hours alongside a portrait of the late Ali Khamenei, said Iran had defended itself "powerfully," said it remained open to negotiation, and said it would not accept "the language of coercion."
There was no offer in it, no gesture toward a meeting, nothing a hardliner could call weakness.
The praise followed within hours, and it praised the defiance.
Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said the president had "at the heart of the system of arrogance, reproduced the message of power, pride, dignity and hope of a nation," in a statement carried by IRNA.
Iran would rely on unity "from the country's highest executive official to the brave fighters in the field and the people in the streets," he said.
Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to the supreme leader, called Pezeshkian "a worthy representative and the voice of all Iranians" who had been "decisive, reasoned and logical."
The message, he wrote on X, was clear: "we will not bow our heads before a bully, we will not forget our martyrs and we will make the aggressors regret their actions."
Ali Abdollahi, chief of staff of the armed forces and commander of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, Iran's wartime command, said the people "through Dr. Pezeshkian, slapped the criminal president of the United States before the eyes of the world," and that the armed forces stood "in harmony and in one voice with the people and the respected president."
Army commander Amir Hatami followed on Thursday. "Mr. President, well done. We sincerely thank you," he said, calling the address "a manifestation of the unity and coordination of all Iran against the bullying enemy."
Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf wrote that Pezeshkian "spoke not just for a government, but for a 3,000-year-old civilization."
Every one of those statements praised the speech for what it refused. None mentioned the talks.
The missing voice
In previous years, state media made a point of showing the president meeting the supreme leader before a major trip, including before the General Assembly. The meeting was the signal: the president traveled with the leader's mandate, and everyone in Tehran knew it. No such meeting was announced this year. Mojtaba Khamenei has not been seen or heard in public since he was named to succeed his father in March, and he has issued nothing on New York.
The closest anyone has come to speaking for him was Major General Yahya Rahim Safavi, one of his military advisers, on Wednesday. "If the Supreme Leader has deemed it expedient and left the government's hands open in the negotiations, that is an important act of prudence," Safavi said on state television. Even the adviser spoke in the conditional.

items.title: Why Trump said no to Iran’s Hormuz proposal
items.summary: US President Donald Trump’s rejection of Iran’s proposal for a swift reopening of the Strait of Hormuz may say less about Washington’s opposition to a deal than about its changing assessment of Tehran’s most important bargaining chip.
items.body_text:
US President Donald Trump’s rejection of Iran’s proposal for a swift reopening of the Strait of Hormuz may say less about Washington’s opposition to a deal than about its changing assessment of Tehran’s most important bargaining chip.
Trump publicly rejected the proposal on Saturday. The plan would have reopened the strait within seven days and resumed nuclear negotiations in return for measures including lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.
The president plainly wants normal shipping restored, but he appears unwilling to pay the price Tehran is asking for it.
Iranian officials have repeatedly described Hormuz as a strategic asset and a source of leverage. Disruption of the narrow waterway affects energy markets, shipping costs and inflation far beyond the region.
That importance has not disappeared. What may be changing is Iran’s ability to convert that disruption into immediate political concessions from Washington.
The US military has spent months trying to reduce Iran’s ability to attack shipping while expanding escorts for commercial vessels. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said last week that US forces had facilitated the transit of more than 2,000 commercial vessels and more than one billion barrels of crude oil through the strait.
The operation has not restored normal shipping, but it has allowed substantial volumes of oil to move without an agreement with Tehran, helping Washington turn Hormuz from an Iranian energy veto into what it increasingly appears to regard as a manageable risk.
Why Trump can wait
If Washington believes it can keep significant quantities of oil moving without Tehran’s cooperation, there is less incentive to lift the naval blockade and ease economic pressure simply to secure the full reopening of the strait.
Trump’s rejection also comes as his administration is increasing rather than reducing that pressure. At the UN General Assembly this week, he called for Iran’s “complete economic isolation” and said he expected an agreement after the November midterm elections
The administration has expanded restrictions on Iranian banking and aviation. Iranian airlines have lost access to several international destinations, while companies servicing sanctioned Iranian carriers face the threat of secondary US sanctions.
Trump’s rejection therefore suggests Washington believes time is, for now, working more in its favor than Tehran’s.
Hormuz still matters
None of this means Iran’s Hormuz strategy has failed.
Keeping commercial traffic moving requires a major US military operation, while shipping and insurance costs remain elevated and the threat of attacks has not disappeared. Washington is paying a price for managing the disruption.
But the balance may have shifted. Tehran still views reopening Hormuz as something it can exchange for relief from economic and military pressure. Washington appears to believe it has reduced the costs of disruption enough that it does not yet need to meet Iran’s asking price.
Seen that way, Trump’s “no” becomes more significant. He has not necessarily rejected diplomacy: contacts through mediators continue, and Iran says it is still awaiting Washington’s formal response to its proposal. US officials have also described indirect discussions as continuing.
What Trump has rejected, for now, is Tehran’s price for ending the Hormuz crisis.
Iran still holds the Hormuz card. Washington’s calculation appears to be that it no longer has to pay as much to take it off the table.
Iran says a negotiated settlement remains the only way out of the war and is awaiting a formal US response to its latest proposal, despite President Donald Trump saying he has rejected Tehran’s offer.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that Tehran had seen an initial reaction from Trump but was still waiting for Washington’s formal response through mediators before deciding its next step.

items.title: Families of slain protesters challenge Pezeshkian over UN remarks
items.summary: Relatives of protesters killed during Iran’s January crackdown challenged President Masoud Pezeshkian’s portrayal of the unrest as foreign-driven, saying their family members were unarmed and had no links to foreign governments, after his UN General Assembly address on Wednesday.
items.body_text:
Families of slain protesters challenge Pezeshkian over UN remarks
Relatives of protesters killed during Iran’s January crackdown challenged President Masoud Pezeshkian’s portrayal of the unrest as foreign-driven, saying their family members were unarmed and had no links to foreign governments, after his UN General Assembly address on Wednesday.
Pezeshkian accused protesters of being incited by the United States and Israel and receiving weapons to disrupt Iran’s security. He also defended system supporters who took to the streets during the unrest.
The sisters of Sina Kazemi, Emad Mavedatipour and Babak Sadeghi Mohseni responded on X, saying their brothers were unarmed when they were killed on January 8 or 9 and were not acting on behalf of any foreign government.
“I testify that my brother was unarmed when he was killed by the Islamic Republic of Iran’s forces on January 8, 2026,” Kazemi’s sister wrote. “He was not acting on behalf of any foreign government. I seek truth, justice, and accountability.”
Mavedatipour’s sister posted the same account of her brother, saying he was unarmed when he was killed on January 9 and denying that he acted for a foreign government.
Sadeghi Mohseni’s sister said her brother was unarmed when he was killed on January 8 and also called for “truth, justice, and accountability.”
The sister of Ahmad Khosravani, a 21-year-old professional basketball player, said her brother was completely unarmed when Iranian forces killed him on January 9.
“He was not acting on behalf of any foreign government,” she wrote. “They shot him directly in the heart.”
Fathers challenge Pezeshkian
Two other bereaved fathers challenged the government's account in separate video messages sent to Iran International.
The father of Erfan Abdipour, an architecture student who also worked at his brother’s restaurant, called on Pezeshkian to publish evidence if authorities had any showing that his son had received military training or carried a weapon.
“My request is that if you have evidence showing that he received military training, was instructed or had a weapon, or anything else that night, publish it,” Abdipour’s father said.
Abdipour had gone to protest on the night he was killed, his father said, questioning what his son could have been trying to seize in an area he described as having no military barracks or security facility.
The father of Pouria Bagheri separately rejected the government's explanation for the scale of the killings.
“I categorically reject the overall argument that such widespread killing was foreign actors work.”
Bagheri’s father questioned why authorities shut down the internet and electricity and said that security agents removed surveillance cameras from shops. He also asked why officials brought government supporters onto the streets two days later if foreign-backed armed groups posed the extensive threat described by authorities.
“Why did you bring your own supporters into the streets two days later? With what guarantee?” he said. “Was it not because you were in control?”
January crackdown
The protests began on December 28, 2025, following a sharp fall in the rial and rising prices before spreading across all 31 provinces and developing into a broader challenge to the Islamic Republic.
The deadliest violence came on January 8 and 9. Amnesty International said verified videos and eyewitness testimony showed security forces using rifles and shotguns against protesters, frequently firing at heads and torsos.
Iran International’s Editorial Board concluded in January that more than 36,500 people were killed by security forces on January 8 and 9 after reviewing classified government documents, field reports and accounts from medical workers, witnesses and victims’ families.
The UN Fact-Finding Mission on Iran later said security forces used lethal force against protesters and bystanders, including children, who posed no imminent threat of death or serious injury.

items.title: مشکات‌الزهرا صفی و ماندگار فرزامی؛ نخستین زنان تنیسور ایرانی پیروز در بازی‌های آسیایی
items.summary: مشکات‌الزهرا صفی و ماندگار فرزامی با پیروزی در دور نخست انفرادی زنان در بازی‌های آسیایی ناگویا ۲۰۲۶، نخستین بردهای تاریخ تنیس زنان ایران در بخش انفرادی این رقابت‌ها را رقم زدند.
items.body_text:
این تیم در آستانه دیدار شنبه لیگ ملتهای اروپا مقابل انگلیس در ورزشگاه ومبلی، با رکورد ۳۸ بازی پیاپی بدون شکست در مسابقات ملی وارد میدان میشود.
- قهرمان یورو ۲۰۰۸ 
- قهرمان جام جهانی ۲۰۱۰
- قهرمان یورو ۲۰۱۲
- قهرمان یورو ۲۰۲۴
- قهرمان جام جهانی ۲۰۲۶
این تیم از شکست یک بر صفر مقابل کلمبیا در سال ۲۰۲۴ تاکنون نباخته است.
موفقیتهای فوتبال اسپانیا به تیم ملی بزرگسالان مردان محدود نمیشود؛
- شش قهرمانی اروپا در رده زیر ۱۹ سال
- سه قهرمانی اروپا در رده زیر ۲۱ سال
- قهرمانی جام جهانی زنان در سال ۲۰۲۳
در سطح باشگاهی نیز تیمهای اسپانیایی از سال ۲۰۰۹ تاکنون نیمی از تمام عناوین قهرمانی ممکن در لیگ قهرمانان اروپا و لیگ اروپا را به دست آوردهاند.
بیبیسی نقش لاماسیا را یکی از عوامل کلیدی تداوم موفقیت اسپانیا میداند؛ هشت محصول آکادمی بارسلونا در تیم قهرمان جام جهانی ۲۰۱۰ حضور داشتند و همین تعداد نیز در تیم قهرمان جهان در سال ۲۰۲۶ بازی کردند.
نفوذ بارسلونا
هشت بازیکن پرورشیافته در آکادمی لاماسیای بارسلونا در تیم اسپانیایی حضور داشتند که با هدایت ویسنته دلبوسکه قهرمان جام جهانی ۲۰۱۰ شد. در تیم لوییس دلافوئنته که تابستان امسال بار دیگر جام جهانی را بالای سر برد نیز هشت محصول این آکادمی حضور داشتند.
بارسلونا در سال ۱۹۹۲ با هدایت کرویف و با سبک «فوتبال کامل» برای نخستین بار قهرمان جام باشگاههای اروپا شد؛ سبکی که تیم ملی هلند در دهه ۱۹۷۰، با حضور خود کرویف، پیشگام آن بود و بعدها بین سالهای ۲۰۰۸ تا ۲۰۱۲ در دوران مربیگری پپ گواردیولا در نیوکمپ بازتاب پیدا کرد.
در آن دوره، بارسلونا سه فصل پیاپی قهرمان لالیگا شد و اسپانیا نیز در فاصله قهرمانیهایش در جام ملتهای اروپا در سالهای ۲۰۰۸ و ۲۰۱۲، جام جهانی ۲۰۱۰ را فتح کرد.
ژاوی، آندرس اینیستا و سرخیو بوسکتس در سیستمی پرورش یافتند که بازیکنان در آن مالکیت توپ و بازی موقعیتی را در خالصترین شکل آن میآموختند.
جوردی گراتاکوس، مدیر بینالمللی آکادمیهای بارسلونا از سال ۲۰۰۹ تا ۲۰۱۱ و سپس از ۲۰۱۶ تا ۲۰۲۰، به رادیو ۵ لایو بیبیسی گفت: «مهمترین نکته، درک معنای تاکتیکی یک اقدام فنی است. منظورم تربیت بازیکنان باهوشی است که از نظر فنی نیز بسیار توانمند باشند.»
او افزود: «در این سطح، همه بازیکنان از نظر فنی بسیار خوب هستند. مهمترین بازیکنان کسانیاند که همیشه بهترین تصمیم را در زمین میگیرند و باعث بهتر شدن دیگران میشوند.»
مدیر پیشین بینالمللی آکادمیهای بارسلونا گفت: «هدف اصلی آماده کردن بازیکنان برای قرار گرفتن در موقعیت مناسب است. این یک آموزش باز است؛ شرایط، زمینه و محیطی ایجاد میکنید که بازیکن در آن باید تصمیم بگیرد و مربی نیز باید بگوید: "این بهترین انتخاب بود؛ دفعه بعد گزینه دیگر را انتخاب کن." مهمترین مساله این است که خود بازیکنان باید در جریان بازی تصمیم بگیرند.»
هانسی فلیک در دو فصل نخست حضورش به عنوان سرمربی بارسلونا، کاری را که گواردیولا انجام داده بود تکرار کرد؛ و این شباهت فقط به دو قهرمانی پیاپی در لالیگا محدود نمیشود.
محصولات آکادمی موتور محرک پروژه او هستند. لامین یامال، دنی اولمو و پائو کوبارسی به بازیکنانی کلیدی در سطح باشگاهی و ملی تبدیل شدهاند؛ درست مانند نسل سالهای ۲۰۰۸ تا ۲۰۱۲.
اسپانیا فرمول تکرار موفقیت را پیدا کرده و بارسلونا در قلب این فرمول قرار دارد.
سرزمین باسک
اگر بارسلونا و کاتالونیا نماینده هنر فوتبال اسپانیا باشند، سرزمین باسک نماینده شخصیت آن است.
پنج بازیکن تیم اسپانیا در جام جهانی ۲۰۲۶ از این منطقه بودند و در اتلتیک بیلبائو یا رئال سوسیداد پرورش یافته بودند؛ دو باشگاهی که هنگام قهرمانی اسپانیا در یورو ۲۰۲۴، هشت بازیکن تیم ملی در آنها بازی میکردند.
میکل مرینو نیز هست؛ بازیکنی که در مرحله یکچهارم نهایی یورو ۲۰۲۴ گل پیروزی مقابل آلمان را زد و سپس در شش مسابقه مقدماتی جام جهانی شش گل به ثمر رساند و در تابستان نیز گلهای دیرهنگام پیروزیبخش مقابل پرتغال و بلژیک را زد.
مرینو باسکی نیست، اما اهل پامپلونا در منطقه خودمختار ناوار است؛ منطقهای که فرهنگ اسپانیایی و باسکی هر دو تاثیر قابل توجهی بر آن دارند.
تنها پنج کیلومتر آنطرفتر از پامپلونا، شهر سیسور مایور قرار دارد؛ شهری که سزار آسپیلیکوئتا، کاپیتان سابق چلسی و ملیپوش اسپانیا، در آن بزرگ شده است.
آسپیلیکوئتا در توصیف فرهنگ باسک به رادیو ۵ لایو بیبیسی گفت: «انضباط، فرهنگ سختکوشی، تسلیم نشدن و تابآوری؛ بدون خودنمایی زیاد. معمولا مردم میخواهند این فرهنگ مبارزه و سرسختی را نشان دهند؛ چیزی شبیه فوتبال انگلیس، با نبردهای بیشتر، بازی فیزیکیتر و جنبه فنی کمتر. اما از نظر تاکتیکی نیز تیمها منسجمترند، شناخت بسیار خوبی از محل حرکت خود دارند و وقتی صاحب توپ میشوند، س

items.body_text:
یک منبع نزدیک به خانواده احمد قاسمپور پیلهرودی، از کشتهشدگان اعتراضات دیماه، به ایراناینترنشنال گفت پس از مخالفت خانواده با ثبت نام او بهعنوان «شهید» و «بسیجی»، فشارها بر آنان افزایش یافته است.
در تازهترین مورد، به پدر قاسمپور هشدار داده شده است برای سالگرد فرزندش مراسم برگزار نکند.
به گفته این منبع، فردی که خود را مرتبط با بنیاد شهید معرفی کرده، همچنین از پدر قاسمپور خواسته است مانع ادامه فعالیت دخترانش در شبکههای اجتماعی شود.
او تهدید کرده است در صورت ادامه انتشار مطالب درباره احمد، علیه آنان «اقدام قانونی» خواهد شد.
منبع نزدیک به خانواده تاکید کرد: «میخواهند ما را ساکت کنند.»
او افزود خانواده با وجود این تهدیدها قصد دارد مراسم سالگرد احمد را در آرامستان «بهشت علی» اشتهارد برگزار کند.
بر پایه بیانیه شورای سردبیری ایراناینترنشنال، بیش از ۳۶ هزار و ۵۰۰ نفر در جریان سرکوب هدفمند انقلاب ملی به دستور علی خامنهای، دیکتاتور پیشین ایران، کشته شدند.
پیشنهاد ۲۰۰ میلیون تومانی و مخالفت خانواده
منبع آگاه در ادامه به ایراناینترنشنال گفت خانواده قاسمپور پیشتر یکی از بستگان خود را در جنگ هشتساله ایران و عراق از دست داده و از همین رو در بنیاد شهید پرونده داشته است.
او افزود پس از کشته شدن احمد، تماسهایی از سوی بنیاد شهید با خانواده برقرار شد و از آنان خواسته شد رضایت دهند نام او بهعنوان «شهید» و «بسیجی» به ثبت برسد.
بر اساس اطلاعات رسیده، در مقطعی حتی پرداخت ۲۰۰ میلیون تومان برای معرفی احمد بهعنوان «شهید» پیشنهاد شد، اما خانواده آن را نپذیرفت.
به گفته منبع آگاه، پس از این تصمیم، فشارها بر خانواده افزایش یافت. خط تلفن منزل آنان با دستور مقام قضایی قطع شد و اعضای خانواده معتقدند تماسهایشان تحت نظارت قرار دارد.
این منبع خبر داد در یکی از مراسمهای پیشین احمد، نیروهایی در محل حضور یافتند و به خانواده اعلام کردند شمار شرکتکنندگان نباید از ۱۰ نفر بیشتر شود.
خانواده این محدودیت را نپذیرفت و با وجود هشدار برای خودداری از ثبت عکس و فیلم، از مراسم تصویربرداری کرد.
سارا حسین، رییس کمیته حقیقتیاب سازمان ملل درباره ایران، ۳۰ شهریور اعلام کرد بسیاری از موارد نقض حقوق بشر در سرکوب اعتراضات دیماه در حد جنایت علیه بشریت بوده است.
احمد قاسمپور چگونه کشته شد؟
احمد قاسمپور پیلهرودی، ۳۴ ساله، ۱۹ دیماه در محدوده فلکه سوم فردیس با اصابت گلوله جنگی به قلبش کشته شد.
منبع نزدیک به خانواده گفت هنگام شدت گرفتن اعتراضات، اعضای خانواده در تماس تلفنی با احمد صدای تیراندازی شنیدند.
احمد در این گفتوگو خبر داد که نیروهای حکومتی به مردم شلیک میکنند. این تماس پس از شنیدن صدای فردی که کمک میخواست، قطع شد.
به گفته منبع، احمد برای کمک به این فرد رفت و هدف گلولهای قرار گرفت که از بالای مجتمع تجاری ارگ فردیس شلیک شد.
حدود نیم ساعت بعد، خانواده از زخمی شدن او مطلع شدند، اما زمانی که پدرش به محل رسید، احمد جان باخته بود.
پیکر او در آرامستان «بهشت علی» اشتهارد به خاک سپرده شد.
بر اساس گزارشها و شواهد متعدد، در بسیاری از شهرها، برای تحویل پیکر کشتهشدگان از خانوادههای داغدار مبالغی سنگین با عنوان «حق تیر» دریافت شده است.
همچنین در برخی موارد، با وجود مخالفت خانوادهها، کشتهشدگان بهعنوان «بسیجی» و «شهید» معرفی شدهاند.
گسترش پویش «یک شمع، یک نام، یک یاد» از سوی خانوادههای جاویدنامان دیماه با خشم و تهدید نهادهای امنیتی جمهوری اسلامی روبهرو شده است.
اطلاعات رسیده به ایراناینترنشنال حاکی است نیروهای امنیتی با احضار و تهدید شماری از خانوادهها، اعمال فشار برای حذف مطالب، محدود کردن صفحات اینستاگرام و مسدود کردن سیمکارتها، در تلاشند فعالیت این خانوادهها و ادامه این کارزار را محدود کنند.
پویش «یک شمع، یک نام، یک یاد» در هفتههای اخیر از سوی خانوادهها و نزدیکان جاویدنامان دیماه راهاندازی شد. شرکتکنندگان در این پویش با روشن کردن شمع و انتشار نام، تصویر و ویدیوهای جاویدنامان، یاد آنان را گرامی میدارند.
بر اساس اطلاعات موجود، در پی گسترش این پویش، نیروهای امنیتی با شماری از خانوادههای دادخواه تماس گرفته و از آنان خواستند پستهای مرتبط با این پویش و در مواردی مطالب پیشین درباره فرزندان یا بستگان کشتهشده خود را از شبکههای اجتماعی حذف کنند.
منابع مطلع همچنین گفتند صفحات اینستاگرام برخی اعضای خانوادههای دادخواه از دسترس خارج یا محدود شده و امکان ادامه فعالیت در این صفحات از آنان گرفته شده است.
مسدود شدن سیمکارتها و فشار بر فعالیت مجازی
بنا بر گزارشهای رسیده، سیمکارت شماری از خانوادههای دادخواه نیز پس از مشارکت در پویش «یک شمع، یک نام، یک یاد»، بدون اطلاع قبلی و بدون دریافت توضیح رسمی، مسدود شد.
