items.title: Polish MP calls for immigration crackdown after Ukrainian kills priest
items.summary: Polish ex-deputy PM Kowalczyk urged tighter border controls, saying the deadly attack could prompt a “wave of hostility” toward Ukrainians Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Polish MP calls for immigration crackdown after Ukrainian kills priest
Poland should tighten its border controls following a deadly knife attack by a Ukrainian national, former Polish Deputy Prime Minister and current Law and Justice (PiS) MP Henryk Kowalczyk has said, warning that the killing could fuel another wave of anti-Ukrainian sentiment.
A 31-year-old Ukrainian citizen attacked five people at a Catholic abbey in the southeastern city of Jaroslaw on Thursday, killing a priest and injuring four others, according to Polish officials. The suspect, who according to investigators had entered Poland from Germany overnight and was apparently heading toward the Ukrainian border, was detained at the scene. Prosecutors are investigating the circumstances and motive behind the attack.
“This will certainly trigger another wave of hostility toward Ukrainians,” Henryk Kowalczyk, an MP with the conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, told Polish Radio’s Jedynka on Friday.
The lawmaker stressed that politicians should not inflame anti-Ukrainian sentiment, but added: “We are talking about the facts. People draw their own conclusions: a Ukrainian killed a Polish priest and injured many people. There is no need to fuel anything here.”
Kowalczyk argued that the incident should prompt Warsaw to step up border controls, reiterating that the suspect had entered Poland from Germany.
“We do not control the German-Polish border at all,” he said, contrasting Warsaw’s approach with Berlin’s selective checks. Poland “cannot accept all migrants who ended up in Germany and then enter our country,” he argued.
The MP also said that punishing the attacker was not enough, urging the Polish authorities to draw broader conclusions from the deadly incident.
“This is a signal that we should check people in advance, rather than just say that we will punish them severely,” he said.
The attack comes as Polish attitudes toward Ukrainian migrants have deteriorated sharply. A July survey by polling agency CBOS found that, for the first time since it began tracking the issue, a majority of Poles opposed accepting them, with 52% against and 42% in favor. Support had stood at 94% shortly after the escalation of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022.
Another CBOS poll published in September found that the share of Poles who believe reconciliation with Ukrainians is possible had fallen to a record low of 53%, while 38% said it was impossible.
Kiev’s ambassador to Warsaw, Vasily Bondar, said earlier this week that attacks and acts of aggression against Ukrainians had risen by around 30% in the first half of 2026, as public attitudes toward refugees continued to sour. He said Polish police had recorded 180 such incidents during the period, compared with 275 throughout 2025.
Relations between Warsaw and Kiev have also been strained by historical grievances. Tensions escalated after Ukraine’s Vladimir Zelensky named a military unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), which Poland holds responsible for massacres of Polish civilians during World War II.
Polish President Karol Nawrocki subsequently stripped Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle, Poland’s highest state honor, citing the decision to honor the UPA.

items.title: UK issues Falklands/Malvinas defense warning
items.summary: UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting says Britain can defend the Falkland Islands as Argentina steps up its sovereignty claim Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
UK issues Falklands/Malvinas defense warning
Britain is fully capable of defending the Falkland Islands if Argentina attempts to invade and take control of the territory, UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting has warned.
The UK has administered the South Atlantic archipelago, known in Argentina as the Malvinas, since 1833. Buenos Aires maintains that the islands are part of its own territory.
The two countries fought a war over the islands in 1982 after Argentine forces seized them and Britain sent a naval task force to retake them. Residents overwhelmingly voted to remain British territory in a 2013 referendum, which Argentina disputes.
The decades-old dispute has recently flared up again, with Argentine President Javier Milei stepping up the country’s sovereignty claim and condemning British-approved oil development around the islands as unlawful.
The renewed tensions come as US President Donald Trump has cast doubt on whether America would come to Britain’s aid in another conflict over the territory. Milei raised the issue at the UN General Assembly in New York this week, pointing to the Sea Lion offshore oil project and warning that Argentina could “take matters into our own hands” if the UN fails to act.
In an interview with The Sun on Sunday published on Saturday, Streeting dismissed Milei’s position as the “same old bogus propaganda,” arguing that “the Argentinians lack the ability” to seize the archipelago.
“We have the ability to defend the Falkland Islands,” he said. Asked if Britain can protect the islands militarily if Argentina sends warships, Streeting said yes.
Milei has stepped up pressure over the dispute, launching sanctions proceedings against companies and individuals linked to Sea Lion and pledging additional funding for a naval base in Tierra del Fuego to strengthen Argentina’s presence in the South Atlantic.
Milei has seized on the possibility of a shift in Washington’s position, saying in a televised address earlier this month that “winds of change” around the world favor Argentina’s sovereignty claim.
The US recognizes Britain’s de facto administration of the islands but has remained neutral on the competing sovereignty claims.
In April, however, an internal Pentagon email reportedly outlined options for punishing NATO members that the US says failed to support the war against Iran. According to Reuters, one option is reassessing US diplomatic support for Britain’s position on the Falklands.
Trump has since questioned whether America would help Britain in another conflict over the islands, citing London’s refusal to support the US against Iran.
“Your country was not there to help me,” the president said when asked whether the US would come to Britain’s aid, noting that then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer told him Britain had no ships available. Trump called the response “pretty sad.”

items.title: Russian and German FMs Meet for First Time Since Ukraine Invasion
items.summary: Russia’s Foreign Ministry said that the ministers discussed bilateral relations and the war in Ukraine.
items.body_text:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov met his German counterpart Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Saturday, their countries’ first talks at foreign minister level since before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Russia’s Foreign Ministry said the German side had requested the talks and that the ministers discussed bilateral relations and the war in Ukraine.
“On these and other issues, Johann Wadephul reaffirmed the German government’s position, which has been stated publicly on numerous occasions,” the ministry said.
The meeting came amid renewed tensions between the two countries after Germany accused Russia of attempting to blow up two cargo planes at Leipzig airport in August using a drone rigged with explosives.
Wadephul told the UN Security Council this week that German support for Ukraine remained firm and called for a ceasefire and negotiations toward a lasting peace.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova claimed the German side had sought restrictions on media access to Saturday’s meeting, including a ban on questions and audio recordings of the opening remarks.
Lavrov last met a German foreign minister in January 2022, when he held talks with Wadephul’s predecessor Annalena Baerbock weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine.

items.title: Evan Gershkovich Says His Arrest in Russia Was Carefully Planned FSB Sting
items.summary: Gershkovich became the first U.S. reporter arrested on espionage charges in Russia since the Cold War when he was arrested in 2023.
items.body_text:
U.S. reporter Evan Gershkovich, in his first detailed published account of his arrest in Russia in 2023, says he was the victim of an elaborate sting operation by the FSB security service.
In an extract from his book "This Cursed Beautiful Land," Gershkovich says that while working on a story for The Wall Street Journal about Russian military production, he held two meetings with the union boss of a factory in Yekaterinburg, a major defense-industry hub.
At their second encounter, in a steakhouse, the source produced papers with hand-copied tables of figures, telling the reporter that they related to the production of tanks.
As he jotted down notes, Gershkovich said, he heard the sound of marching feet and looked up to see a group of masked men approaching their table.
"A pang of guilt ripped through me: Had I compromised a source? But panic immediately replaced that thought. Instinct took over, my hands moving to hide the papers in the gap between the bench and the wall," he wrote in the book extract, published by the Journal on Friday.
"The men quickly descended on us. An arm was yanking my neck, pulling me off the couch... Someone shouted: 'You are under arrest by the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation'."
A long sentence, then a prisoner swap
Gershkovich, then 31, became the first U.S. reporter arrested on espionage charges in Russia since the Cold War. He was later sentenced to 16 years in prison before being freed in an East-West prisoner swap in August 2024.
He writes that he and his editors had considered the risks of the reporting trip and agreed that the source should not bring any documents to the meeting; if he did so, Gershkovich should not accept anything from him.
But at the meeting, the source had "thrust the papers into my hands."
Although he had reported on the arrests of other Americans in Russia, and on the targeting and even murder of Russian journalists, Gershkovich writes that the "unspoken rule" was that foreign correspondents enjoyed a degree of immunity: they might be expelled, but not arrested.
Reeling with shock, he was handcuffed, had a black sack placed over his head and was whisked into a van where he was placed in a chokehold and punched in the abdomen while being questioned, he writes.
FSB 'backup plan'
Gershkovich said that since his release he had learned of evidence that the FSB had a "backup plan" to arrest him on another of his planned reporting trips, to Siberia, if the Yekaterinburg operation had failed.
He said he believes the two meetings with the source in Yekaterinburg were designed to help the FSB persuade President Vladimir Putin that he was a spy and secure approval for his arrest at the second meeting.
"Putin, it seems to me, fully bought into this narrative," he said.
The Kremlin did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Putin said in a February 2024 interview with U.S. television host Tucker Carlson that Gershkovich had been "caught red-handed" while collecting confidential information.
The journalist, his newspaper and the U.S. government all strongly deny the allegation that Gershkovich was a spy.

items.title: Russia Can Restart 80% of Black Sea Grain Export Terminals if Attacks Stop – Analysis
items.summary: The disruption to shipments has driven up global grain prices and renewed concerns about food security linked to the war in Ukraine.
items.body_text:
Russia could quickly restart up to 80% of its grain terminal capacity in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov if diplomatic efforts to halt mutual attacks by Russia and Ukraine result in a ceasefire, a Reuters analysis of industry data showed on Friday.
But three terminals accounting for about 20% of Russia's grain export infrastructure in the area have suffered heavy damage and could take months to repair, the analysis showed.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is leading an international effort by grain-importing countries to restore Black Sea grain trade, which has been stalled by attacks on ports and vessels in recent months.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday that India, Egypt and other Middle Eastern countries were also involved. The Kremlin acknowledged diplomatic contacts but said Russia was finding alternate export routes in the meantime.
Reuters analyzed the condition of Russia's nine major grain terminals in the region, as well as smaller facilities in the Sea of Azov and Don river delta, using information from four sources familiar with terminal operations.
The sources spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the issue. Before the attacks, the route handled up to 70% of Russia's grain exports.
Russia is the world's largest wheat exporter, and disruption to shipments has driven up global grain prices and renewed concerns about food security linked to the war in Ukraine.
The analysis found that three of nine major terminals had suffered serious damage in Ukrainian attacks, affecting about one-fifth of grain-loading capacity in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov.
Extent of damage
One of Russia's three largest grain terminals, NKHP in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, suffered serious damage in an Aug. 12 attack. The terminal has annual capacity of 7.1 million metric tons and repairs could take up to six months.
"At NKHP, that conveyor gallery was completely destroyed. It actually collapsed onto the road and was lying across it," one source at Novorossiysk told Reuters.
"The staff were sent home for six months. I don't even know how long the shutdown will last," he said, adding that damage at the other two Novorossiysk terminals, KSK and NZT, was minor and that both were ready to resume operations.
The company said repairs at NKHP could take up to four months.
The other damaged terminals, ZTKT at the Black Sea port of Taman and a terminal in Taganrog on the Azov Sea, have halted operations although the full extent of the damage could not be established. Together, ZTKT and Taganrog have annual capacity of 6.7 million tons.
ZTKT, which has annual capacity of 5.5 million tons, was hit on July 30 and is unable to load grain, another source said, adding that it was unclear when operations could resume.
The analysis showed that terminals with combined capacity of about 53 million tons are currently idle because of security risks but could resume operations. Total grain terminal capacity in the region is about 67 million tons.

Berlin’s ‘Russian House’ stayed open despite Russia’s war in Ukraine and EU sanctions, shielded by a reciprocal deal over Moscow’s Goethe-Institut. Germany’s sabotage accusation was the final straw.
In early September, Germany’s Foreign Ministry announced the closure of the Russian House in Berlin, Russia’s largest cultural center abroad. The center had operated in the heart of the German capital for more than 40 years. It remained open after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, even as similar institutions across Europe shut down. What finally brought it to an end was a drone attack on Leipzig Airport that German authorities described as Russian sabotage. Meduza tells the center’s story.
In early August, a DHL cargo plane approaching Leipzig Airport had to climb sharply when the airport unexpectedly closed. After the plane landed in Hanover, inspectors found minor damage caused by a collision with an unidentified flying object.
At Leipzig Airport, bomb disposal experts found and defused a drone fitted with explosives and a detonator near a Ukrainian An-124 cargo plane. Ten days later, another drone bearing traces of explosives was found near the airport.
German authorities investigated for nearly a month before blaming Russia for the attempted sabotage. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced Germany’s response: the closure of Russia’s consulate in Bonn and the Russian House in Berlin. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova criticized the decision. Speaking about the Russian House, she said:
The Russian House was obviously a thorn in their side. Why?.. Its first and foremost purpose is to teach Russian. Demand was enormous. […] That’s the Russian House’s main offense — the reason the German establishment disliked it so much.
There are more than 70 Russian Houses worldwide. The full-scale war has disrupted their work.
The worldwide network of Russian Houses took its present form in 2008, when President Dmitry Medvedev signed a decree creating Rossotrudnichestvo, a Russian federal agency for cultural outreach abroad. Officially overseen by the Foreign Ministry, the agency runs Russian language courses and promotes Russian culture, science, and education.
Before the war, Russian Houses operated in at least 77 countries. Their work became more difficult after the EU imposed sanctions on Rossotrudnichestvo following the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In July 2022, the EU added the agency to its sanctions list, accusing it of promoting the ideas of the “Russian World,” funding propaganda projects, and spreading “Kremlin narratives” and historical revisionism.
After the EU’s decision, Russian Houses suspended operations in six European countries: Slovenia, Slovakia, Croatia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, and Romania. The Russian House in Baku also suspended operations in 2025 after a passenger plane crashed near Aktau. In July 2026, the Russian House in Chișinău closed indefinitely. Moldovan authorities called it a “tool of the Kremlin’s hybrid influence.”
In Berlin, however, the Russian House kept operating after the sanctions against Rossotrudnichestvo. Its seven-story modernist building on Friedrichstraße, within walking distance of the Russian embassy, opened in 1984 as the House of Soviet Culture and Science. It was the Soviet Union’s largest cultural center abroad. Russia later took ownership of the building, and the center became the Russian House of Culture and Science.
The Russian House’s activities changed little over more than 40 years. At its 20th anniversary celebration in 2004, then-director Anatoly Bogushevsky said the center drew about 300,000 visitors a year. Its main aim, he said, was to give people in Germany “as comprehensive a picture as possible of a new, reformed Russia seeking to strengthen democracy.” Its activities centered on a Russian language center, a Russian college, a Pushkin Library with more than 40,000 books, small clubs and workshops, concerts, an

items.body_text:
A humanitarian crisis is gripping Russian-occupied Oleshky as food deliveries stop and safe evacuation becomes nearly impossible
Oleshky (Alyoshki in Russian) is a city on the left bank of the Dnipro River, across from Kherson on the right bank. Only nine kilometers (about six miles) separate them in a straight line. People once crossed between them by bridge, but the bridge is now closed. The two cities are on opposite sides of the front: Ukraine controls Kherson, while Russia has controlled Oleshky since 2022. As in other cities near the front, life in Oleshky is difficult and dangerous. By September 2026, conditions had deteriorated so badly that people in both Ukraine and Russia were calling the situation critical. Those who remain are trying to survive without food, electricity, and adequate medical care. They cannot leave safely and often cannot even bury their loved ones. Here is what Meduza has been able to learn about conditions in the city.
The situation in Oleshky was already being called critical in Ukraine in the spring. By September, even the Kremlin agreed
“It’s a humanitarian catastrophe, people are driven to despair,” Tetiana Hasanenko, head of Oleshky’s evacuated Ukrainian administration, told The Kyiv Independent in April 2026. She tries to keep in touch with residents and tells Ukrainian media what is happening there.
“If the situation doesn’t improve, people will just die there from hunger. Because there’s no way out, no food supplies coming in,” Anna, an Oleshky resident who recently escaped to a Ukrainian-controlled area, told the outlet.
In the summer, the U.N. mission in Ukraine said Oleshky’s last store had closed in January 2026, and all food deliveries had stopped by late May. Medical care was available only for the most urgent cases. Ambulances no longer responded to calls, and patients with serious conditions could not be transferred to other hospitals. Anyone trying to enter or leave the city faced two dangers: drones overhead and mines on the ground.
In July, Human Rights Watch said shortages of food and medical care in Oleshky were compounded by the collapse of basic utilities. The city had no electricity or gas, and people had switched to wood-burning stoves. People who had managed to leave Oleshky said they were afraid even to go out for water because drones circled overhead and mines lay scattered along the streets. Human Rights Watch said it was impossible to say for certain whose weapons they were. Both Russian and Ukrainian forces had used drones and mines in the area during the war.
At the time, the Russian occupation authorities in the Kherson region still denied that there was a humanitarian catastrophe. By August, however, they acknowledged that Oleshky and nearby villages had no water or electricity, communications were unreliable, and utility crews could not make repairs because of shelling. On September 21, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the situation in the city critical. “The Kyiv regime is doing everything it can to obstruct deliveries [of food and medicine]. Russian troops are continuing to work to resolve the situation,” he said.
Oleshky is in its fifth year under occupation. Why is there talk of a humanitarian catastrophe now?
Continued fighting and the gradual deterioration of infrastructure appear to have made conditions worse.
In the fall of 2022, when Russian troops retreated from the right bank of the Dnipro and left Kherson, Oleshky became a frontline city. The destruction of the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant dam flooded Oleshky in the summer of 2023, badly damaging its infrastructure. The occupation administration says Ukrainian attacks have hampered repairs and deliveries of food and medicine.

items.body_text:
Putin says Russia will not attack Europe and blames Ukraine for the breakdown in peace talks
This is a brief summary of statements Vladimir Putin made to journalists on the sidelines of the United Cultures Forum in St. Petersburg. Their full meaning and context have been preserved, though some passages may have been edited or rearranged.
Shortly before the State Duma elections, Ukraine said it was ready to return to negotiations. Russia was prepared to resume contact after the elections. But on the main voting day, Kyiv attacked Moscow, launched more than 1,600 drones, and struck polling stations. After what they did, we’ll consider how to respond. We’ll decide whether to resume negotiations based on our own interests. Ukraine must feel the effects of Russia’s retaliatory strikes. The strikes are so destructive that Ukraine is raising the prospect of a ceasefire and trying to stop Russia’s “Geran” drone strikes. Kyiv’s provocations only make things worse for Ukraine. Russia is not preparing for military action against Europe; we have no such plans. European countries themselves are escalating tensions and engaging in provocations. They want to keep using Ukraine as a tool in their fight against Russia. We know that Russian speakers’ rights are being violated in the Baltic states, and we are responding with humanitarian measures.
At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication.
If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at [email protected].
To read Meduza’s exclusive content in English, please subscribe to our newsletter.

items.title: 'Oye maar kaise raha hai': On cam, Delhi minister Parvesh Verma slaps man
items.summary: Captured on video during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar, Delhi, PWD Minister Parvesh Verma's unexpected slap to a young man has stirred controversy. Released by the Aam Aadmi Party, the footage shows Verma confronting the individual before a security guard intervenes. This incident has ignited debate regarding the behavior of public servants in the line of duty, attracting the attention of numerous onlookers.
items.body_text:
NEW DELHI: Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma was seen allegedly slapping a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar on Sunday.
In the video shared by AAP leaders, Verma can be seen pulling down the man's mobile phone with his left hand and slapping him across the face with his right hand.
The man, identified as Saheb, then appears to confront the minister before a security guard steps between them. Several people can be seen gathered around the two.
"Oye maar kaise raha hai (How are you hitting)," a man can be heard saying in the video.
The incident took place while Verma was inspecting a road in the area.
Speaking to ANI, Saheb said he handles social media activities for the local MLA and had come to the spot after the PWD department called them to inspect the condition of the road.
"I showed him how the road surface was breaking apart. When this was pointed out, the Minister couldn't handle it; he raised his hand against me, and his associates threatened to kill me," he said.
Saheb alleged that police personnel were present when the incident took place.
"He must apologise, and whatever disciplinary action is required - such as suspension - should be taken," Saheb said, adding that there was video evidence of the incident.
"We aren't just making claims; there is video evidence of everything. Action must be taken. We have lodged an FIR and will pursue further action," he said.
AAP MLA Jarnail Singh, who represents Tilak Nagar, also shared a video of the incident and accused Verma of assaulting the man who was recording the proceedings.
Singh said he had accompanied Verma during the road inspection and pointed out portions of the road where the surface was coming off. He alleged that instead of taking action over the road's condition, Verma slapped the person recording the incident.
Singh also alleged that the SHO of Vikaspuri police station was present when the incident occurred and accused the officer of helping the minister leave the spot.
"We have called the emergency number - 112 - to report this," Singh said in the video.
Singh said he would remain at the spot until an FIR was registered and Verma was arrested. He also called on the Delhi Police Commissioner to take action against the minister under the law.
Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal also shared Singh's video and called for Verma's arrest.
Parvesh Verma reveals the 'truth behind' video
Verma, responding to the video, said people should know the "truth behind" what he described as a video being circulated by the 
Aam Aadmi Party
.
He alleged that road construction work had been underway on the Vikaspuri Ring Road for several days and claimed that Jarnail Singh had been pressuring PWD engineers to introduce him to the contractor and arrange a commission for him.
Verma said a PWD engineer had lodged a complaint at a police station and was getting an FIR registered.
He further alleged that Singh would visit the site after roadwork was completed at night, tear up the newly laid road and record videos alleging corruption because he had not received a commission.
Verma said he had stopped at the site on Sunday to inspect the road and found that the work was progressing well. He said local residents told him the road had not been built for 15 years.
"I personally called the local MLA, Jarnail Singh, three times. I waited for him for 45 minutes. I had not called any of our own party workers to the site," Verma said.
He alleged that Singh arrived with his own workers and "immediately began behaving rudely".

items.title: NEET leak fallout: CISF to guard NTA’s confidential exam areas
items.summary: Responding to the alarming issue of exam paper leaks, the National Testing Agency has fortified its security protocols. A dedicated team of 29 CISF personnel is now assigned to the agency's new office for rigorous oversight. In addition to advancing cybersecurity measures, the NTA is revisiting its entire examination-cycle systems to thwart unauthorized access. Independent audits will also be conducted, aiming for a significant improvement in examination integrity moving forward.
items.body_text:
(Representative image): CISF will carry out access-control and screening measures, including frisking with X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs).
NEW DELHI: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has tightened security around its examination work with 39 CISF personnel deployed at its New Delhi office. The force will monitor confidential areas, control access and screen staff and visitors. The move follows repeated questions over paper leaks and administrative lapses, including the handling of sensitive examination material.The CISF personnel have been deployed at entry and exit points of the confidential areas at the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. They will carry out access-control and screening measures, including frisking with X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs).The NTA has also demarcated confidential areas within its new premises. Movement and operations in these areas will be closely monitored as part of efforts to prevent unauthorised access to examination material."Confidential areas have been demarcated in the building where the movement and operations will be strictly monitored to ensure that a foolproof system is in place. The Home Ministry has approved Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) security cover for the premises," a senior official said.
NTA shifts sensitive operations to new office
The security measures come after the NTA moved its confidential and sensitive operations from its earlier office in Okhla to a new facility on Minto Road."A dedicated over 55,000 square feet office space has been allotted in the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. The fifth floor and parts of the fourth and sixth floors of the said building have been allotted to the National Testing Agency. Confidential and sensitive operations have been shifted in the last one month to the newly allotted building," the official said.Other parts of the Government of India Press Building are already protected by the CISF. The NTA will now have a dedicated security arrangement for its examination-related confidential areas.The agency's new security framework also includes tighter monitoring of examination-critical technology systems. The NTA is working on strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage."Arrangements are being made in mission mode for establishing strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage for all examination-critical workloads."
Cybersecurity measures being strengthened
The NTA is also reviewing the security of systems used throughout the examination cycle. These include candidate registration, fee payment, admit cards, computer-based testing, OMR processing, result systems and other examination-supporting infrastructure."Running security readiness reviews of all examination-supporting systems before each examination cycle in coordination with NTA's technology function and coordinating with NTA's test-security function on the technical security of examination day workflows -- including biometric authentication, face-matching, CCTV systems and live monitoring infrastructure -- are among the action items being worked upon," the official said.The agency is also preparing an examination-specific cyber-incident response system. It plans to have enhanced security operations centre monitoring and rapid-response capabilities on examination days.The NTA has designated a dedicated chief information security officer (CISO) to oversee information security."The position of general manager and CISO has been advertised, and the selection process is at an advanced stage. Independent third-party cyber-security audits by CERT-In and C-DAC empanelled agencies continue to be undertaken," the official said.
Paper leak exposed gaps in confidential section
The latest security measures follow the 2024 NEET-UG paper leak, which triggered nationwide student protests

items.title: Tamil Nadu govt rolls back law and order department’s RTI exemption amid backlash
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government faced backlash after it issued a notification that exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act. Critics, including numerous political leaders, argued that such an action would jeopardize transparency and obstruct public access to crucial law records. In response to widespread criticism, the government promptly withdrew the exemption, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the RTI Act.
items.body_text:
Tamil Nadu govt received backlash even from member of its ally Congress over the notification
The Tamil Nadu government on Sunday withdrew its notification exempting the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information Act, hours after issuing the Gazette notification that classified the department as an "Intelligence and Security Organisation".The rollback came after the move drew criticism from political leaders, including Congress's Karti P Chidambaram and BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan. The government, however, did not publicly cite a specific reason for issuing the exemption or explain why it was withdrawn. An official communication later confirmed that the order issued under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act had been rescinded, reported ANI.
What was the notification?
The original notification, issued by the Human Resources Management Department and published in the state Gazette, used the power available to state governments under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act. The provision allowed a state government to notify an organisation established by it as an intelligence or security organisation, thereby taking it outside the normal scope of the RTI Act.Tamil Nadu's notification designated its Public (Law and Order) Department as such an organisation. Had it remained in force, routine RTI access to a broad range of records held by the department would have been restricted.The records covered included information relating to communal and caste clashes, political agitations, police action and custody, deaths of prisoners, police firing, inquiries into law-and-order incidents and requests for withdrawal of cases arising from political or communal tensions.
The exemption was not absolute. Section 24 specifically preserves access to information relating to allegations of corruption and human-rights violations, subject to the procedure prescribed under the Act.The notification itself invoked Section 24(4) and classified the department as an intelligence and security organisation. The government has not, in the material available publicly gave a detailed explanation for why the Public (Law and Order) Department was brought under this provision.The department handles sensitive law-and-order and policing-related matters, which appears to be the basis on which the exemption was framed. But that is distinct from saying that the government officially justified the move on a particular security ground. The notification, as reported, simply exercised the statutory power under Section 24(4).
The backlash
The proposed exemption would have affected access to records concerning issues such as police firing, custodial deaths, torture, communal and caste clashes and politically sensitive cases, prompting criticism that the move could reduce transparency.Karti Chidambaram initially criticised the decision, saying it "does not set a good precedent" and recalling that the RTI Act was enacted by the UPA government to strengthen democratic accountability."The Law and Order Department handles crucial matters such as examining inquiry reports on police firing, custodial deaths, torture, and deaths of remand prisoners, security-related detention cases, communal and caste clash reports, requests for withdrawal of politically sensitive cases and matters relating to sanction of prosecution for defamatory articles, news items, and speeches. This crucial information is now being shielded from the public. Such rollbacks are not in line with transparent governance. RTI must be expanded, not restricted," Chidambaram posted on X.After the government withdrew the notification, he welcomed the decision, saying: "My unsolicited & friendly advice to the TVK Government & CMO Tamil Nadu â don't let bureaucrats set the tone, tenor & direction of the administration."
BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan also criticised the original notification, saying: "So they are afraid of meeting the press, they are afraid of meeting the people, and they are afraid of the legal proce

items.title: Thailand declares two-day civil service holiday amid floods, could affect court ruling
items.summary: The move could however delay a ‌court decision over electoral ballots ​used in February's election — which could put the election ⁠results in doubt
items.body_text:
Thailand's cabinet on Sunday (September 27, 2026) approved Sept. 28 and 29 as special holidays for civil servants in Bangkok and three surrounding provinces due to heavy rainfall, a move that could affect the timing of a court ruling on electoral ballots used in February's election.
"The measure aims to reduce travel and ease traffic disruptions for the public," it said, adding that important official business scheduled during the holidays may continue as deemed appropriate by their heads.
The move could however delay a court decision over electoral ballots used in February's election — which could put the election results in doubt, though the court has not made any announcement on whether the timing of the verdict would be changed.
The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration declared the capital a disaster-affected area on Saturday (September 26) after nearly 300 mm (12 inches) of rain fell over 48 hours, leading to flooding on major roads that left some cars partly submerged.
Floodwater receded on Sunday (September 27) as rainfall eased, but some residents remained stranded in their homes.

items.title: Afghanistan says 28 fighters killed after crossing from Pakistan
items.summary: The Afghan Defence Ministry alleges Pakistani intelligence trained and sent former Afghan security personnel across the border, an allegation Islamabad has not responded to
items.body_text:
Afghanistan's Defence Ministry said on Sunday (September 27, 2026) that its forces had killed 28 fighters and wounded 32 in the eastern province of Nuristan, after a group it said included Islamic State militants crossed from Pakistan.
The Ministry alleged Pakistani militias had supported the fighters, and that most of them were former Afghan government security personnel. Pakistan's military and Information Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and Reuters could not independently verify the Ministry's account or its casualty figures.
Kabul's claim that Pakistani intelligence trained and sent former Afghan security personnel across the border is a direct allegation of state involvement in an armed incursion. It comes less than a week after Pakistan launched airstrikes inside Afghanistan, saying it had targeted militants. Pakistan has repeatedly accused Afghanistan of sheltering fighters who attack its territory, a charge Kabul denies.
The Ministry said the group crossed into Kamdesh, a district of Nuristan near the Pakistani border, on Saturday (September 26, 2026), intending to carry out attacks. Afghan forces launched an operation, and the surviving fighters fled back across the border towards Pakistani militia positions, it said.
It alleged that Pakistani armed personnel and militia members had coordinated with the fighters, but withdrew when fighting began. The Ministry also accused Pakistani intelligence of taking former Afghan security personnel to Pakistan under the pretext of offering them assistance, training them and sending them towards Nuristan.
The incident follows Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan on September 21, 2026, that Islamabad said killed 28 militants. Afghan officials said civilians were killed, and the U.N. mission in Afghanistan confirmed three civilian deaths.
Published - September 27, 2026 05:10 pm IST

items.summary: आम आदमी पार्टी ने रविवार को X पर एक वीडियो शेयर किया, जिसमें दिल्ली सरकार में मंत्री प्रवेश वर्मा एक लड़के को थप्पड़ मारते नजर आ रहे हैं। AAP का आरोप है कि तिलक नगर में सड़क बनाने में हुए भ्रष्टाचार को लेकर कुछ लोग उनसे सवाल कर रहे थे। इस बीच उन्होंने वहां खड़े एक युवक को थप्पड़ मार दिया। हालांकि इसके बाद उनके गार्ड और मौजूद साथियों ने युवक को दूर हटाया। पीड़ित युवक का आरोप है कि पुलिस के सामने उसे पीटा गया। जान से मारने की धमकी दी गई। उसने पुलिस को शिकायत दी है। मंत्री को लिखित में माफी मांगनी होगी
items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Delhi BJP Minister Slap Video; Parvesh Verma Vs AAP | Arvind Kejriwal
दिल्ली के मंत्री प्रवेश वर्मा ने युवक को थप्पड़ मारा:AAP बोली- भ्रष्टाचार पर सवाल किया था; प्रवेश बोले- मेरे परिवार को गाली दी थी
- कॉपी लिंक
आम आदमी पार्टी ने रविवार को X पर एक वीडियो शेयर किया, जिसमें दिल्ली सरकार में मंत्री प्रवेश वर्मा एक लड़के को थप्पड़ मारते नजर आ रहे हैं। AAP का आरोप है कि तिलक नगर में सड़क बनाने में हुए भ्रष्टाचार को लेकर कुछ लोग उनसे सवाल कर रहे थे।
इस बीच उन्होंने वहां खड़े एक युवक को थप्पड़ मार दिया। हालांकि इसके बाद उनके गार्ड और मौजूद साथियों ने युवक को दूर हटाया।
पीड़ित युवक का आरोप है कि पुलिस के सामने उसे पीटा गया। जान से मारने की धमकी दी गई। उसने पुलिस को शिकायत दी है। मंत्री को लिखित में माफी मांगनी होगी। भाजपा को भी उन्हें सस्पेंड कर देना चाहिए।
विवाद के बाद प्रवेश वर्मा ने वीडियो जारी करके कहा कि जरनैल रात में बनी सड़क सुबह उखाड़ रहे हैं। उन्होंने कमीशन मांगा था, नहीं मिलने पर विवाद खड़ा कर दिया। उन्होंने कहा-
जरनैल के साथियों ने मेरे परिवार को गाली दी, इस हालात में कोई भी आम आदमी जो करता, वही मैंने किया।
दिल्ली में हुए हंगामे की 3 तस्वीरें…
प्रवेश वर्मा-जनरैल के बीच हुई बहस
तिलक नगर की घटना का एक और वीडियो सामने आया है, जिसमें प्रवेश वर्मा और विधायक जनरैल सिंह के बीच बहस होती दिख रही है। जनरैल तारकोल से बनी सड़क के टुकड़े दिखाते हुए प्रवेश से कह रहे हैं- आपने जो सड़क बनाई वो उखाड़ कर दिखा दी।
इस पर प्रवेश ने कहा- गलत नहीं बोलना है, आप 15 साल में नहीं बना पाए। जवाब में जनरैल ने कहा- आप बना दो लेकिन ऐसी मत बनाओ जो 15 घंटे न चले।
इसके बाद मंत्री वर्मा वहां से चले गए। जनरैल उनकी गाड़ी तक पीछे-पीछे जाते हैं, वहीं प्रवेश वीडियो बना रहे युवक को थप्पड़ मार देते हैं।
प्रवेश ने 2.56 मिनट का वीडियो में रखा अपना पक्ष
प्रवेश वर्मा ने एक वीडियो जारी किया, जिसमें वे कह रहे हैं कि “आम आदमी पार्टी जो वीडियो शेयर कर रही है, उसके पीछे की सच्चाई आपको पता होनी चाहिए। विकास पुरी रिंग रोड पर पिछले कई दिनों से सड़क बनाने का काम चल रहा है। उस इलाके के विधायक जरनैल सिंह कई दिनों से PWD विभाग के इंजीनियरों से कह रहे थे कि वे उन्हें कॉन्ट्रैक्टर से मिलवाएं और उनके लिए कमीशन का इंतजाम करें। हमारे इंजीनियर ने पुलिस स्टेशन जाकर शिकायत दर्ज कराई है और उनके खिलाफ FIR दर्ज की जा रही है।”
प्रवेश ने बताया- "आज जब मैं उस रास्ते से जा रहा था, तो मैंने इंजीनियरों से कहा कि मैं एक बार सारे काम देखना चाहता हूं। मैंने देखा काम अच्छे से हो रहा था। स्थानीय लोगों ने मुझे बताया कि 15 साल से सड़क नहीं बनी थी। शायद आम आदमी पार्टी इस बात से बहुत नाखुश है कि दिल्ली में सभी सड़कें बन रही हैं, जिनमें वे सड़कें भी शामिल हैं जो 15 साल से नहीं बनी थीं।"
प्रवेश आगे कहते हैं, "...मैंने 45 मिनट तक उनका इंतजार किया। जब जरनैल सिंह आए, तो उन्होंने पहले ही अपने कार्यकर्ताओं को बता दिया था और उनके साथ आए थे। आते ही उन्होंने बदतमीजी शुरू कर दी। जब उनके एक कार्यकर्ता ने मेरे परिवार को गाली दी, तो ऐसी स्थिति में कोई भी गुस्से में प्रतिक्रिया देगा, और मैंने भी वही किया।"
प्रवेश वर्मा से जुड़े बड़े विवाद
- 2020- शाहीन बाग के प्रदर्शनकारी रेप-हत्या कर सकते हैं: एक वीडियो सामने आया, जिसमें प्रवेश वर्मा ने शाहीन बाग के प्रदर्शनकारियों पर आरोप लगाया था कि वे दिल्ली के लोगों के घरों में घुस सकते हैं, महिलाओं से रेप और हत्या कर सकते हैं।उन्होंने यह भी कहा था कि BJP की सरकार बनने पर शाहीन बाग को एक घंटे में खाली करा दिया जाएगा। चुनाव आयोग ने उन्हें 96 घंटे प्रचार करने से प्रतिबंधित किया था।
- 2020- केजरीवाल को आतंकवादी कहा: एक चुनावी भाषण और बाद में मीडिया बातचीत में उन्होंने तत्कालीन मुख्यमंत्री अरविंद केजरीवाल को आतंकवादी कहा। केजरीवाल की तुलना नटवरलाल और आतंकवादियों से की। चुनाव आयोग ने उन्हें 24 घंटे चुनाव प्रचार से प्रतिबंधित किया। यह शाहीन बाग मामले से अलग कार्रवाई थी।
- 2022- यमुना में केमिकल डालने पर अधिकारी से तीखी बहस: एक वीडियो में वे यमुना घाट पर दिल्ली जल बोर्ड के अधिकारी से बहस करते दिखे। अधिकारी ने बताया कि झाग हटाने वाला डिफोमर इस्तेमाल किया जा रहा है। इसके जवाब में वर्मा ने पूछा था कि अगर केमिकल सुरक्षित है तो उसे अधिकारी के सिर पर डाल दें।
- 2024- महिलाओं को ₹1,100 देने का मामला: प्रवेश वर्मा के घर के बाहर बड़ी संख्या में महिलाएं दिखाई दीं थीं। कुछ महिलाओं ने कैमरे पर कहा कि उन्हें ₹1,100 और एक कार्ड दिया गया और BJP को वोट देने के लिए कहा गया। वर्मा न

TMC विधायक कुणाल घोष पर लगातार दूसरे दिन हमला:बोले- रिवॉल्वर दिखाकर मुझे कार से खींचने की कोशिश की, शीशे तोड़े; 4 महीने में चौथा अटैक
- कॉपी लिंक
TMC विधायक कुणाल घोष ने रविवार को दावा किया कि कोलकाता में दिनदहाड़े उनकी कार पर फिर हमला किया गया। उन्होंने कहा कि बाइक सवार हथियारबंद लोगों ने कार को घेरा, शीशा तोड़ा और उन्हें बाहर खींचने की कोशिश की।
घोष के मुताबिक, हमलावरों के पास रिवॉल्वर थे। विधायक की सुरक्षा में तैनात जवानों को भी हथियार निकालने पड़े। घटना के बाद कुणाल घोष सीधे नारकेलडांगा पुलिस स्टेशन पहुंचे और शिकायत दर्ज कराई। उनकी क्षतिग्रस्त कार भी थाने के बाहर खड़ी दिखी।
घोष ने भाजपा पर आरोप लगाते हुए कहा कि उनकी हत्या की कोशिश की जा रही है। पिछले 4 महीने के दौरान घोष पर हमले का यह चौथा मामला है। एक दिन पहले हुगली के श्रीरामपुर में ममता बनर्जी की रैली में जाते समय भीड़ ने उनकी कार पर अंडे और पत्थर फेंके थे। पीछे का शीशा भी तोड़ दिया था।
दो दिनों में दो हमले: अंडे फेंके, कार के शीशे तोड़े
1. 27 सितंबर
2. 26 सितंबर
कुणाल घोष पर हमले के दो पुराने मामले
1. 15 जून: ममता के घर के बाहर अंडा फेंका
कोलकाता के कालीघाट में ममता बनर्जी के आवास के बाहर कुणाल घोष पर अंडा फेंका गया था। घटना उस समय हुई, जब घोष ममता से मुलाकात के बाद बाहर निकलकर मीडिया से बात कर रहे थे।
घोष ने शिकायत भी दर्ज कराई थी। इसके बाद पुलिस ने चंदन सिंह और रवि कोयल को गिरफ्तार किया था। दोनों को बाद में जमानत मिल गई थी।
2. 12 अगस्त: घर और पार्टी ऑफिस में तोड़फोड़
कोलकाता के गरपार इलाके में घोष के घर, क्लब और पार्टी ऑफिस में तोड़फोड़ का आरोप लगा था। उस समय घोष घर पर मौजूद नहीं थे। उन्होंने दावा किया था कि बाहर से लोगों को बुलाकर उन्हें निशाना बनाया गया।
घोष के मुताबिक, हमलावरों ने घर के पास पहुंचने की कोशिश की और बाद में पार्टी ऑफिस में तोड़फोड़ की। कुछ लोगों ने ऑफिस के बाहर लगे ममता बनर्जी और कुणाल घोष के पोस्टर और बैनर फाड़ दिए थे।
बंगाल चुनाव में हार के बाद ममता पर 3 बार हमला
- 8 जुलाई: कोलकाता में TMC की रैली के दौरान ममता बनर्जी के कार्यक्रम में अंडे फेंके गए और ‘चोर-चोर’ के नारे लगाए गए थे। यह रैली बारुईपुर रेप-मर्डर मामले के विरोध में निकाली गई थी।
- 9 अगस्त: नॉर्थ 24 परगना के हालीशहर में ममता बनर्जी की कार को प्रदर्शनकारियों ने घेर लिया था। इस दौरान कार पर कीचड़, चप्पल और पत्थर फेंकने का आरोप लगा। प्रदर्शनकारियों ने ‘चोर-चोर’ के नारे भी लगाए। ममता ने आरोप लगाया था कि उनकी कार पर ईंट-पत्थर फेंके गए और उनकी जान को खतरा हो सकता था।
- 11 अगस्त: कोलकाता के श्यामबाजार में नेताजी सुभाष चंद्र बोस को लेकर आयोजित TMC कार्यक्रम के दौरान भी ममता बनर्जी के खिलाफ ‘चोर-चोर’ के नारे लगाए गए थे।
5 महीने में 25 से ज्यादा TMC नेताओं पर हमले
पश्चिम बंगाल में 4 मई को विधानसभा चुनाव के नतीजे आए थे। 15 साल बाद TMC सत्ता से बाहर हो गई। वहीं पहली बार भाजपा की सरकार बनी। चुनाव के बाद पिछले 5 महीनों में 25 से ज्यादा TMC नेताओं और कार्यकर्ताओं पर अंडे फेंकने या हमले की घटनाएं सामने आई हैं। इनमें TMC सांसद अभिषेक बनर्जी और महुआ मोइत्रा जैसे बड़े नाम भी शामिल हैं।
- 28 मई को नॉर्थ 24 परगना जिले में TMC सांसद सौगत रॉय की कार पर अंडे फेंके गए और ‘चोर-चोर’ के नारे लगे।
- 30 मई को सोनारपुर में ममता के भतीजे और TMC सांसद अभिषेक बनर्जी पर अंडे, पत्थर और जूते फेंके गए। सुरक्षाकर्मियों को उन्हें पुलिस हेलमेट पहनाकर वहां से निकालना पड़ा।
- 6 जून को मदन मित्रा के काफिले पर अंडे फेंके गए। वहीं 16 जून को युवा नेता सौमित्र बनर्जी और 18 जून को पूर्व मंत्री उदयन गुहा पर भी अंडे और जूते फेंकने की घटनाएं सामने आईं।
- 1 जुलाई को कृष्णनगर में TMC सांसद महुआ मोइत्रा पर अंडे, सब्जियां और पत्थर फेंके गए।
सुरक्षा घेरे के बावजूद नेताओं तक कैसे पहुंच रहे हमलावर
नेताओं की सुरक्षा उनके पद से नहीं, खतरे के हिसाब से तय होती है। खतरे के मुताबिक X, Y, Y+, Z और Z+ सुरक्षा दी जाती है। इसकी जिम्मेदारी मुख्य रूप से राज्य पुलिस की होती है। ममता बनर्जी को Z+ सुरक्षा मिली है।
कुणाल घोष जैसे TMC नेताओं ने सवाल उठाया है कि ममता बनर्जी के Z+ सुरक्षा वाले आवास के पास अंडा कैसे फेंका गया? उनका कहना है कि इतनी कड़ी सुरक्षा वाली जगह पर ऐसी घटना सुरक्षा व्यवस्था पर सवाल खड़े करती है।
लेकिन दूसरे TMC नेताओं की सुरक्षा में हाल के महीनों में बदलाव हुआ है। मई 2026 में अभिषेक बनर्जी की सुरक्षा Z+ से घटाकर Z कर दी गई और उनके घर-दफ्तर के बाहर अत

छात्रा की मौत, पिता बोले- गैंगरेप के बाद मारा:गुवाहाटी में ब्वॉयफ्रेंड संग होमस्टे में रुकी थी, फोन पर मां से कहा था- मुझे मार डालेंगे

असम के गुवाहाटी में एक होमस्टे में मृत पाई गई 22 साल की छात्रा के परिवार ने आरोप लगाया है कि गैंगरेप के बाद उसकी हत्या की गई।
छात्रा के पिता ने रविवार सुबह मीडिया को बताया कि उन्होंने बेटी के शरीर पर जख्म के कई निशान देखे। उन्हें कहा कि हत्या से पहले उसके साथ गैंगरेप किया गया था।
छात्रा के पिता ने आगे बताया कि आधी रात को बेटी का कॉल आया था। वह सिर्फ इतना ही कह सकी- वो मुझे मार डालेंगे। इसके बाद उसका फोन स्विच ऑफ हो गया था। आशंका है कि उससे फोन छीन लिया गया होगा।
घटना के बाद पुलिस ने उसके साथ ठहरे 26 वर्षीय बॉयफ्रेंड आसिफ अली को गिरफ्तार कर लिया है। हालांकि, आसिफ का दावा है कि छात्रा ने आत्महत्या की है। लेकिन, पुलिस को प्राथमिक जांच में यह हत्या का मामला लग रहा है।
केयरटेकर ने सुनी थी चिल्लाने की आवाजें
आजरा इलाके में स्थित होमस्टे के केयरटेकर बिपुल बाइलुंग ने बताया कि दोनों रूम नंबर-10 में ठहरे हुए थे। दोनों ने रात को करीब साढ़े 9 बजे खाने का ऑर्डर दिया था। इसके बाद रात को करीब ढाई बजे किसी मर्द के चिल्लाने की आवाज सुनी था, जो कह रहा था- उठो, उठो।
बाइलुंग ने कहा- जब हम आवाज की दिशा में गए, तो देखा कि रूम नंबर-10 में लड़की फर्श पर पड़ी हुई थी और लड़का उसकी बॉडी पकड़े हुए था। बाइलुंग ने आगे बताया कि ये दोनों अक्सर इसी होमस्टे में ठहरते थे और शुक्रवार की रात भी उन्होंने यहां कमरा बुक किया था।
बाइलुंग ने कहा- हमने पुलिस को खबर दी। इसके बाद लड़की को बेहोशी की हालत में अस्पताल ले गए, जहां डॉक्टरों ने उसे मृत घोषित कर दिया।
एक महीने में 5वीं बार होमस्टे में आए थे: डीसीपी
गुवाहाटी पुलिस के डीसीपी (वेस्ट) बोलिन देवरी ने कहा- आसिफ का कहना है कि छात्रा ने छत के पंखे से फांसी लगाई थी और उसने उसे नीचे उतारा था। लेकिन पुलिस को उसके दावे पर शक है। डीसीपी ने कहा है कि पुलिस मामले की बारीकी से जांच कर रही है।
उन्होंने आगे कहा- जांच के दौरान हमें मालूम हुआ है कि दोनों इस महीने पांचवीं पर होमस्टे में ठहरने आए थे। जांच में यह भी पता चला है कि दोनों से ही उनके डॉक्यूमेंट्स नहीं लिए गए थे। होमस्टे के मालिक से पूछताछ कर ली गई है। होमस्टे के खिलाफ भी कार्रवाई की जाएगी।
लव जिहाद का आरोप, इलाके में तनाव
मृतका हिंदू समुदाय से थी और गिरफ्तार आरोपी मुस्लिम है, जिसके चलते घटना के बाद इलाके में तनाव फैल गया। शनिवार को कुछ दक्षिणपंथी संगठनों ने लव जिहाद का आरोप लगाते हुए विरोध प्रदर्शन किया और निष्पक्ष जांच की मांग की।
मौके पर पहुंची पुलिस ने प्रदर्शनकारियों को समझा-बुझाकर स्थिति को नियंत्रित किया और यातायात बहाल कराया। पुलिस फिलहाल पोस्टमॉर्टम रिपोर्ट और कॉल डिटेल रिकॉर्ड्स के आधार पर मामले की गहराई से जांच कर रही है।

items.title: Vijay govt revokes RTI exemption for law and order department after backlash
items.summary: Vijay govt revokes RTI exemption for law and order department after backlash
items.body_text:
Vijay govt revokes RTI exemption for law and order department after backlash
The Tamil Nadu government withdrew an order exempting the Public (Law and Order) Department from the RTI Act hours after the move drew a backlash from parties, including its ally, CPI(M).
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay’s government on Sunday revoked its order exempting the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act, hours after the move triggered criticism from the Opposition and CPM, an ally of the ruling TVK.
The Human Resources Management Department issued a fresh order, saying the exemption measure issued on September 21 under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act, “stood revoked”. The earlier order had classified the Public (Law and Order) Department as an intelligence and security organisation, bringing it under the RTI exemption.
The department handles matters including communal and caste clashes, political agitations, preventive detention, custodial deaths and allegations of police torture. Under Section 24 of the RTI Act, intelligence and security organisations specified by the government can be exempted from the law, subject to limited exceptions, including information relating to corruption and human rights violations.
Education Minister Raj Mohan said he would study the matter and assured that there would be no hurdle to freedom of expression, while stressing that a 'Lakshman Rekha' (red line) also had to be considered.
"Let me study it (the amendment) and there will not be any hurdle to freedom of expression. The 'Lakshman Rekha' of freedom of expression must also be considered. For one party’s sake, data should not be deliberately manipulated," Mohan said.
CPM, DMK SLAM TVK OVER RTI EXEMPTION MOVE
The now-revoked RTI exemption drew stinging responses from the Opposition, with CPI(M) MP S Venkatesan alleging that it would shield law-and-order matters from public scrutiny, while DMK spokesperson Saravanan accused the government of seeking to prevent disclosure of crime figures.
"The Right to Information Act exempts only public sector law and order matters from its purview. Government officials are ordering surveillance of leftist organisations. Custodial deaths are occurring. The education department has been ordered to suppress student protests," Venkatesan tweeted.
"The police are entering college campuses and arresting students. Struggles for legitimate rights are being suppressed through violence. In this context, exempting law and order matters from the Right to Information Act is deserving of severe condemnation. This is an overt attempt to turn Tamil Nadu into a 'police state'. The government must immediately withdraw this order," he said.
Saravanan alleged that the move was aimed at preventing scrutiny of crime figures in the state.
"The only reason this draconian amendment in the RTI has come is to ensure that we do not ask for the number of crimes that have taken place in Tamil Nadu. As the LOP @Udhaystalin says, 500 murders have so far taken place after TVK assumed office," he said.
To prevent the actual numbers coming out, this amendment bars law and order from the purview of RTI. We will fight this," he added.
Following Sunday's notification, the September 21 order has been withdrawn and the RTI exemption for the Public (Law and Order) Department no longer applies.

items.title: Video: Delhi minister Parvesh Verma slaps man filming him during road inspection
items.summary: Video Delhi minister Parvesh Verma slaps man filming him during road inspection
items.body_text:
Video: Delhi minister Parvesh Verma slaps man filming him during road inspection
The man, identified as Sahib Singh, was recording the exchange when Verma pulled down his phone and slapped him. Verma later defended his reaction, saying an AAP worker had abused his family, while Singh accused the minister of losing his temper.
Delhi Public Works Department (PWD) Minister Parvesh Verma slapped a young man who was recording a road inspection in west Delhi's Tilak Nagar on Sunday, with the incident caught on camera. The confrontation came after Verma and AAP MLA Jarnail Singh clashed over the quality of road construction in the area.
The video shows Verma pulling down the man's mobile phone with his left hand before slapping him across the face with his right. The man, identified as Sahib Singh, then appears to confront the minister, before a security guard steps between the two as a crowd gathers around them.
Verma later posted a video on X giving his account of the incident, saying, "Aaj ki ghatna ke peeche ki poori sacchai suniye...lekin jo hua woh nahi hona chahiye tha" (Listen to the complete truth behind today's incident...but what happened should not have happened). Singh, an aide of Jarnail Singh, was recording the exchange between the minister and the AAP MLA.
ROAD INSPECTION TURNS INTO HEATED EXCHANGE
The incident unfolded during Verma's inspection of a road in the Tilak Nagar Assembly constituency. The minister and Jarnail Singh were seen arguing over the quality of the road and trading accusations over its construction.
At one point, Jarnail Singh pulled at the newly paved road with his hand, lifting large chunks of the surface with apparent ease. "Ye lo, mantri ji aap humse poocho, bura manne ki baat nahi hai isme. Ye BJP ki Sarkar mein ho raha hai kaam. Hamari video delete karwa rahe ho (Here, Minister, you can ask us. There is nothing to feel bad about. This work is being carried out under the BJP government. You are getting our videos deleted)," the AAP MLA said, holding up pieces of the road.
He then challenged Verma, saying, "Aapne jo sadak boli woh ukhad ke dikha di, ab batao (You challenged me to tear up the road, and I have shown you by uprooting it. Now tell me)."
Verma, who had his arm around the AAP MLA at the time, told him, "Galat nahi bolna (Don't say anything wrong)."
When Singh asked what he had said wrong, the minister replied, "Bilkul galat bola. Aapne 15 saal mein sadak nahi banayi, ab hum bana rahe hain (That is completely wrong. You did not build the road in 15 years; now we are building it)."
Singh hit back, saying, "Aise mat banao na, ye toh 15 ghante nahi chalegi (Don't build it like this. It won't even last 15 hours)."
At this point, Verma turned around and started walking away. As Singh followed him holding the chunks of road, Sahib Singh, his personal assistant, continued recording the exchange. Verma then turned towards Singh and slapped him while he was filming.
MINISTER SLAPS MAN FILMING EXCHANGE
Verma then began walking away from the spot. Singh followed him while holding chunks of the road, as Sahib Singh continued recording the exchange on his mobile phone.
The video shows Verma turning towards Singh's aide, pulling down his phone and slapping him. A voice can be heard saying, "Oye maar kaise raha hai (How dare you hit me)?"
Another person says, "Are maar diya thappad, bhai. Bhai, thappad mar diya ji. Ye lo ji, video banate hue thappad mar diya."
Another voice from the crowd says, "Aam aadmi ko koi thappad nahi maar sakta."
The video then shows the young man getting into a brief physical confrontation with the minister before a security guard intervenes and separates them.
VICTIM FILES POLICE COMPLAINT
Speaking to news agency ANI, Sahib Singh said he was live-streaming the conversation between Jarnail Singh and Verma when the minister intervened.

items.title: Guwahati student death: Father's gang-rape claim, 2 am call and five homestay visits under probe
items.summary: Gauhati University student Nimisha called her mother at 2 AM saying she was beaten and injured. Hours later, she was found dead at a homestay. Father alleges gang rape; companion claims suicide. What really happened?
items.body_text:
Image Credit: X, AI. Nimisha and Ashiq.
A phone call at around 2 am is now a key part of the investigation into the death of 22-year-old Gauhati University student Nimisha Thakuria. Her father says she called her mother, saying she had been beaten and was injured. The family could not reach her again. Within hours, Nimisha was taken from a homestay on the outskirts of Guwahati to hospital, where she was declared dead.
Police have detained 26-year-old Ashiq Ali, who was staying with Nimisha at the homestay in the Dharapur-Garal area. Ali has told investigators that she died by suicide. Nimisha's father has rejected that account and alleged that his daughter was gang-raped and murdered.
According to her father, Deep Thakuria, Nimisha left home at around 5 pm on Friday after saying she was going out to eat with friends. Later that night, she told her mother that she would stay at the Gauhati University hostel with friends because it was getting late.
Her family had no reason at that stage to believe she was at a homestay, her father said.
Then came the call at around 2 am.
"Ma, they have beaten me. They punched me in the chest and assaulted me. I am injured," Nimisha allegedly told her mother, according to her father.
In another statement describing the same call, Thakuria said his daughter told her mother that "they were hitting me and I cannot breathe." The connection was then lost. Her parents repeatedly called her phone but could not reach her.
The family went to Azara police station and sought help. Police later received information about a young woman who had been taken to Garal Primary Health Centre in a critical condition. She was Nimisha.
She was referred to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival.
After seeing his daughter's body, Thakuria alleged that she had been assaulted before her death. He claimed there were marks on her body and also alleged that she had been tied with ropes.
"It was a gang rape case because her body has marks. She was gang-raped before she was killed," he told reporters.
The father's allegation has not been established by police. The post-mortem findings have not been publicly released, and investigators have not announced that sexual assault has been confirmed.
For police, the medical findings and forensic evidence from the homestay will be important in establishing what happened that night.
Ali has told investigators that Nimisha hanged herself. Police are checking that account against the medical evidence, witness statements and material collected from the room.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (West) Balin Deuri said, "Whether it is true or a lie, it would come out during the investigation."
Police have questioned the homestay owner, caretakers and other employees. CID and forensic teams have also examined the room and collected evidence.
The account given by the homestay staff has added another part to the night's timeline.
Employee Bipul Bailung said Nimisha and Ali were staying in Room 10 and had ordered food at around 9.30 pm. Several hours later, at around 2.30 am to 3 am, staff heard shouting followed by crying in a male voice.
"Three of us went to their room and found the girl lying on the floor, with the boy holding her in his hands and crying," Bailung said.
That timing is close to the call Nimisha's father says she made to her mother. Police are now examining the statements as they piece together what happened inside the homestay during those hours.
The investigation has also turned to the way the homestay handled its guests.
Police said Nimisha and Ali had visited the property about five times in the past month. Yet the homestay had not collected mandatory identification documents from them.
The property has since been sealed. Police are examining its records and have questioned the owner over the alleged failure to carry out guest verification.

items.title: PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti calls for Jantar Mantar protest on voter rolls
items.summary: PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti has urged "secular-minded" Indians to join protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on September 29 over alleged voter deletions and demolition of religious sites.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti.
PDP president Mehbooba Mufti has asked "secular-minded" Indians to join a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on September 29, where a newly formed national committee plans to take up alleged voter deletions and demolition of religious sites. The former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister said the gathering would run from 2 pm to 5 pm.
The demonstration has been called by the Monitoring Committee for Indian Muslims, also known as the National Monitoring Committee. Mufti, who is a member of the panel, released a video message on Saturday asking people outside the Muslim community to take part.
"You know that today in our country, mosques, shrines, and churches are being demolished with great ruthlessness. Apart from this, in the voter lists that are being prepared, the names of opposition supporters, secular-minded people, and especially Muslims, are being removed," she said.
"I appeal to all secular-minded people to participate in this and help us protect this country's democracy, this country's brotherhood, and the Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb of this nation."
In a separate post, Mufti wrote: "An appeal to every Indian who cherishes the democratic and secular values that bind our diverse nation together. Let us come together and raise our voices for the India we believe in. Join us at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on 29 September, from 2–5 pm."
Mufti's remarks come during the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, of electoral rolls. The exercise was extended to 16 states and three Union Territories under Phase III in May. The Election Commission said its objective was to ensure that no eligible citizen was excluded and no ineligible person was included.
Delhi has become one of the main centres of attention during the exercise. More than 31 lakh electors received notices seeking verification after their records were flagged for issues such as mismatches or difficulties linking them with earlier electoral records. Those receiving notices have included External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, CBI Director Praveen Sood and other serving and retired officials.
The Election Commission has said receiving such a notice does not mean a person's name has automatically been deleted or that the voter has been found ineligible. Electors can submit documents and seek verification of their entries.
The 51-member National Monitoring Committee was announced earlier this month by Indian Muslims for Civil Rights. It followed a July 24 meeting of Muslim leaders and intellectuals at the Constitution Club of India in New Delhi.
The panel includes National Conference president Farooq Abdullah, Mufti, former Union minister Salman Khurshid, former Delhi lieutenant governor Najeeb Jung, former judges, lawyers, MPs, religious scholars and civil society members. Organisers have said the committee will use constitutional, legal and political channels to take up matters concerning civil rights, religious freedom and political representation.
The September 29 gathering is the committee's latest public action. Mufti has presented the demonstration as open to Indians across communities, linking her appeal to democracy, communal brotherhood and the country's Ganga-Jamuni cultural tradition.

items.title: Instagram influencer flaunts gold & cash in reels - Loses Rs 1 crore in burglary
items.summary: An influencer's home in Tamil Nadu was burgled while her family was shopping, with gold, diamond jewellery and cash worth about Rs 1 crore stolen. Police suspect the thieves tracked her Instagram Reels before striking.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Instagram/@madhumithaaaaaaa_3154284. Kanyakumari influencer loses Rs 1 crore in robbery.
A social media influencer from Tamil Nadu lost valuables worth nearly Rs 1 crore in a burglary at her residence. Police suspect the thieves may have monitored Madhumitha's social media posts before targeting the house on Thursday night, when she and her family had gone out shopping.
Madhumitha, a YouTube and Instagram influencer, lives with her businessman husband Vinoth Kumar and their child at Thamathukonam near Nagercoil.
According to a Times of India report, Madhumitha regularly posted glimpses of the family's valuables and purchases online. Some videos showed gold jewellery kept at home, while another showed bundles of currency spread across a mattress. She had also posted a video showing money being showered on her child.
Police are now examining whether those posts gave the burglars an idea of the valuables kept inside the house.
More significantly for the investigation, some of the Reels allegedly revealed the family's movements.
"She had also uploaded videos saying the family bought gold every month and posted updates about where they went to purchase jewellery. Other reels routinely disclosed where the family was travelling and the purpose of their outings," an investigating officer told TOI.
Investigators suspect someone could have followed those updates and waited for an opportunity to enter the house when the family was away. Police have not yet established that the burglars definitely used Instagram to plan the break-in.
The burglary took place on Thursday evening after Madhumitha, Vinoth Kumar and their child left home to shop for clothes.
When the family returned later that night, Vinoth Kumar found that the bedroom wooden cabinet/wardrobe had been forced open. Gold, diamond jewellery and cash stored inside were missing.
According to the report, the burglars took 120 sovereigns of gold ornaments, diamond jewellery and Rs 50,000 in cash. The total value of the stolen property has been estimated at nearly Rs 1 crore.
The intruders are believed to have entered from the rear of the house. Police found that a door lock had been cut open with a cutting machine.
After gaining entry, the burglars allegedly went to the bedroom, broke open the wooden cabinet/wardrobe and fled with the valuables.
The manner of the break-in and its timing are being examined as police try to determine whether the house had been under surveillance before the family left.
Kanyakumari Superintendent of Police Anshul Nagar visited the house after the burglary was reported, while police formed five special teams to identify and trace the suspects.
"Kanyakumari SP (Anshul Nagar) visited the crime scene and five special teams have been formed to track the suspects," inspector Jayalakshmi told TOI.
Investigators are examining evidence from the house and Madhumitha's social media posts as they reconstruct the events leading up to the burglary.
No arrest had been reported in the TOI account published on September 25.
“She had also uploaded videos saying the family bought gold every month and posted updates about where they went to purchase jewellery. Other reels routinely disclosed where the family was travelling and the purpose of their outings,” an investigating officer told TOI.

items.title: Delhi High Court sends Muslim husband to jail for impregnating 16-year-old wife, says secular POCSO is above communal personal laws
items.summary: The Delhi High Court The court examined the legal scheme under the BNS and the POCSO Act and noted that both laws penalised sexual intercourse with a woman under 18 years of age.
items.body_text:
Before moving on to the High Court’s observations on the point of law, let’s take a look at the brief facts of the case.
Brief background of the case
The case concerns a Muslim couple who married on December 20, 2024. At the time of the marriage, the wife was 16 years and 3 months old, and the husband was about 28 years of age. In May 2026, when the wife was about 8 months pregnant, she visited a government hospital. The hospital authorities noticed that she was a minor and informed the police.
The police verified the minor wife’s age from her school certificate and proceeded to register an FIR against her husband under Section 64(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 6 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). The wife said that the marriage was performed with her consent and was also consummated with her consent.
In her statement before the Special Judge, she maintained that she was under no compulsion to marry her husband or have sexual intercourse with him. The wife subsequently gave birth to a stillborn child on June 6, 2026. The child was buried but later exhumed with the permission of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate for DNA profiling and collection of evidence.
The present petition sought the quashing of the FIR filed against the husband, and action against police officers, concerning allegations of false implication and harassment. The petition has relied on Muslim personal law to claim immunity for the husband from penal action for having sexual intercourse with his minor wife.
What the Muslim husband told the High Court
Citing Muslim personal law, the Muslim husband argued that his wife had attained puberty before their Nikah, as required under the personal law. As per Muslim personal law, puberty is presumed if the wife has completed 15 years of age at the time of Nikah. The petitioner argued that it was a valid marriage under Muslim personal law and therefore, subsequent cohabitation or sexual intercourse is also valid and cannot attract criminal liability.
Legal question before the High Court
The task before the High Court was to decide on the point of convergence of Muslim personal law and the criminal law meant to protect minors against sexual abuse. The High Court divided the legal issues in the case into two parts: first, the legal character and consequences of a Nikah performed with a Muslim minor girl who has attained puberty; and second, whether a Nikah excludes sexual intercourse with a minor wife from the ambit of the BNS and the POCSO Act. The court refused to decide the question relating to the validity of the Nikah and limited the scope of its examination to the second issue.
The question, precisely, before the High Court was “whether consent and the asserted validity of the marriage can displace that protective framework where the law itself fixes eighteen as the age below which consent to sexual activity has no legal efficacy”. In other words, the High Court examined whether a Nikah, even if valid, can grant a Muslim husband, who had sexual intercourse with his minor wife, immunity from the legal provisions that treat sexual intercourse with minors as an offence.
Observations of the High Court
The High Court drew the distinction between the legal status of a relationship and the criminal character of an act committed within the relationship. The court said that a valid marriage cannot grant immunity from criminal liability.
A valid marriage does not immunise conduct criminalised under a secular statute
“…a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, by reason of that status alone, confer immunity from POCSO or the BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below eighteen at the relevant time. Any other view would create, through judicial decision, an exception which Parliament has expressly excluded,” the High Court observed. items.title: Bombay HC imposes a total ban on firecrackers and loud music during festivities in Maharashtra: Read what the court said
items.summary: The court adopted a strict stance and pulled up the authorities for insufficient implementation of the existing laws.
items.body_text:
The Bombay High Court recently took suo motu cognisance of noise and environmental pollution being caused by various factors, including the bursting of firecrackers and the use of amplified music systems during festivals in public places. A Bench of Justices G. S. Kulkarni and Dr Neela Gokhale, on September 22, 2026, examined the factors contributing to the pollution and issued directions to the concerned authorities to curb it.
Celebrations need to be more “dignified” and “civilised”: HC.
The High Court expressed concern over the noise and air pollution caused by the use of firecrackers and loud music systems during festivities in public places. “We are also seriously concerned with the level of air pollution that would be generated by the bursting of firecrackers on public streets…We are also concerned with the potential hazards caused by the bursting of
firecrackers, including firecrackers generating noise pollution in excess of the prescribed decibel limits,” the court said.
The High Court observed that the manner of celebrating festivals needs to change and become more “dignified” and “civilised”, keeping in mind the requirements of contemporary times. The Court said that the problem is magnified in large cities with huge populations, where the majority of people become silent sufferers of the brazen violations.
“It is high time that in large cities having dense population like Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Nashik, where majority of the citizens are made to silently suffer such brazen violations, a regime of total restraint on the playing of loud music by use of high watt speakers, sound system, loud speakers, dhol tashas, use of cylinders etc. needs to be completely banned, and a more dignified and civilised way of having these processions and celebrations is the imminent requirement of the contemporary times,” the court stated.
Rules have remained as mere paper provisions: HC.
The court adopted a strict stance and pulled up the authorities for insufficient implementation of the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 and the failure to act on violations under the rules. “…although robust provisions are available in law to control and regulate the levels of noise pollution being generated by the processions and venues in the festivities, mostly they have remained to be paper provisions, much less being effectively implemented in letter and spirit,” the High Court observed.
The court said that due to the laxity displayed by the concerned authorities in implementing the laws, the ordinary citizens are left to suffer the effects of noise and environmental pollution. “This is the sad ground reality from which the authorities at the helm of affairs cannot run away. The casualties in the whole process are the innocent persons who are subjected to such noise pollution, bringing about serious health hazards…” the court noted.
The High Court said that the authorities need to become proactive and take preventive measures to curb the problem instead of swinging into action only after a complaint is filed. “…there is no warrant in having a mechanism that only after complaints of violations and breaches are made, and only then the official machinery would step in to set into motion to impose petty penalties. This would be a situation when enormous damage has already been caused…” the court remarked.
