items.title: LASTMA impounds 84 vehicles over traffic offences
items.summary: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, has impounded 84 commercial and private vehicles for various traffic offences during a comprehensive enforcement operation across identified traffic flashpoints in the state. The exercise, conducted at the weekend around Idumota, Iddo, Ijora-Olopa, Costain and Onipanu, was aimed at restoring order and ensuring […] The post LASTMA impounds 84 vehicles over traffic offences appeared first on Vanguard News.
items.body_text:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
LAGOS — The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, has impounded 84 commercial and private vehicles for various traffic offences during a comprehensive enforcement operation across identified traffic flashpoints in the state.
The exercise, conducted at the weekend around Idumota, Iddo, Ijora-Olopa, Costain and Onipanu, was aimed at restoring order and ensuring compliance with traffic regulations, particularly along corridors where persistent violations by motorists and commercial bus operators have affected the free flow of traffic.
LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, said the agency was particularly concerned about the practice of commercial buses reversing against traffic along the one-way stretch from Iddo to Idumota through Cater Bridge.
According to him, the practice posed serious risks to motorists, commuters and pedestrians using the corridor.
“Motorists and other legitimate road users approaching the bridge may have little or no forewarning that a commercial vehicle is unlawfully reversing against the prescribed direction of traffic, thereby creating an extremely hazardous situation with the potential to precipitate devastating collisions, injuries and fatalities,” he said.
Miscreants attack officers
The enforcement operation, however, reportedly met resistance from some individuals, with LASTMA personnel assaulted and injured while carrying out their duties.
Bakare-Oki confirmed that some alleged miscreants who attacked officers and damaged the agency’s operational vehicles during the exercise were apprehended.
He said the enforcement had become necessary to curb what he described as a growing culture of impunity among some road users and restore discipline along critical traffic corridors.
The LASTMA boss said the agency had repeatedly cautioned transport operators, commercial bus drivers and other road users against using under-bridge spaces, road setbacks and other unauthorised locations as illegal garages.
“We have repeatedly cautioned transport operators, commercial bus drivers and other road users against occupying under-bridge spaces, road setbacks and unauthorised locations as illegal garages as such practices constitute serious impediments to effective traffic management and pose considerable risks to public safety,” he said.
Bakare-Oki said LASTMA would sustain its enforcement campaign to secure compliance with traffic regulations, deter hazardous driving practices and protect the lives and property of motorists, commuters, pedestrians and other road users.
He warned that no individual or group would be allowed to appropriate public roads, bridges or under-bridge spaces for illegal loading, parking, vehicle repairs or garage operations.
He consequently urged commercial bus operators, motorists, transport unions and other stakeholders to desist from one-way driving, dangerous reversing, illegal parking, indiscriminate loading and the occupation of unauthorised garages or under-bridge locations.
He warned that further violations would attract appropriate enforcement measures in accordance with extant Lagos State traffic laws.
The LASTMA boss also urged members of the public to remain vigilant and report dangerous driving, traffic obstructions, reckless motorists and other traffic-related offences through the agency’s toll-free short code, 3367, to enable prompt intervention and prevent avoidable incidents on the state’s road network.
items.normalised_title: lastma impounds 84 vehicles over traffic offences

items.title: NDC-UK leadership reaffirms commitment to party
items.summary: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The leadership of the United Kingdom Chapter of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, has reaffirmed its commitment to the growth and development of the party following a high-level meeting with its National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, in London. The NDC-UK Executive Committee paid a courtesy visit to Dickson at the […] The post NDC-UK leadership reaffirms commitment to party appeared first on Vanguard News.
items.body_text:
Dickson
By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — The leadership of the United Kingdom Chapter of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, has reaffirmed its commitment to the growth and development of the party following a high-level meeting with its National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, in London.
The NDC-UK Executive Committee paid a courtesy visit to Dickson at the London Park Lane Hilton Hotel on Saturday, where members of the chapter and representatives of the Nigerian community across Great Britain and Ireland interacted with the former Bayelsa State governor.
In a statement on Sunday by the Publicity Secretary of NDC-UK, Boniokoye Imegwu, the meeting provided an opportunity for Dickson to brief party members and supporters on developments within the party, its progress since its formation and preparations for the forthcoming general election.
Dickson was in London on his return to Nigeria from the Netherlands, where he had inaugurated the NDC Netherlands Chapter.
During the interaction, the NDC National Leader expressed confidence in the party’s leadership and presidential ticket.
He also urged institutions and officials responsible for conducting the elections to uphold integrity, fairness, responsibility and patriotism throughout the electoral process.
The NDC-UK Country Chairman, Princewill Urum, thanked Dickson for his leadership and reaffirmed the chapter’s commitment to advancing the objectives and programmes of the party.
Also present at the meeting was the leader of the Coalition for the Protection of Democracy, COPDEM, a Nigerian and global political network.
The COPDEM leader commended what he described as the direction and progress of the NDC, saying the organisation would deploy its available resources and personnel in support of initiatives aimed at promoting democratic participation and a credible electoral process in Nigeria.
Dickson also disclosed that he would return to the United Kingdom later this year with the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi; his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso; and other senior party officials for the formal launch of the NDC-UK Chapter.
The meeting ended on a convivial note, with participants expressing renewed commitment to the expansion of the NDC and its forthcoming electoral activities.

items.title: French loan cannot fund electioneering — Makinde’s aide
items.summary: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — The Oyo State Government has said the French Treasury Loan secured for its development programme cannot be diverted for electioneering or other purposes outside the scope for which it was approved. Special Adviser to Governor Seyi Makinde, Mrs Ronke Adedayo, who facilitated the sourcing and acquisition of the facility on […] The post French loan cannot fund electioneering — Makinde’s aide appeared first on Vanguard News.
items.body_text:
By Adeola Badru
IBADAN — The Oyo State Government has said the French Treasury Loan secured for its development programme cannot be diverted for electioneering or other purposes outside the scope for which it was approved.
Special Adviser to Governor Seyi Makinde, Mrs Ronke Adedayo, who facilitated the sourcing and acquisition of the facility on behalf of the state government, disclosed this while speaking with journalists at the weekend.
Adedayo said the facility was being implemented in line with the conditions under which it was approved by the French authorities, adding that its financing structure did not permit the state government to divert, reallocate or deploy the funds to projects outside the approved scope.
According to her, the loan operates under a ring-fenced disbursement arrangement, with each tranche tied to specific project milestones and subject to mandatory compliance requirements.
She added that the facility was also subject to compliance audits by relevant French authorities and independent monitors, as well as a restricted expenditure framework designed to ensure that the funds were used only for their approved purposes.
Adedayo said the safeguards prevented the state government from unilaterally changing the purpose of the facility.
She said: “Under these conditions, no government can unilaterally alter the use of the loan, nor can the funds be applied to any project outside the original scope approved by the French Treasury and AFD.
“Any deviation would immediately trigger international compliance violations and halt further disbursement. Those insinuating that the funds might be used for electioneering are merely exhibiting their ignorance.”
The governor’s aide maintained that the Makinde administration remained committed to transparency and compliance with international financing standards throughout the implementation of the facility.
“Just as Governor Seyi Makinde has said, the Oyo State Government remains committed to full transparency and adherence to all international financing standards.
“The French Treasury Loan will continue to be implemented strictly for its designated purpose, in line with global best practices and the development priorities of Oyo State,” she said.
Adedayo also explained why a facility obtained in 2020 was only being accessed in 2026, attributing the delay to the lengthy bureaucratic processes involved in securing the necessary approvals from the Federal Government.
She said the facility was secured on highly concessionary terms, including very low interest rates, which she described as favourable to the state.
The Special Adviser further disclosed that the financing arrangement included a significant French-content component involving the provision of equipment.
According to her, the component was fixed under the agreement and could neither be altered nor tampered with by the state government.
She reiterated that the loan would remain tied to the development programme for which it was approved, with its implementation continuing under the conditions and safeguards attached to the international financing arrangement.

items.title: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence
items.summary: The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province. “The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said. It added: “Pakistan categorically rejects the fabricated claims of involvement by its security forces or inte
items.body_text:
The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province.
“The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said.
It added: “Pakistan categorically rejects the fabricated claims of involvement by its security forces or intelligence agencies in any internal clashes in Nuristan or elsewhere in Afghanistan, including allegations of recruiting or training former Afghan security personnel or facilitating Daesh or any other terrorist group operating in Afghanistan.”
The information ministry’s statement came after Afghanistan’s defence ministry alleged that Pakistan-backed individuals had crossed the border and were involved in the reported violence.
The information ministry pointed out that “not a shred of evidence has been produced to substantiate Pakistan’s involvement; no identities, documents, communications, forensic evidence or independent verification”.
It further noted that an alleged video “being peddled on social media to support this false claim only shows a few unarmed individuals who are not even properly dressed or equipped were arrested in what seems to be a pre-planned video shoot by Afghan Taliban regime, well known for lies and fabricated claims”.
“Instead of externalising responsibility for its internal security challenges through fanciful allegations, the Afghan Taliban regime should take credible and verifiable action against terrorist organisations operating from its territory and fulfil its commitments that Afghan soil will not be used for terrorism against Pakistan or any other country.”
The statement further said it was “particularly ironic for the Afghan Taliban regime to accuse Pakistan of supporting terrorism while terrorist organisations operating from Afghanistan continue to pose a direct threat to Pakistan and regional security”.
The ministry highlighted that the presence and activities of “terrorist groups of all types inside Afghanistan are well documented”, including in successive reports of the United Nations and other neutral international organisations.
“Attempts to manufacture a Pakistani connection cannot obscure the reality that these terrorist groups continue to find sanctuary and [a] permissive environment for growth in Afghan territory,” it asserted.
“Such claims by this non-inclusive, non-representative Taliban regime are also reflective of lies to externalise internal dissent and oppression of women, children and minorities,” the ministry said.
Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.
According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afghan Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.
The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).
Pak-Afghan tensions
Ties between the two neighbours have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism. Meanwhile, September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed.

items.title: Newly inducted Hangor-class submarine conducts maiden live weapon firing in Arabian Sea: ISPR
items.summary: The navy’s first Hangor-class submarine successfully conducted its maiden live weapon firing in the Arabian Sea, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday. The Hangor-class submarine arrived at Karachi Port in June, underscoring the deepening strategic defence cooperation between Pakistan and China. Terming it a “major demonstration of operational readiness”, ISPR said the newly inducted PNS/M HANGOR accurately engaged a “designated long-range target with an anti-ship cruise missile”
items.body_text:
The navy’s first Hangor-class submarine successfully conducted its maiden live weapon firing in the Arabian Sea, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.
The Hangor-class submarine arrived at Karachi Port in June, underscoring the deepening strategic defence cooperation between Pakistan and China.
Terming it a “major demonstration of operational readiness”, ISPR said the newly inducted PNS/M HANGOR accurately engaged a “designated long-range target with an anti-ship cruise missile” during the weapon firing exercise.
Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf witnessed the firing, praising the submarine’s combat power and emphasising the “strategic importance of enhancing subsurface capabilities for credible maritime deterrence”.
“The milestone underscores the Pakistan Navy’s commitment to maintaining a modern, combat-ready force to safeguard national maritime frontiers and regional peace,” ISPR highlighted.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the Pakistan Navy and its leadership on the first live weapons firing by the newly inducted submarine, according to a statement issued by his office.
“The submarine successfully struck a long-range target with an anti-ship cruise missile, demonstrating the operational readiness, professional expertise and combat capability of Pakistan Navy’s submarine force,” the premier was quoted as saying.
PM Shehbaz reaffirmed the government’s commitment to ensuring the armed forces’ readiness to tackle national security challenges, the statement added. He also commended the Naval chief and the personnel involved in the induction and operationalisation of the submarine.
President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the navy on the successful firing, lauding the “operational readiness and enhancement” of naval defence capabilities, his office said in a post on X.
“Equipped with modern combat capabilities, the Pakistan Navy is playing a vital role in safeguarding national maritime boundaries and ensuring regional peace and security,” President Zardari was quoted as saying.
The statement added that President Zardari was a chief guest at the handover ceremony of the Hangor-class submarine on April 30.
The navy is set to induct a total of eight Hangor-class submarines.
The Hangor-class submarine is equipped with advanced combat systems, modern sensors, Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) technology and enhanced stealth features, which will significantly enhance the navy’s combat capability.
The name Hangor holds a significant place in Pakistan’s naval history, referring to the 1971 Pakistan-India war, during which then-PNS Hangor became the first submarine since World War II to sink a warship when it sank the Indian frigate INS Khukri.
The first of the new submarines was launched in China in April 2024, while the second, third and fourth were launched on March 15, Aug 15 and Dec 17 in 2025, respectively.
On April 21, the Pakistan Navy conducted a successful test of an indigenously developed Anti-Ship Weapon System — Taimoor, the military’s media wing said.
In the same month, the Pakistan Navy fired a locally developed anti-ship ballistic missile to engage targets at an extended range.
“In a resolute display of preparedness and precision-strike capability, Pakistan Navy successfully conducted a live weapon firing of an indigenously developed ship-launched anti-ship missile, accurately engaging its target with high speed at extended range,” the ISPR had said at the time.

items.summary: Heavy rain triggered floods and landslides across northern India and Nepal, killing at least 68 people over the past three days, disaster authorities said on Sunday. In India’s most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, 56 people have died over the past three days with more than 1,000 houses damaged, the relief commissioner’s office said in a statement. Neighbouring Nepal, already reeling under the catastrophic August 26 flood, was struck by a fresh wave of flooding and landslides that has killed 12
items.body_text:
Heavy rain triggered floods and landslides across northern India and Nepal, killing at least 68 people over the past three days, disaster authorities said on Sunday.
In India’s most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, 56 people have died over the past three days with more than 1,000 houses damaged, the relief commissioner’s office said in a statement.
Neighbouring Nepal, already reeling under the catastrophic August 26 flood, was struck by a fresh wave of flooding and landslides that has killed 12 people since Thursday.
“Since Thursday, 12 people have died in rain-related disasters like floods and landslides,” Shanti Mahat, spokesperson at Nepal’s disaster authority, told AFP, adding that seven more were missing.
Scientists have warned in recent years of an increase in extreme weather events across South Asia, linking them to rising temperatures and changing climate patterns.
The flooding in Nepal last month, triggered by a glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border, has killed more than 1,400 people and left thousands missing.
Uttar Pradesh, home to more than 240 million people, is frequently battered by rain and thunderstorms during the annual monsoon season from June to September.
The latest deaths were reported during a spell of “exceptionally heavy rain” after a “depression over the Bay of Bengal moved inland and intensified rainfall across the region”, it said.
The state recorded 66.5 millimetres of rain between Friday and Sunday, compared to the season average of 7.6mm, it added.
The heavy rain caused extensive damage to crops, with farmers raising concerns over sowing delays in the upcoming season.
In India’s eastern state of Odisha, over 70,000 people living in low-lying areas were evacuated after rivers swelled due to heavy downpours, NDTV news network reported.
The rains have damaged bridges and culverts, forcing officials to shut down Devkund, a popular tourist spot in the state.
Monsoon-related disasters are an annual occurrence across India after long summers when many parts of the country face water scarcity and drought.

items.summary: Calls for timely efforts to resolve issues.Urges sides to avoid deaths and financial losses.Says Pakistan is suffering multiple crises.LAHORE: PML-N leader Saad Rafique has urged the state and protesters to hold talks, saying timely efforts are needed to resolve issues and prevent...
items.body_text:
Published September 27, 2026
- Calls for timely efforts to resolve issues.
- Urges sides to avoid deaths and financial losses.
- Says Pakistan is suffering multiple crises.
LAHORE: PML-N leader Saad Rafique has urged the state and protesters to hold talks, saying timely efforts are needed to resolve issues and prevent further losses.
“Whenever there is an initiative, it is always the state that takes it. Take the initiative,” Rafique said on Sunday in a post on X, urging the government and protesters to rise above ego, stubbornness and factionalism.
“If there is an intention to resolve problems, a way will certainly be found,” he said.
Rafique warned both sides against viewing the confrontation as a contest, saying: “Remember, none of you will be the winner because everyone is losing.”
He also called for efforts to prevent loss of life and property, saying Pakistan was “groaning” under the pressure of inflation, unemployment, injustice and terrorism.
“If wounds are not treated in time, they turn into festering sores,” the PML-N leader said.
His remarks came after the PTI postponed its long march towards Islamabad by a week. Following the postponement, routes connecting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Islamabad began reopening.
Traffic on the GT Road at Khairabad in Attock was restored after four days, while the removal of obstacles from the Peshawar-Islamabad M-1 motorway was underway.
Sandbags, iron sheets and containers had been placed on the motorway to stop the PTI long march, while traffic at Punjab’s entry points in Taxila also returned to normal.
The Cpec route in Mianwali, however, remained closed, according to the information provided.
Despite the postponement of the September 27 march, the number of containers around Islamabad’s Red Zone increased.
A case was also registered over barriers being broken at Attock Bridge and thrown into the river, with 250 PTI workers nominated in the case. Several PTI workers were also detained, while authorities said action would be taken under the law over damage to state property.
The PTI had initially planned to hold its long march towards Islamabad on September 27, but KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi later announced that it had been postponed until October 4.
Afridi had also offered talks to the federal government, saying the issues could be resolved through mutual understanding.
Speaking to senior journalists in Peshawar, Afridi said: “If the federal government wants to resolve the issue within seven days, it should do so through mutual understanding.”
He questioned why the government would wait until the long march before holding talks, saying: “If negotiations have to be held after the long march, why not do them before?”
“We want the issue to be resolved,” the chief minister added.

items.title: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs called to appear at Australian AI probe
items.body_text:
OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs called to appear at Australian AI probe
- By Reuters -
- Sep 27, 2026
SYDNEY: The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic have been called to appear at an Australian Senate inquiry on AI, the head of the probe said on Sunday, days after the revelation that a rogue OpenAI bot had hacked the country’s health-system database.
The Medicare breach, condemned by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the US.
OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei have been sent written requests to appear at the inquiry, which is to hold public hearings in the capital Canberra on Thursday, said a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young of the Australian Greens party, who chairs the probe.
OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside business hours.
The OpenAI agent’s incursion on one of the country’s most used government agencies may prompt Albanese’s Labor government to toughen AI-specific laws it is readying for next year, adding pressure to Australia-US relations already tested by Canberra’s ban on social media for teens, tech policy experts say.
The Senate inquiry is examining the potential impacts of AI and data centres on Australian communities, industries, water and energy. It is one of several state and federal probes into AI.
“There are serious questions for Sam Altman to answer about the OpenAI hack of Australian government websites,” Hanson-Young said in a statement. Altman and Amodei “must front up, face the Senate’s questions and have an honest conversation about what effective, lasting regulation of this industry should look like”, she said.
Albanese, who revealed the June breach of Medicare on Thursday, called it “unacceptable”, saying he had voiced “extreme concern” to Altman.
OpenAI says it only learned of the breach — one of at least four of Australian government websites — in August. It says the incident was not intentional and did not compromise any private information.

items.title: Saudi authorities shift schools in Riyadh to remote learning for week
items.body_text:
Saudi authorities shift schools in Riyadh to remote learning for week
- By AFP -
- Sep 27, 2026
RIYADH: Parents across Riyadh received emails from schools on Sunday announcing a last-minute plan to shift to remote learning for a week, according to messages seen by AFP.
“We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week,” read two separate messages seen by AFP.
There was no official reason given but the move comes amid heightened tensions in the Gulf and attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen.
The announcement comes a day after the coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom.
The strikes were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war.
The United Nations Security Council earlier condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi fighters, noting that the strikes have wounded “civilians, including women and children”.

items.title: Two giant pandas sent by China arrive in US
items.body_text:
Two giant pandas sent by China arrive in US
- By AFP -
- Sep 27, 2026
Two giant pandas sent by China arrived in the United States on Sunday, Beijing’s state media said, after a leaders’ summit that was heavy on symbolism and light on major breakthroughs.
The pandas’ transfer had already been agreed but the departure was announced Thursday during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington.
The black-and-white mammals are immensely popular around the world, and China loans them out as part of a “panda diplomacy” programme to foster foreign ties.
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang departed from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport on a chartered flight at around 3:00 am (1900 GMT on Saturday), state news agency Xinhua reported.
After a 16-hour flight that crossed the international date line, the bears touched down in Atlanta, Georgia shortly before 7:00 am local time (1100 GMT on Sunday), Xinhua said later.
Steamed corn buns, bamboo shoots and carrots were prepared to keep the pandas nourished during their flight, Chinese state-run media the Global Times reported.
The Boeing 777 operated by FedEx was the top-tracked aircraft on aviation information platform FlightRadar24 as it neared Alaska, roughly halfway into its journey.
The pandas will be hosted by Zoo Atlanta for the next 10 years.
A farewell ceremony was held for the pair before their departure by the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding.
Experienced keepers were dispatched by the US side to accompany the duo on their flight, the Global Times reported.
In preparation for their arrival, Zoo Atlanta has renovated its panda facilities and assembled a team of animal caretakers.
It has also ensured a stable and long-term supply of bamboo, grown locally in Atlanta, which has a climate that is very similar to Chengdu.
Zoo Atlanta previously hosted pandas on loan from China for a quarter of a century starting in 1999, but it has not had any since 2024.
Both arrivals were born in 2020. Ping Ping, a male, is now six years old while Fu Shuang, a female, will turn six next month.
Pandas in captivity typically live for around 30 years.
Beijing has sent the furry creatures across the globe for decades as soft-power ambassadors of its diplomatic goodwill.
In 1972, China gifted a pair of pandas to Washington, following US president Richard Nixon’s historic visit to the Communist nation.
Beijing recalled two of its pandas from Japan early this year, following a diplomatic spat that began when Japan’s prime minister hinted that Tokyo could intervene militarily in the event of any attack on Taiwan.

items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US-led international coalition has officially halted financial aid to Iraqi Kurdistan’s Peshmerga forces following the expiration of a four-year agreement. The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and […] The post International coalition halts financial aid to Peshmerga appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
International coalition halts financial aid to Peshmerga
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US-led international coalition has officially halted financial aid to Iraqi Kurdistan’s Peshmerga forces following the expiration of a four-year agreement.
The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and the United States Department of Defense inked an agreement that extended from September 21, 2022, until September 21, 2026.
On Thursday, the troops received their final allowance for August and September 2026.
According to the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs, Bakhtiar Sadiq, the financial aid under the initial agreement was planned to steadily reduce by 25 percent each year until reaching a complete halt.
This cash halt aligns with the overall conclusion of the international coalition’s military operations in Iraq, with a full stoppage of combat and training responsibilities expected by September 30, 2026.
Additionally, the proposed US Counter-ISIS Train and Equip Fund (CTEF) plan for 2027 includes no support for the Peshmerga.
The international coalition has tied its financial assistance to necessary reforms and the unification of the Peshmerga forces, particularly the integration of politically separated units. Earlier in September, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) publicly announced that the unification process was complete.
To address the newly established funding imbalance, the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs has formally requested the federal government in Baghdad to adjust Peshmerga salaries to align them permanently with federal Iraqi military and security forces.

Iraq seeks US exemption to resume Iranian flights
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi government revealed on Saturday that it is holding discussions with the US administration to obtain an exemption for certain Iraqi airports from the ban on Iranian airline flights imposed under US sanctions, citing the disruption caused to traveling patients, students, and pilgrims.
According to the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the Iraqi government is engaged in direct talks with the US side to exempt specific Iraqi airports from these measures.
The exception would allow for the resumption of flights for humanitarian grounds, which include medical care, education, religious pilgrimages, and civilian interests.
Iranian airlines primarily handle the transport of Iranians traveling to Iraq in large numbers to visit the shrines of Shiite Imams, as well as Iraqis flying to Iran for religious pilgrimages, studies, or medical treatment.
Iraq joined several other nations in suspending Iranian flights to and from its territory after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that all Iranian airlines will cease operations as of September 23.
Under the new measures, any country or firm that provides services to Iranian aircraft is completely removed from the global US dollar system. The services include fueling airplanes, offering ground handling and landing services, and selling passenger tickets.

items.body_text:
Iraq unveils plan for data centers in Baghdad, Basra, and Mosul
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Communications unveiled an ambitious strategic blueprint on Saturday, September 26, 2026, to construct a distributed network of enterprise data centers across Baghdad, Basra, and Mosul, aiming to upgrade national digital infrastructure and localize hosting for global technology conglomerates.
In an exclusive statement granted to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the Director General of the General Company for Communications and Informatics, Ali Yassin, confirmed that establishing tier-standard data centers across multiple provinces stands among the ministry’s top executive priorities to accelerate digital transformation.
Yassin revealed that the capital city of Baghdad will host three dedicated data centers situated across prime connectivity hubs, specifically at the Al-Sinak telecommunications complex, the Al-Intisar facility, and the Al-Mamoun Telecommunications Tower compound adjacent to the ministry’s headquarters.
The geographical distribution within the capital ensures redundant network routing, continuous uptime, and high-speed fiber interconnection to support both federal e-governance platforms and commercial cloud services.
Beyond Baghdad, the national strategy targets key regional logistics and transit corridors, including a specialized facility planned in Basra Governorate in close proximity to the international submarine cable landing station, directly capitalizing on Iraq’s high-capacity maritime fiber-optic gateways.
Additionally, the ministry is preparing to establish another facility in Mosul to anchor cloud architecture across the northern provinces.
Yassin emphasized that these specialized data centers are purpose-built to attract major multinational technology companies, creating localized environments capable of hosting global content, accelerating low-latency data delivery, and reinforcing Iraq’s sovereign digital ecosystem.

Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty said on Saturday, September 26, 2026, that the Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology (E-JUST) remains a central part of educational cooperation between Egypt and Japan.

The Minister stated that the university has become one of the main areas of bilateral cooperation, helping train skilled professionals, transfer modern technology, and strengthen educational and scientific ties between the two countries.
Abdelatty affirmed that education is an important part of Egypt-Japan relations, pointing to cooperation between Cairo and Tokyo to establish more than 100 Japanese schools in Egypt.
He also thanked Japan for its support for educational cooperation and praised E-JUST for providing postgraduate scholarships to students from African countries.
The Minister congratulated the graduates, saying their knowledge and technological skills would contribute to Egypt’s development.
President of Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology Ahmed el Sabbagh said that E-JUST is working to prepare graduates for changes in technology, artificial intelligence and the knowledge economy.
He added that the university continues to develop its academic and research programs and expand cooperation with academic and industrial institutions in Egypt and Japan.
The ceremony was attended by Alexandria Governor Ayman Attia, Japanese Ambassador to Egypt Iwai Fumio and the ambassadors of Kenya and Malawi, along with university and education officials.

items.body_text:
The Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said that the textile and spinning sector is a key target of Egypt’s industrial strategy, given its strong potential to integrate into global supply chains, deepen local manufacturing and boost exports.
During a tour of the 6th of October City’s industrial zone, Hashem inspected two factories specialized in textiles, knitting, dyeing, printing and finishing, reviewing production operations and manufacturing stages.
He highlighted the sector’s competitive advantages, including its labor-intensive nature, relatively low energy consumption and availability of skilled workers, which he said could attract further investment and support production and exports.
At Naga Tex, the Minister reviewed a factory producing around 1.44 million meters of fabric annually, with 90 percent local components. The company exports about 60 percent of its output to Switzerland, Turkey, Germany, Brazil and Italy, generating around $2 million in exports.
He also inspected Misr al-Salam for knitting, dyeing, printing and finishing, which has an annual capacity of 5,000 tons of dyed and printed fabric, with 80 percent local components. The company exports 20 percent of its output to Turkey and Morocco, generating three million dollars in exports.
Hashem stressed the importance of raising local components and integrating production chains to enhance the competitiveness of Egyptian products and support the country’s export and industrialization targets.

items.body_text:
Ahmed al-Zaher, CEO of the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), said Egyptian talent is the key factor driving global technology companies to choose Egypt for expansion and international service centers.
Speaking at the ninth edition of DevOpsDays Cairo 2026, El Zaher said rapid advances in artificial intelligence, particularly Agentic AI, are reshaping software development and operations, requiring updated work methodologies, governance and security frameworks, and continued investment in specialized skills.
He highlighted ITIDA’s role, through its Software Engineering Competence Center (SECC), in developing Egyptian capabilities through specialized training, consulting, technical capacity building, and international certifications, enhancing the competitiveness of Egyptian engineers and companies in global markets.
El Zaher said global companies have repeatedly highlighted the quality of Egyptian talent in their meetings with ITIDA, citing a recent meeting with NVIDIA, which expressed appreciation for Egyptian developers and startup founders. NVIDIA’s programs include more than 200 Egyptian startups and around 46,000 programmers, he said.
He added that continued expansion by global companies in Egypt to serve international markets reflects growing confidence in Egyptian talent and strengthens the country’s position as a global technology and digital-services hub.
Held under the theme “Sustainable DevOps in the Agentic AI Era,” the conference brought together local and international experts to discuss AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity and the future of software development and operations. The ninth edition featured 66 speakers, including 13 international speakers from nine countries.
ITIDA has hosted DevOpsDays Cairo since 2018, making Cairo the only Arab city to host the conference, which is held in more than 60 cities worldwide.

                As diplomats and heads of states from around the world descend on New York this week to hold official and unofficial talks during the United Nations General Assembly, the already-long ledger of regional crises continues to grow.
In recent weeks the Houthis have taken key areas overlooking the crucial Bab al-Mandab Strait, triggering renewed fighting in Yemen. Meanwhile in Ethiopia, the long-simmering tensions in Tigray have boiled over, with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front seizing on Wednesday the restive northern state’s three airports and setting the stage for what could become another complex regional war in the Horn of Africa.
This is in addition to the continued war in Sudan, the threat of escalation in Iran, the dire oil crisis that the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz has created, and the stalled diplomatic process on Gaza.
Egypt finds itself at the intersection, if not directly involved in many of these crises. To represent Egypt’s position at the mega-diplomatic forum that is the UNGA, President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly for the second year in a row to lead Cairo’s delegation.
Sisi led Egypt’s delegations to the UNGA himself from 2014 to 2019. Since then, he has sent his foreign minister in his place: first Sameh Shoukry, who held the post from 2014 to 2024, and now Badr Abdel Atty.
The president’s decision to not personally lead the delegation this year, according to a government official, comes down to the fact that he “did not want to personally participate in the meeting of the Board of Peace, even though the primary issue on the agenda was Gaza — a pivotal matter for Egypt.”
“To this day, the board remains unable to take serious action to improve the situation for Palestinians on the ground — despite a full year having passed since the ceasefire agreement between Hamas and Israel, following two years of an Israeli war of extermination against Gaza — which is, of course, deeply embarrassing for Cairo,” the government official says.
The Board of Peace, chaired by United States President Donald Trump, was established earlier this year, with Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov selected as the board’s envoy to the Gaza Strip. According to a member of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza — a body established by the Board of Peace to succeed Hamas — the board is “completely powerless to even secure Israel’s consent for the committee to enter the Strip, or to allow the exit of 10,000 individuals selected for training in Egypt to serve as a Palestinian police force replacing Hamas’s police, even though Hamas has publicly declared its readiness to relinquish all its weapons.”
Although a source with direct insight into Egyptian-Israeli relations states that Cairo is maintaining all official and unofficial communication channels with Tel Aviv to address the situation in Gaza, this does not imply that the head of government will personally participate in Board of Peace meetings, given its limited effectiveness.
Instead it was Madbuly who led the delegation to the Board of Peace meetings to discuss the situation in Gaza on Wednesday.
Setting aside what a member of the team preparing for the Egyptian delegation’s visit to New York described to Mada Masr as Madbuly’s largely ceremonial role, much of Egypt’s political messaging is being handled by Foreign Minister Badr Abdel Atty, whose schedule has been packed with meetings. Egypt’s top diplomat arrived in New York on September 19 — two days before Madbuly — and is set to return to Cairo next week.
According to the team member, there are four key issues atop Abdel Atty’s agenda during his meetings in New York. The first is the situation in Sudan.

items.body_text:
Rizeigat clan bids for Hemedti’s ear, Burhan’s US visa troubles, Kordofan battles come to head as RSF presses ahead in Blue Nile, Kiir re-engineers electoral scene          
        As world leaders gathered in New York this week for talks at the United Nations General Assembly, Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan had to watch the proceeding from afar. And that is because, while the military leader had been penciled in to give a speech to the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, the US denied his visa.
For Sudanese officials familiar with the internal planning, the move doesn’t come as a complete surprise, given that the US had sanctioned Burhan last year and the relationship has become increasingly fractious. But the visa denial is yet another sign of the frustration and polarization that dominates talks over a humanitarian truce, ceasefire and political settlement to Sudan’s war.
Sources in New York and others familiar with communications between Sudan, regional capitals and the US described efforts to mitigate the crisis, which they viewed as US pressure on Sudan to accept a 90-day humanitarian truce, while emphasizing that the government would not back down from its core position.
But the military wasn’t the only one facing a political crisis this week. In Darfur, the Nawaiba, one of the Rizeigat’s main clans in East Darfur, announced it was withdrawing from the nazirate of Musa Madibo, the head of the Rizeigat.
The Nawaib were keen to underline they still support the RSF leadership, who hail from the Rizeigat. According to a Rizeigat tribal leader informed of discussions within several of the tribe’s components, the move is really a bid to open a direct line of communication with RSF Commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo.
Nonetheless, for the RSF, which has already seen internecine fighting among its base, with loyalists jockeying for rungs in the broader hierarchy, the move’s catalytic effect could create an even larger opening for rival military and political actors to exploit the crisis.
Away from political management, Sudan’s two main battlefronts continue to churn. Following weeks of military gains in North Kordofan, fighting is narrowing in on the remaining RSF-held positions. Both sides are upping the ante with front line deployments to try to sway the fight for the state one way or another.
The military holds a much less firm position in the Blue Nile, even as it continues to prevent being overrun. With its eyes set on the state’s capital of Damazin, the RSF unsuccessfully attempted to take key towns that would have allowed it to create linkages in its supply chain between its positions on the southeastern border with Ethiopia and its forces farther south near South Sudan.
As wars engulf its neighbors, South Sudan seems set for its own breaking point. In a continuation of his efforts to marginalize his one-time enemy, one-time co-leader in power former Vice President Riek Machar, Kiir overhauled the country’s electoral process this week, appointing a new elections commission chair, amending the electoral law and dissolving the transitional government.
An opposition source called the move politically biased, saying electoral rules set specific grounds for removing the chair, including proven bias, inability to perform the job or serious misconduct.
Elections are set to be held in December, and while voices in South Sudan and beyond continue to warn that current government practices are widening divides, Kiir continues to press ahead, pushing the country, perhaps, to be yet another blazing front in a region on fire.

items.body_text:
After seizing Tigray airports, TPLF announces ‘defensive war’ against Ethiopian govt          
        The confrontation between the Tigray regional government and the Ethiopian federal government entered a new phase on Wednesday when Tigrayan forces seized control of the Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports.
Clashes broke out at several locations in the restive northern state, the site of a two-year civil war that concluded in 2022, and in the neighboring Afar region — a development that has pushed the Ethiopian conflict back toward open warfare, four years after the signing of the Pretoria Agreement that ended the previous war between the Tigray People’s Liberation Front and federal forces.
A source in the Tigray regional administration told Mada Masr that the seizure of the airports was part of a military redeployment that began in the early hours of Wednesday, with Tigrayan forces using the airports as facilities of operational importance amid the expanding scope of the fighting.
In the wake of the TPLF takeover, Ethiopian Airlines announced the suspension of flights to the three airports due to the “current situation” in the Tigray region.
A Tigrayan military source noted that Wednesday’s developments followed months of troop buildup and limited skirmishes along the front lines, describing Wednesday’s events as a shift from a phase of mutual pressure to direct confrontation. He added that Tigrayan forces view federal movements as an attempt to alter the military landscape established since the Pretoria Agreement and believe that seizing certain vital sites could prevent federal forces from utilizing the region’s civilian and military infrastructure during ongoing operations.
The federal government framed Wednesday’s events differently. A former security source in Addis Ababa described the movements by the TPLF as a “full-scale attack” on government positions in Afar and Amhara.
While seizing airports does not in itself decide the outcome of the battle, it signals a shift in the nature of operations, a security source in Addis Ababa told Mada Masr. Mekelle serves as the region’s political and administrative hub, while the airports at Axum and Shire provide crucial links to northern and western Tigray. Consequently, placing airports under the control of regional forces strains the federal government’s ability to manage its presence within the region and gives Tigrayan forces a strategic advantage in any future negotiations, the source said.
The security source added that any operation to retake the airports would require careful calculation due to the presence of civilians in the cities, and because the use of air power and artillery in urban areas would heighten humanitarian risks.
In its first official comment on Wednesday’s escalation, the Ethiopian military said it had repelled attacks from Tigrayan forces and their allies in parts of northern Ethiopia, adding that hostilities began in an area of the Amhara region close to the border with Tigray.
The military added that it had killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 in a counteroffensive in the Amhara region.
Wednesday’s escalation in the long simmering tension between the TPLF and federal government immediately follows a series of airstrikes that targeted areas in Tigray over the past few days. In Alamata, located in southern Tigray, an attack on Tuesday left 14 civilians dead and 22 injured, a local media source told Mada Masr.
The source stated that more than six drones and three fighter jets carried out over 21 raids, beginning around 3:30 am, adding that the strikes hit civilian educational facilities, including a secondary school.
The media source noted that the area has recently seen an increase in military activity and troop movements involving both federal and Tigrayan forces.
The TPLF is increasingly worried about drone strikes, a senior official in the front told Mada Masr, saying that many top officials are limiting their movements to avoid being targeted b

Omar Hisham Talaat stated that the schedule comprises 11 tournaments in the first half of the year and nine in the second half. items.body_text:
The Egyptian Golf Federation will host 20 international tournaments in 2026 as part of a campaign to promote sports tourism and support the national economy, the federation’s president said.
Omar Hisham Talaat stated that the schedule comprises 11 tournaments in the first half of the year and nine in the second half. The competitions fall under the “Egypt Golf Series,” an initiative launched by the federation at the beginning of the year.
The federation is executing a plan to enhance the country’s position on the global golf tourism map. Omar Hisham Talaat noted that hosting these major events aims to attract players and foreign delegations, while promoting Egyptian tourist destinations through international media coverage.
Omar Hisham Talaat cited the recent Asian Development Tour tournament, hosted by Madinaty Golf Club, as an important milestone in this plan. He said the event featured international participation with players representing more than 30 nationalities, which serves to place Egypt on the global sports tourism map.
Outlining the upcoming schedule, Omar Hisham Talaat said Egypt will host the Arab Junior and Youth Championship, which is expected to see broad regional participation, followed by the Arab Senior Championship.
The agenda also includes the return of the MENA Golf Tour to Egypt with two tournaments. Additionally, the Egypt International Open for Professionals will be held for the second consecutive time following a 15-year absence.
The 2026 schedule will conclude with the Egypt International Junior and Ladies Championship, alongside the Egypt International Men’s Championship. Omar Hisham Talaat stated that these events are intended to strengthen Egypt’s international presence and support the federation’s efforts to market the country as a destination for golf tourism.

The agreement was signed by Ayman Elbayaa, Executive Director of the IMC, and Mohamed Abdeen, CEO of Corporate […] The post IMC, Corporate Stack Solutions sign pact to accelerate SME digitalisation fir
items.body_text:
The Industrial Modernisation Center (IMC) has signed a cooperation protocol with Corporate Stack Solutions, a company specialising in digital consulting and applications, to support the digital transformation of Egyptian industrial companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The agreement was signed by Ayman Elbayaa, Executive Director of the IMC, and Mohamed Abdeen, CEO of Corporate Stack Solutions, in the presence of representatives from both sides and officials from the industrial and information technology sectors.
The protocol aims to enable local industrial companies to adopt enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and advanced digital applications through locally developed software-as-a-service (SaaS) solutions based on monthly subscriptions.
The initiative is intended to improve factories’ operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance their competitiveness in local and international markets, as part of Egypt’s efforts to accelerate digital transformation and the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies.
IMC Executive Director Ayman Elbayaa said the cooperation reinforces a “three-way partnership model” between the IMC, the technology developer, and beneficiary companies, adding that the centre is focused on raising the level of digital maturity across the industrial sector.
He added that the IMC will provide technical and supervisory support, as well as a package of facilities under the partnership, to help ensure the successful and sustainable implementation of digital transformation within factories.
For his part, Corporate Stack Solutions CEO Mohamed Abdeen said the company would provide locally developed software solutions and customised packages at preferential costs for IMC clients.
The company will also commit to a 60- to 90-day timeline for installation, implementation, and training, in addition to providing continuous technical support to factories throughout the contract period, he said.
Abdeen said digital transformation should not be limited to large companies, noting that SMEs also need efficient tools to manage their resources, operations, and data, but through simpler solutions suited to their business models and capabilities.
He pointed out that the partnership with the IMC provides an opportunity to implement this approach on a wider scale, adding that the objective extends beyond providing factories with technology to offering an integrated transformation process.
This process will start with identifying each factory’s needs and continue through implementation, training, and operation, ultimately enabling companies to use digital tools effectively in their day-to-day operations and achieve measurable business results.

Addressing the event’s theme, “Sustainable DevOps Methodologies in the Era of Agentic AI,” Hindi stated that the competence of Egyptian […] The post Egypt highlights 200,000-strong digital export workforce at DevOpsDays Cairo 2026 first appeared
items.body_text:
Approximately 200,000 specialists are currently working in exporting digital services from Egypt to global markets, Minister of Communications and Information Technology Raafat Hindi said during the opening of the ninth DevOpsDays Cairo 2026 conference.
Addressing the event’s theme, “Sustainable DevOps Methodologies in the Era of Agentic AI,” Hindi stated that the competence of Egyptian developers remains a major sector strength and a catalyst for multinational companies expanding their local operations.
Hindi noted that global software development is experiencing a deep transition toward autonomous artificial intelligence systems. As AI increasingly participates in writing code, testing, and autonomous decision-making, the minister raised questions regarding the maintenance of human oversight, accountability, energy and computing resource consumption, and cybersecurity compliance.
To demonstrate local technological advancement, Hindi highlighted the recent launch of “Karnak,” the first Egyptian large language model (LLM) developed by local engineers, which is capable of understanding classical and colloquial Egyptian Arabic. He emphasised the role of DevOps engineers in transitioning such digital models from technical achievements into sustainable, reliable services.
Ahmed El-Zaher, CEO of the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), said the rapid evolution of Agentic AI is transforming software systems from assistive tools into entities capable of autonomous task execution and planning. This shift requires updated work methodologies, governance frameworks, and continuous investment in specialised skills, he said.
El-Zaher added that the ninth edition of the conference features 66 speakers, including 13 international experts from nine countries.
The event is organised by ITIDA’s Software Engineering Competence Center (SECC) at the Creativa Innovation Hub in Giza. Cairo hosted the first regional edition in 2018 and remains the only Arab city to host the DevOpsDays series, which operates in over 60 cities worldwide.
The conference agenda comprises four main tracks addressing DevOps in the Agentic AI era: cost and environmental sustainability, human sustainability and governance, security and reliability, and tools and infrastructure. The programme also includes three panel discussions on governance, corporate culture, and organisational aspects, alongside three specialised workshops.
The event will conclude with the announcement of the winning teams in a competition focused on employing DevOps and AI to accelerate automation and innovation. Out of 142 applicant teams, 20 reached the final stage, split equally between 10 student teams and 10 professional graduate teams. The finalists were evaluated by a 12-member panel comprising six Egyptian and six international judges.
The conference was attended by SECC Head Haitham Hamza, ITIDA officials, and IT and software development managers from local and global companies.

items.title: Israeli Forces Shell Farmland in Rural Quneitra
items.summary: Documenting these movements, the Sijil human rights centre recorded 267 Israeli violations inside Syrian territory in August, bringing the total it has documented since the start of 2026 to 1,752. The post Israeli Forces Shell Farmland in Rural Quneitra first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Israeli forces on Thursday fired artillery shells at farmland on the outskirts of the village of Al-Hamidiyeh in rural Quneitra, a Syria TV correspondent reported.
No information has yet emerged on casualties or the extent of the damage caused by the shelling.
Israeli forces have stepped up their military activity in southern Syria over the past two weeks, particularly in rural Quneitra and Rural Damascus, where the area has seen a series of incursions, artillery shelling, checkpoints, raids and detentions.
The escalation followed a visit by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, accompanied by Defence Minister Israel Katz, to the Mount Hermon (Jabal Al-Sheikh) area in occupied Syrian territory on September 9.
267 Israeli Violations
Documenting these movements, the Sijil human rights centre recorded 267 Israeli violations inside Syrian territory in August, bringing the total it has documented since the start of 2026 to 1,752.
In its monthly report, the centre said the number of violations recorded in August rose by 43 percent compared with July, which saw 187, and by about 12 percent compared with June, which recorded 239.
According to the report, August recorded the second-highest monthly number of Israeli violations since the start of the year, after March, which saw 321, and ahead of April’s 254.

items.title: Joe Wilson to Al-Modon: Sharaa Is Reconnecting Syria With the World
items.summary: U.S. Congressman Joe Wilson praised the transformation underway in Syria in a statement to Al-Modon, saying that Syria’s positive presence on the international stage mattered greatly to Syrians and to Syrian-Americans. Mr Wilson was commenting on President Ahmad Al-Sharaa’s visit to New York to attend the 81st session of the U.N. General Assembly, his third […] The post Joe Wilson to Al-Modon: Sharaa Is Reconnecting Syria With the World first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
U.S. Congressman Joe Wilson praised the transformation underway in Syria in a statement to Al-Modon, saying that Syria’s positive presence on the international stage mattered greatly to Syrians and to Syrian-Americans.
Mr Wilson was commenting on President Ahmad Al-Sharaa’s visit to New York to attend the 81st session of the U.N. General Assembly, his third visit to the United States since taking office.
He affirmed U.S. support for President Sharaa’s efforts to reconnect Syria with the world and to promote peace and prosperity.
Syria Regains Its International Presence
“It is extremely important for Syrians and Syrian-Americans to see their country, once a pariah because of the former regime, represented positively on the world stage,” Mr Wilson said. He added: “President Sharaa is helping reconnect Syria with the world, and America supports his efforts to promote peace and prosperity.”
In New York, President Sharaa is holding four days of high-level meetings with leaders and diplomats on the sidelines of the General Assembly, most notably an expected meeting with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
A Supportive Voice for Syria in Congress
In recent months, Mr Wilson has backed improved U.S. relations with Syria and pushed Washington to ease economic and political restrictions on the country, while also calling for Syria’s stability to be protected and for an end to airstrikes on Syrian territory.
In his latest statement, Mr Wilson called for a halt to Israeli airstrikes on Syria, saying that they undermined the stabilisation process Washington sought to support.
In a series of posts on X, he said he appreciated U.S. Envoy to Syria Tom Barrack’s opposition to the strikes. Asked whether he was explicitly calling for them to stop, he replied: “Absolutely.”
Mr Wilson linked this position to the need to give Syria a chance to consolidate stability, peace and prosperity, arguing that the success of this process would benefit not only Syria but the wider region.
His efforts have not been limited to political statements. Over the past period, he has worked within Congress to remove legal and economic obstacles to Syria’s opening to the world.
In June, Mr Wilson called on the U.S. Department of State to remove Syria’s designation as a “State Sponsor of Terrorism” and to lower the U.S. travel advisory for the country, arguing that developments in Syria warranted a review of U.S. policy to reflect the new reality.
He said that, in his assessment, Syria had taken historic steps towards peace and prosperity and had cooperated with the United States on the regional agenda and counterterrorism.
Mr Wilson also acted on sanctions. In 2025, he introduced an amendment in Congress to repeal the Caesar Act, saying it was time to give Syria a chance.
The Caesar Act was repealed in December 2025 as part of the U.S. National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for fiscal year 2026.

items.title: Kherson government shows operation delivering 4 tonnes of food to occupied Oleshky – video
items.summary: Ukrainian forces used heavy drones to drop nearly 4,000 kg of humanitarian food aid across 100 locations in Russian-occupied Oleshky, Kherson Oblast.
items.body_text:
Kherson government shows operation delivering 4 tonnes of food to occupied Oleshky – video
Ukrainian forces carried out one of their largest humanitarian aid delivery operations to the occupied town of Oleshky in Kherson Oblast, using drones to transport nearly 4,000 kilograms of food.
Source: Kherson Oblast Military Administration on Telegram
Details: The food supplies were delivered simultaneously across 100 designated locations in the town.
The Oblast Military Administration did not specify the exact date when the operation took place.
Units participating in the operation included the 30th Marine Corps, the Hrom tactical group, the 34th Borysfen Separate Marine Brigade, the 11th National Guard Brigade, the 34th National Guard Regiment and the 79th Border Guard Detachment.
The Oblast Military Administration noted that Ukrainian forces have been systematically delivering food to Oleshky across the Dnipro River via unmanned aerial vehicles since March.
According to the administration, around 2,000 people remain in the occupied town, including nearly 50 children.
The Oblast Military Administration also stated that Russian forces actively try to prevent aid delivery by shooting down food-bearing drones, confiscating or reselling provisions and detaining residents who receive humanitarian packages.
Background:
- On 19 September, the Ukrainian Council of Churches and Religious Organisations (UCCRO) reported a critical humanitarian situation in the occupied town of Oleshky.
- The UCCRO said the last food supplies reached Oleshky in late May 2026. More than 6,000 people, including around 200 children, may still remain in Oleshky and the surrounding district, according to various estimates.
- Ukraine's 34th Marine Brigade posted a video showing temporarily occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast, describing it as "a city the Russians have turned into a ghost town".

items.title: Drone debris found near Moldovan village
items.summary: Moldovan border guards discovered pieces of an unidentified drone in Ștefan Vodă District on 26 September, hours after another unidentified drone entered the country's airspace amid Russian attacks on Ukraine.
items.body_text:
Drone debris found near Moldovan village
On the evening of 26 September, Moldovan border guards discovered debris of an unmanned aerial vehicle outside the village of Volintiri in Ștefan Vodă District.
Source: Moldova's Border Police
Details: Pieces of an unidentified drone were discovered at around 20:25 after local residents alerted the authorities.
Border guards immediately cordoned off the area. The necessary measures are currently being taken to establish all the circumstances surrounding the incident.
Moldova's Border Police said that, in cooperation with other competent authorities, it was continuously monitoring the situation and maintaining contact with the relevant Ukrainian authorities.
Law enforcement officers urged the public not to approach or touch possible pieces of aircraft, ammunition or other unidentified objects. Anyone who discovers such objects is advised to move away from the area and immediately call 112.
It is worth noting that earlier the same day, amid Russian attacks on Ukraine, an unidentified drone illegally entered Moldovan airspace. The object reportedly entered the country's airspace at 11:16, approaching from the direction of Stepanivka in Odesa Oblast, Ukraine, and crossed the state border towards Novokotovsk in the unrecognised breakaway region of Transnistria.
At 11:18, the object left Moldovan airspace, crossing the border towards Lymanske in Odesa Oblast.
It was also reported that an unidentified object violated Romanian airspace overnight on 26 September, prompting allied fighter jets to be scrambled.
On 18 September, police found drone fragments near Chișinău.

“There are important results from our troops in the Lyman sector of the Donetsk region as part of Operation Vivaldi, as well as from the Airborne Assault Forces grouping as part of another one of our active defense operations. The occupiers continue to be eliminated, and the designated objectives are being achieved. Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Mykhailo Drapatyi delivered a report today. Overall, this week, across all sectors of active combat operations on the front, our units neutralized 10,660 Russian troops killed and wounded,” the President wrote.
He added that every Russian casualty is accompanied by video confirmation.
Zelensky said that the most intense fighting is taking place in the areas of the Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, and Lyman sectors. According to him, operations are also being carried out in Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, and Sumy regions.
“Based on this week’s results, the warriors of the Third Army Corps and the 68th Separate Oleksa Dovbush Airmobile Brigade of the 8th Corps of the Airborne Assault Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine deserve special recognition. Thank you all for the results, warriors! Every such week on the front that becomes ours – Ukrainian – in terms of the overall situation prevents Russia from mounting greater offensive activity against Ukraine,” he wrote.
Zelensky added that during the meeting, he and the commander-in-chief identified further active steps.
As Ukrinform reported, soldiers of the 3rd Army Corps used remote mining during the Vivaldi offensive operation and, over two nights, created 400 meters of mine barriers using ground-based robotic systems.

items.title: Budanov Announces Major POW Exchange With Russia as Early as Next Week
items.summary: Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov said Sunday, Sept. 27 that a major prisoner exchange between Ukraine and Russia could take place, as early as next week. However, he did not provide any additional information regarding the possible date or scale of the exchange.
items.body_text:
Ukraine and Russia are reportedly preparing another major prisoner of war (POW) exchange, according to the head of the Presidential Office, Kyrylo Budanov Sunday, Sept. 27.
The exchange could take place as early as next week, Budanov told Novyny.LIVE on the sidelines of the national “Golden Hands” award ceremony.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“It should happen very quickly, in the near future. I think, within the next week,” Budanov said according to RBC-Ukraine, without providing any additional information regarding the possible date or scale of the exchange.
Moscow had not independently confirmed the planned swap at the time of the report.
A rare channel of dialogue
Prisoner exchanges have remained one of the few areas where Kyiv and Moscow continue to cooperate, even as broader peace efforts stall, according to Budanov on Aug. 29.
He also said that the war in Ukraine will most certainly continue through the winter, dismissing hopes of a near-term ceasefire and saying that Russia’s refusal to stop the war made any immediate freeze “unrealistic.”
Previous swaps
The last known return took place on Aug. 24, when Ukraine brought home 10 servicemen from captivity via Belarus, according to RBC-Ukraine.
The release was carried out as a special stage of an exchange agreed between the two sides.
All 10 had fought in the Donetsk sector and had previously been listed as missing, two of them since 2024 and eight since 2025.
UK Police Call In Bomb Disposal Team Near US-Used Air Base
Just two weeks earlier, on Aug. 10, Ukraine and Russia exchanged 103 prisoners each. On Ukraine’s side, the released POWs included troops from the Armed Forces (AFU), Border Guard Service, and National Guard who fought in Mariupol and across several other regions.
In April, Budanov announced a new exchange was being prepared shortly after Ukraine brought home 182 people in its 72nd prisoner swap.
That group included 175 military personnel and seven civilians, many of whom had been in captivity since 2022, among them defenders of Mariupol and the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant.
At the time, Budanov said a larger group could not be returned right away because of what he described as bureaucratic delays on the Russian side.
Foreign citizens dragged into Russia’s war
According to Ukraine’s “I Want to Live” project – which helps Russian soldiers surrender – one in 10 POWs held in Ukraine is a foreign citizen.
As of September, Russian POWs in Ukraine include citizens of 55 countries.
Nearly 29,000 foreign nationals have signed contracts with Russia’s armed forces since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in 2022, pointing to the growing international outreach of Russia’s military recruitment which deliberately targets economically vulnerable people from Third World countries.
Russia had also signed a defense pact with North Korea on June 19, 2024, with both countries officially recognizing North Korean troop deployments in April 2025.
Since then, North Korean troops have continued to be deployed or rotated through Russia. Ukrainian military intelligence estimates that around 25,000 North Korean troops have served in Russia so far.
On July 29, Zelensky warned that Russia is preparing to receive 30,000 additional North Korean troops and more ballistic missile launchers.
In August, Kyiv had warned of Pyongyang’s fresh troop deployments to Russia, numbering 8,500.
