items.title: Finnish ministry wants to hear about kids' social media habits from parents, guardians
items.summary: The survey is meant to help a ministerial working group find ways to reduce social media harms.
items.body_text:
The Ministry of Social Affairs and Health has asked parents and guardians to share their views on children's use of social media platforms via an online survey.
The survey is available in Finnish, Swedish and English, and responses can be submitted until the closing date of Sunday 11 October.
According to the ministry, the survey's responses will help inform a ministry-appointed working group's study, entitled Protecting Children and Young People from the Harms of Social Media.
The call-out comes in the wake of the European Union announcing last week that it plans to restrict social media access for kids under the age of 15. The move could see the introduction of age limits for social media platforms, restrictions on addictive online games, as well as other protective measures concerning children and young people.
There has been widespread discussion in Finland about the harmful effects social media can have on kids, in particular since Australia introduced a ban at the end of last year.
A survey published last month found that more than half of Finns support banning children under 15 from using social media.
Yle News' All Points North podcast delved into the debate around the introduction of a ban on social media for under-15s earlier this year. Listen to the episode via this embedded player, on Yle Areena, via Apple, Spotify or wherever you get your podcasts.

items.title: Finnish MP warns against politicians becoming "AI puppets"
items.summary: Use of the technology is increasingly evident in day-to-day politics, Left Alliance MP Anna Kontula says, including to write speeches delivered in parliament.
items.body_text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is already having a significant impact on Finland's politics, according to Left Alliance MP Anna Kontula.
Speaking on Yle's Finnish-language Uutispodcast, Kontula said AI use has become increasingly evident in parliament's plenary hall.
"Some use it as a summary tool, which can condense large amounts of material. Others directly write speeches using AI. I have heard that in the preparation of legislative proposals and during consultation rounds, AI-generated statements have started to be used," she said.
The threats posed by AI, and especially by its rapid development, have been widely discussed in Finland and around the world in recent years — with concerns ranging from AI taking people's jobs to wiping out humanity.
Earlier this week, an OpenAI agent infiltrated an Australian government website in what experts say is the first major example of the technology going "rogue".
Kontula told the podcast that politicians have limited powers to influence the effects of AI.
"Politicians propose regulation as a solution to AI risks, because we have nothing else to offer," she noted.
However, she further added that the increasing use of AI in politics is not purely a bad thing, as it can help reduce workloads and assist with more mundane tasks.
But she warned against the dangers of politicians becoming "AI puppets".
"AI creates a government bill. This goes to a committee, whose position and dissenting opinions are drafted by AI, and then in the plenary session the legislative initiative is discussed partly with AI-generated speeches, so if AI drafts the text and reads it, what's the point of the text at all?"

items.title: From the obvious to the unthinkable: Nine options for Sweden's government
items.summary: Prime minister Ulf Kristersson lost Sweden's election earlier this month, but until Magdalena Andersson manages to form a government, she hasn't won. We run through nine possible coalitions with politics professors Jonas Hinnfors and Nicholas Aylott.
items.body_text:
In the week after the election on September 13th, Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson was appointed sonderingsperson by the parliament's speaker, Andreas Norlén. This means she gets the first shot at trying to negotiate enough support among the other parties to be tolerated as prime minister in a parliamentary vote.
She has said she is willing to negotiate with every party apart from the far-right Sweden Democrats (although she qualified this by saying that the Left Party has "a long journey to go on" before it should have ministerial positions.
So, what sort of government coalitions might she have in mind, and if she fails, what possibilities are available to Kristersson?
To get tolerated by parliament, Andersson doesn't have to negotiate a government coalition with a majority.
One or more parties could stay outside the government but have a detailed agreement, like the current government's Tidö Agreement.
One or more could also have a looser agreement when they agree to support the government's budgets, but make few other commitments.
It's even possible that one or more parties might let Andersson become prime minister by abstaining in the vote on her candidacy without making any other commitments at all, forcing her government to cut deals every time it wants to pass a bill, and leaving every budget at risk of falling.
What are the options for Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson?
1) S C MP (V)
According to Johan Hinnfors, Professor Emeritus in Politics at Gothenburg University, it is clear which coalition is top of her list: a government including the Social Democrats, Centre Party, and the Green Party. But will she get it?
“If she were to choose, she would like to form a three-party government: the Centre Party, the Greens and the Social Democrats, with a confidence and supply deal in writing with the Left Party," Hinnfors told The Local.
This agreement, he says, would "state issue areas where they are to cooperate, and particularly state that those four parties, the government and the left party, have to agree on the budget.”
This would be a minority government, with a two-seat majority once the votes of its support party are included.
The issue with this constellation (as we have repeated ad nauseum) is that the Left Party refuses to support a government in which it does not have ministers, and the Centre Party refuses to support a government in which the Left Party does have ministers.
One of them, or perhaps both, will need to compromise and so far neither show any signs of doing so.
Andersson will be hoping that the Left Party will in the end accept a similar position to that held by the Sweden Democrats over the past four years, with officials in parliament, a formal coalition agreement, and perhaps Left Party spokespeople appearing at government press conferences.
If the Left Party was given a big enough policy win – perhaps if the Centre Party agreed to end profit-making at Swedish free schools – might that be enough of a win to allow it to back down?
We shall see.
2) S MP C V
The Green Party has said that its preferred solution is to have all four of the former opposition parties inside the government. This would give the government an even more stable majority than the Tidö government's. This, however, would require the Centre Party to drop its opposition to Left Party ministers.
Might it agree to do so if the Left Party was given only junior ministers or if it agreed in exchange to allow the government to run a thoroughgoing centre-right economic program dictated by the Centre Party?
Hinnfors doubts that it would drop its red line whatever it is offered. The party, he points out, has extremely strong finances, so it has less to fear from an emergency new election.
“I think it’s more likely that the Left Party is technically outside the government than inside the government."
3) S MP (V C)

items.title: 'Standing up for immigrants': Why The Local's readers voted big for the Swedish Greens
items.summary: The results of our (highly unscientific) reader survey on how you voted in Sweden's election are in.
items.body_text:
Over a hundred readers responded to our voting survey and the results are a mix of the expected and the surprising, especially when compared with how the electorate voted overall.
The party readers of The Local voted for most was the Social Democrats, putting them right in line with the rest of the electorate – so close, in fact, that the percentage of vote share was almost identical, at just over 28 percent.
For most of the rest of the parties, however, reader respondents to our survey veered off from the overall electorate in Sweden, sometimes quite far off.
The most striking example is probably support for the Green Party, which among survey respondents was inching towards 27 percent, nearly on par with the leading Social Democrats, but which scraped a pretty measly 6.12 percent in the election overall (putting them not far above last-place Liberals, with 5.34 percent of the overall vote).
The Left Party also did quite well among readers compared to the electorate overall, receiving 17 percent from readers and 8.4 overall.
The Moderates had almost an inverse result: just 7.6 percent of our readers said they voted Moderate, as opposed to nearly 20 percent of the total electorate.
Like the other parties which were in opposition during Tidö's time in government, the Centre Party over-performed the general electorate with our readers, but not as dramatically: 10.5 percent of respondents to our survey said the voted Centre compared to 7 percent overall.
With two exceptions, all respondents said they had immigrated to Sweden at some point from another country.
So, why did readers vote the way they did?
There was a diversity of answers, but some clear patterns as well. We'll break them down for you by party, starting from the most popular party among respondents to the least.
Why did readers vote Social Democrat?
The two main reasons respondents voted Social Democrat were: they think it's a well-balanced and reasonable party, and they felt it was the main way to oppose the Tidö government.
"[It is] a party that is relatively balanced on most topics," wrote Seyi, a senior banker originally from Nigeria and now based in Stockholm.
"Although leaning right in immigration they have taken what I think is common sense and not caused division or targeted a particular group," he continued. "Also I think their policies on economics and taxes are usually well balanced. Plus they promised to reform the immigration laws as a whole to make it easier to understand."
An anonymous reader identifying as a centrist had similar comments: "I didn’t want the Tidö parties in government, so as a centrist, I felt I had two options: the Social Democrats or the Centre Party. I chose the Social Democrats because they have more support," they wrote.
A British remote tech worker based in Västernorrland summed up this view, describing the Social Democrats as, "broadly a safe choice, mainly a tactical vote to offset Tidö parties."
Some Social Democrat voter respondents also cited the leadership qualities of Magdalena Andersson as their reason for voting for the party, and others the positive role they felt it played in Sweden in the past.
"I listened to Magda’s debates and while I don’t agree completely with the economic policies of the Social Democrats I think she has what it takes to take the country out of the situation we are in because of the Sweden Democrats and the poor Moderate leadership," wrote a software engineer in Jönköping who wanted to remain anonymous.
"They were the leading party when I liked Sweden," wrote a reader who also wanted to remain anonymous.
Why did readers vote Green?
Unsurprisingly, many readers chose to vote for the Green Party because of their focus on climate issues.
"Because I care for the world we’ll leave behind," wrote a reader in Malmö who has been in Sweden for 12 years.
"I’m most concerned with environmental issues and how we are destroying our planet with climate breakdown well under way. For me the environmental is THE i

items.title: Where are the breakthroughs for the radical and far-right in Europe?
items.summary: After recent regional election breakthroughs by the Alternative for Germany (AfD), here is an overview of radical, nationalist and far- and hard-right parties' positions across Europe in recent years.
items.body_text:
Germany: AfD breakthrough
The far-right AfD became Germany's main opposition party in the February 2025 legislative elections, finishing second behind Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservatives with 20.8 percent of the vote.
The anti-immigration party, which is sympathetic to Russia and US President Donald Trump, scored a historic victory in the September 6 regional election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
It also came first in the September 20 regional election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state, but the centre-left SPD party looks set to continue governing by forming a coalition with left-wing allies.
READ ALSO: Why are young Europeans increasingly supporting anti-immigration parties?
Italy: governing force
In Italy, Giorgia Meloni -- whose post-fascist Brothers of Italy party scored a historic victory in the 2022 legislative elections -- has headed the government since October that year.
Her coalition includes another far-right party, Matteo Salvini's League, as well as the conservative Forza Italia.
Advances in Austria, Switzerland
In Austria, the Freedom Party (FPO), founded by former Nazis, came first in the September 2024 legislative elections but failed to find coalition partners to form a government.
In Switzerland, the October 2023 elections consolidated the radical-right and nationalist Swiss People's Party (SVP) as the largest party in the National Council, the lower house of parliament, with 62 of its 200 seats.
France: Le Pen rides high
In France in 2024, the National Rally became the largest single party in the lower house of parliament by number of seats, but its power there was curbed by an alliance of rival parties.
The National Rally's most prominent figure, Marine Le Pen, is the frontrunner for the spring 2027 presidential election in current opinion polls.
Spain surge
In Spain, buoyed by gains in regional elections, the far-right Vox party has allied with the conservative Popular Party (PP) to jointly govern or collaborate in several regions.
Portugal
In Portugal, the far-right Chega ("Enough") party topped 20 percent of the vote for the first time in the May 2025 legislative elections. The minority right-wing government has struck ad hoc deals with Chega to pass legislation, including on nationality and naturalisation.
Eight months later, Chega leader and populist Andre Ventura reached the second round of the presidential election, only to be defeated by moderate Socialist Antonio Jose Seguro.
Setback in Sweden
Sweden's legislative elections on September 13 brought an unexpected setback for the far-right Sweden Democrats (SD). Their support declined for the first time since the party entered parliament in 2010.
The party fell to third place, behind the Social Democrats and the centre-right Moderates.
In Finland, the far-right Finns Party, which came second in the April 2023 legislative elections, is part of the governing coalition led by conservative Petteri Orpo.
READ ALSO: EXPLAINED - What needs to happen for Sweden to get a new prime minister?
Britain, Belgium: seats won
In Belgium, the far-right Vlaams Belang in the June 2024 elections increased its seats to 31 of 124 in the Flemish parliament and 20 of 150 seats at federal level. It is the largest opposition group in both assemblies.
In Britain, Nigel Farage's anti-immigration Reform UK won 14 percent of the vote and secured its first five MPs in the July 2024 general election. In August 2026, Farage was re-elected as an MP in a snap by-election, albeit one that all the main UK political parties refused to take part in.
Netherlands: far-right persists -

items.title: Germany calls on Russia to 'abandon its dangerous path'
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul called on Moscow to "abandon its dangerous path of escalation" during a meeting with Russia's Sergei Lavrov at the UN on Saturday, a diplomat for Berlin said.
items.body_text:
The talks took place as tensions between Berlin and Moscow intensified in recent weeks, with Germany accusing Russia of orchestrating an attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport and each country ordering the closure of the other's consulate.
"Wadephul called on the Russian Federation to abandon its dangerous path of escalation vis-a-vis Germany, Europe, and NATO," the German diplomat said.
"He made it clear: incidents such as the recent attempted attack in Leipzig or further hybrid assaults would not shake Germany's resolve to support Ukraine, which has come under attack."
READ ALSO: Hanover Airport disrupted by drone week after Leipzig explosives find
It was the first such meeting since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.
Lavrov, who was to address the UN's gathering of world leaders in New York Saturday, last met with a German foreign minister, Annalena Baerbock, in January 2022, less than a month before Russian forces invaded Ukraine.
Germany is one of Kyiv's main allies, and relations between Moscow and Berlin -- already tense before the Ukraine invasion -- have deteriorated in recent days.
Lavrov -- Russia's longest-serving minister -- recently accused Germany of "wanting war again," and is one of Russia's most vocally anti-western officials.
European countries, including Germany, have sounded the alarm in recent days over what they say is increased Russian sabotage activities on their soil.
Direct flights between Russia and Germany have been suspended since the invasion.
The meeting Saturday was closed to media but Ukraine dominated, according to the German diplomat.
"The German foreign minister condemned Russia's ongoing and increasingly targeted aggression against the Ukrainian civilian population. This attempt to increase pressure does nothing to change Russia's untenable situation: every month, tens of thousands of Russian soldiers die in a hopeless war of positions, while the Russian economy continues to collapse," the diplomat said.
Before the meeting with Lavrov, the German side demanded that media access be restricted and that the opening remarks not be recorded, Moscow's foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said, according to the Russia's TASS news agency.
She said Saturday's meeting was initiated by Berlin and lasted about 20 minutes.

items.title: Where are public transport fares set to rise in Germany in 2027?
items.summary: Millions of passengers in Germany are facing higher public transport costs in 2027. Berlin, Munich and Hamburg have already announced fare changes, with at least one region holding prices steady.
items.body_text:
Public transport users across Germany are beginning to get a clearer picture of what they'll be paying for buses, trams and local trains next year.
While several major transport authorities are still finalising their fare decisions for 2027, some of the country's biggest networks, including those serving Berlin, Munich, Hamburg and Bremen, have already announced price increases.
Most operators say rising energy, fuel and staffing costs are behind the hikes, but not every region is following the same path. The Rhine-Main Transport Association (RMV), which covers Frankfurt and surrounding areas, has announced a rare fare freeze while it prepares a major overhaul of its ticket system.
Meanwhile, millions of Deutschlandticket holders are also likely to face another increase, with current estimates suggesting the nationwide pass could become slightly more expensive from January.
Berlin and Brandenburg
The Berlin-Brandenburg Transport Association (VBB) will raise fares by an average of 3.72 percent from January 1st, 2027.
The good news for occasional travellers in the capital is that the standard Berlin AB single-ride ticket will remain unchanged at €4.00.
That means passengers travelling entirely within Berlin's most commonly used fare zone will not see a further increase after the ticket price rose from €3.80 to €4.00 at the start of 2026.
Several other tickets, however, are becoming more expensive. The Berlin AB four-trip ticket will increase from €12.40 to €13.20, while the short-distance ticket will rise from €2.80 to €2.90.
Travellers heading to BER Airport or destinations in the wider Berlin-Brandenburg region will also notice a change. The Berlin ABC single ticket is increasing from €5.00 to €5.20.
According to the VBB, the increase is needed because inflation, higher operating costs and ongoing investment in vehicles and infrastructure continue to put pressure on public transport finances.
READ ALSO: The app helping Berliners track ticket inspections on public transport
Munich
Passengers in and around Munich will see one of the larger increases announced so far.
The Munich Transport and Fare Association (MVV) says fares will rise by an average of 4.9 percent from January 1st, largely because of higher energy and fuel costs.
Like Berlin, the MVV has chosen to protect some of its most frequently used tickets. The short-distance ticket and the standard single ticket for Munich's central Zone M will remain unchanged.
Other fares are rising. A day ticket for Zone M will increase to €10.80, while the multi-trip ticket will cost €21.00, or €19.50 when purchased digitally.
Weekly passes are also becoming more expensive. A weekly pass for Zone M or two zones will cost €25.80, while a pass covering Zones M to 5 will rise to €87.30.
Monthly pass prices will increase by an average of 4.8 percent.
The MVV is also simplifying its ticket range, with more than a quarter of current ticket types being discontinued due to changing travel patterns. These include the 9am monthly pass (9 Uhr Monatskarte) and the transfer/extension ticket (Anschlussticket)
READ ALSO: Six things to do on a rainy day in Munich
Hamburg
Hamburg's transport association HVV is raising fares from 2027, though some of its most popular tickets will remain unchanged.
Passengers travelling within the central Hamburg AB area will continue to pay €4.10 for a single ticket and €8.20 for a day ticket.
But one change that could catch passengers off guard is the end of HVV's seven-percent online booking discount
While the official fare remains unchanged at €4.10 and €8.20, passengers who previously bought tickets through the HVV app will lose the existing seven percent online discount and therefore pay more.
The transport authority says the discount was introduced to encourage digital ticket sales but is no longer necessary because more than half of all tickets are now sold digitally.

items.title: REVEALED: The best places to go mushroom foraging in Germany
items.summary: As the chilly autumn days set in, hoards of Germans wrap up warm and venture out into the forests to forage mushrooms. Here are some of the best spots to go to - and some tips for getting started.
items.body_text:
Though it may be hard to believe that summer's over, there's a lot to love about autumn in Germany. It's the season for spending afternoons in cosy cafes absorbed in a good book, preparing hearty Kürbissuppe (pumpkin soup) at home, and enjoying Germany's most beautiful and rugged landscapes as the leaves turn red and orange.
For lovers of the great outdoors, it's also the perfect season to try the popular German pastime of collecting mushrooms. The damp, misty nights and cool days between mid-September and late October offer the perfect climate for fungi to thrive, producing a glut of different mushrooms for keen-eyed scavengers to find.
Though seasoned Pilzsämmler (mushroom collectors) all have their own preferred spots for foraging, these are usually well-guarded secrets protected by the fungus-hunters' unwritten code.
That said, Germany is teeming with forests where endless varieties of mushrooms can be found - often near or around the pathways. Even if you're a complete beginner, these are the ideal places to take your first few steps into the world of mushroom-picking.
How to prepare for a mushroom foraging trip
While gathering wild mushrooms in the fresh autumn air may sound very wholesome, there's always a risk of stumbling across poisonous species, including those that are deadly to humans.
If you're a novice or first-timer, you may want to take part in a local seminar or guided forage to gather some essential knowledge beforehand. Otherwise, bringing a friend who knows what they're doing is a great way to get the lay of the land.
Daniela Pensold, a keen mushroom collector and the founder of We Cycle Brandenburg, recommends that beginners head to fir forests on their initial outings. Though there are fewer varieties of fungus to be found here, there's a higher concentration of particular types that can be easier to vet and identify.
She's usually on the lookout for porcini, chestnuts, umbrella mushrooms, birch mushrooms, red caps and chanterelles, and generally leaves the harder-to-identify species alone.
READ ALSO: What's behind the German fascination with foraging for wild mushrooms?
If you're unsure, the best place to call is a Pilzberatungstelle - or mushroom advice centre - where you can get free advice from a specialised Pilzberater, or mushroom consultant. (Yes, that's a real thing.) Here's a list of some local experts and advice centres across Germany, prepared by the German Mycological Society.
In terms of equipment, at the minimum you'll want a breathable container like a a woven basket and a pocket knife for cleaning your haul.
To reap the best harvest, head out first thing in the morning. That way you'll get the pick of the bunch before the fair-weather mushroom pickers descend on your patch.
It's also a good idea to know the ground rules.
Under German law, wild mushrooms can be only be foraged for your own consumption (and family and friends of course) - but not to sell. In reality, that means anyone caught with several kilos of mushrooms in their basket is likely to have them confiscated and face a pretty hefty fine to boot.
Foraging inside nature reserves and on private property is also forbidden - as is picking protected species - so stick to the well-trodden path, and well-known varieties, if in doubt.
Popular mushroom-picking spots around Germany
With so many forests and wooded areas, there's no shortage of locations to seek out wild mushrooms in Germany, regardless of where you live.
To help you narrow it down, we've compiled some mushroom-picking hotspots around the country that are easily accessible from major cities.
Bavaria
With its verdant forests and hilly landscapes, Bavaria is a true paradise for both seasoned and novice mushroom-pickers.
Residents of Upper Bavaria are particularly spoilt for choice, with a multitude of options both in and around Munich. The Weltwald Freising is around 40 kilometres north of the Bavarian capital, and offers an astounding 16,000 hectares of woodland for forage

Riau Disaster Mitigation Agency Chief Edy Afrizal said the fires were under control. Despite no active fires, authorities remained on alert for potential flare-ups.
“Thankfully, Riau has zero forest and land fires today. There are no active fires we are handling,” Edy said in Pekanbaru, the capital of Riau Province, on Sunday.
However, all personnel remain on standby and monitoring continues because conditions on the ground can change at any time, he said, adding that the improving situation reflected joint efforts by personnel working in the field.
Firefighting, cooling operations, and patrols continued to prevent previously burned areas from reigniting, Edy said.
Meanwhile, Riau Police Public Relations Head Senior Commissioner Akmadi said the zero-fire status would not ease prevention efforts. Patrols and monitoring continued, particularly in fire-prone and peatland areas.
“We must maintain zero forest and land fires today. Personnel continue to conduct patrols and prevention efforts,” Akmadi said.
“We must not let our vigilance decline once the situation is under control, because fires could break out again,” he said.
The Riau Police also continued preventive measures through public outreach and monitoring of activities that could trigger fires. Residents were reminded not to clear or prepare land by burning.
They were also urged to immediately report any signs of fire, Akmadi said.
“Collaboration among local governments, the military and police, the disaster agency, Manggala Agni, businesses and communities remains key to preventing fires from recurring,” he said.

items.summary: PT Bank Tabungan Negara Tbk (BTN) is committed to helping complete President Prabowo Subianto’s Three Million ...
items.body_text:
BTN Commercial Banking Director Hermita said the program targets two housing-loan schemes: the Housing Financing Liquidity Facility (FLPP) and the Housing Program Credit (KPP).
“Previously, we focused only on FLPP. Now, there is KPP,” Hermita said in Palu, Central Sulawesi, on Sunday.
FLPP is a government-backed housing financing facility for low-income households, with interest subsidies making mortgage payments more affordable and fixed until the loans are fully repaid.
KPP, meanwhile, offers preferential interest rates to low-income communities, particularly micro, small, and medium enterprises. It provides affordable financing to expand businesses while supporting access to decent housing.
“With FLPP, you can only buy a house. With KPP, you can build or renovate an existing house, particularly for online businesses,” she said.
Of the 160,000 FLPP units allocated by the government, 78,000 had been realized as of September 2026, according to Hermita.
KPP, she said, is supported by an integrated ecosystem spanning housing construction through sales. KPP Supply provides government-backed working-capital or investment financing through banks such as BTN.
“The program targets housing developers, construction service providers or contractors, as well as building-material traders or suppliers,” she said.
BTN has also offered FLPP financing with terms of up to 40 years. The longer tenure enables lower monthly payments, while interest rates remain fixed throughout the loan period.
“This allows more people to benefit from the government’s subsidies,” she said.

items.title: Bagunas rues Alas’ lack of support in Asian Games; PNVF apologizes
items.summary: Bryan Bagunas reveals Alas Pilipinas players have not received their allowances since July, forcing some to miss practices during their Asian Games buildup due to financial constraints
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – Alas Pilipinas Men team captain Bryan Bagunas rued the lack of financial support in the lead-up to and during the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, revealing that some players were forced to borrow money just to attend training.
xBagunas voiced his frustration after the Philippines’ 25-16, 27-25, 25-22 tournament-opening loss to South Korea on Sunday, September 27.
The star outside spiker said the players have not received their allowances since July, forcing some to miss practices during their Asian Games buildup due to financial constraints.
“Regarding our allowance, even some of the players borrowed money from our teammates or other people just so they could get to training and travel back home. It was really tough for us to practice every day. Sometimes, we’re only seven or eight in training. It was really difficult,” said Bagunas in Filipino.
“I understand because most of the players are student-athletes. We just helped each other out so we could have complete attendance in practice.”
Although the Philippine Sports Commission provided allowances to the athletes, Bagunas said Alas Men players still have to pay for expenses out of their own pockets.
For instance, Bagunas and his teammates sometimes have to buy their own meals because the serving hours at their hotel often clashed with their training sessions.
“It is really disheartening because we’re representing the country. We do not feel the support that we deserve,” said Bagunas.
All Bagunas could do is encourage his teammates as Alas Men focuses on the task at hand, with matches against China and Chinese Taipei in Group D coming up on Monday, September 28, and Tuesday, September 29, respectively.
The Philippines needs a top-two finish in the group to advance to the quarterfinals.
“I just motivate them to keep fighting. Hopefully, we’ll get better support in the future,” Bagunas said.
The Philippine National Volleyball Federation apologized on Sunday following Bagunas’ remarks and explained its side, saying it continues to deal with “substantial financial liabilities and outstanding obligations” that the new administration headed by president Frank Lao inherited.
“We acknowledge the concerns raised by Mr. Bagunas in his recent interview. We recognize the sacrifices our athletes have made, including having to shoulder their own expenses and, in some instances, borrow money. This is a situation that no National Athlete should ever have to endure,” the PNVF said in a statement.
The PNVF also said that Lao gave Alas Men allowances and has advanced funds to address concerns raised by the teams competing in the quadrennial showpiece.
“Our national athletes deserve a federation that works just as hard for them as they battle for our country. Our athletes deserve better. Philippine volleyball deserves better. And we will work tirelessly to deliver better,” the PNVF said. – Rappler.com

items.title: DFA: Yes, PH delegation joined walkout during Netanyahu’s UN speech
items.summary: DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel says the Philippines takes part in a 'call for all parties to desist from unilateral actions that erode the conditions of peace and undermine the visibility of a future Palestine state'
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- The walkout was in response to Israel's actions in Gaza and the West Bank, as international scrutiny of these policies has intensified.
- The Philippines continues to advocate for a two-state solution as a means to achieve lasting peace in the region.
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines joined dozens of delegations that walked out of the United Nations General Assembly hall during Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s speech on Thursday, September 24, in New York, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said.
“Yes, the Philippines joined the walk out, in global solidarity for peace in the Middle East and the call for all parties to desist from unilateral actions that erode the conditions of peace and undermine the visibility of a future Palestine state,” DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel told Rappler on Sunday, September 27.
Reports showed that several delegates left the UN hall as Netanyahu took the podium — in protest over Israel’s actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
Netanyahu continued his address to a largely emptied chamber, where he defended Israel’s military operations and rejected accusations that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza. He also took aim at New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Western European leaders, Qatar, and Turkey, accusing them of backing or spreading what he described as false and hostile claims against Israel.
The walkout came as international scrutiny of Israel’s policies in the Palestinian territories intensified. A September 24 UN report highlighted settler violence, settlement expansion, displacement, and movement restrictions that continued to undermine prospects for a viable Palestinian state.
One focus has been Israel’s E1 settlement plan in the occupied West Bank. UN Secretary-General António Guterres said that advancing the E1 plan would deal a “deathblow” to the prospect of a contiguous and viable Palestinian state.
The DFA said the Philippines remains concerned about Israel’s actions in both Gaza and the West Bank.
“These actions are detrimental to finding a just, lasting and comprehensive solution to the Middle East conflict,” Ratonel said. “The Philippines has always supported the two-state solution as the viable path to peace in the region.” – Rappler.com

items.title: Sibol nails maiden Asian Games esports medal with Pokemon Unite bronze
items.summary: The Sibol Pokemon Unite team of Lance David, Ducke Harnold Leoncio, Lawrence Anthony Gatmaitan, Kim Rey Salazar, Robert Jon Mempin, and Michael Vaughn Ocio earn the Philippines' first-ever esports medal in the Asian Games
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines scored a breakthrough esports medal at the Asian Games as Sibol clinched a Pokemon Unite bronze at the Aichi Sky Expo in Japan on Sunday, September 27.
The team of Lance David, Ducke Harnold Leoncio, Lawrence Anthony Gatmaitan, Kim Rey Salazar, Robert Jon Mempin, and Michael Vaughn Ocio still secured a bronze despite a 2-0 loss to Indonesia in the semifinals.
Sibol built a commanding lead in the first game but ran out of steam, surrendering the opener and failing to recover as it fell to a sweep in the best-of-three affair.
Nevertheless, it was still a commendable result as the Philippines won its first-ever esports medal in the Asian Games, which included esports as a demonstration competition in 2018 then adopted it as a medal event in 2023.
“I’m still in awe because this is the first time and I’m really happy for the boys because this is something they’ll carry with them for the rest of their lives, that they were able to bring home a medal to the Philippines,” said Sibol head coach Albert Camp.
Sibol topped Group A with 4 points then scored a 2-0 win over Hong Kong in the quarterfinals to assure itself of a podium finish.
Another Sibol squad is guaranteed a medal as the Honor of Kings crew of Golden Hart Dajao, Justine Ritchie Tan, Charles Roman Esguerra, Dragon Hart Dajao, Jhon Mike Tungol, and Chammy Paul Nazarrea advanced to the semifinals following a 2-0 victory over South Korea.
Sibol battles China on Monday, September 28, for a spot in the gold-medal match. – Rappler.com

items.title: US backs Philippines, calls out China over ‘dangerous’ maneuvers at Ayungin
items.summary: The United States has slammed the China Coast Guard and the People’s Liberation Army Navy following a confrontation that forced the Philippines to suspend a routine resupply mission to the anchored BRP Sierra Madre.
items.body_text:
US backs Philippines, calls out China over ‘dangerous’ maneuvers at Ayungin
MANILA, Philippines — The United States has slammed the China Coast Guard and the People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) following a confrontation that forced the Philippines to suspend a routine resupply mission to the anchored BRP Sierra Madre.
In a statement on Sunday, September 27, US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton denounced Beijing's use of "dangerous blocking and other irresponsible maneuvers" near Ayungin Shoal on September 24.
“We stand by our Philippine Allies and laud their professionalism and restraint. We call on the China Coast Guard (CCG) and PLAN to cease the use of escalatory tactics that threaten the freedom of navigation and a free and open Indo-Pacific,” Lipton’s statement read.
On September 24, Chinese maritime forces blocked and interfered with a Philippine rotation-and-resupply mission to Ayungin Shoal, forcing Manila to suspend the operation without delivering supplies or rotating troops aboard the BRP Sierra Madre.
The Philippines sent a convoy that included Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) vessels BRP Malabrigo and BRP Cabra, plus a civilian supply boat, M/V Lapu-Lapu, to deliver food, fuel and other essentials and rotate personnel on the grounded BRP Sierra Madre.
According to the National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea and the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), CCG and PLAN warships obstructed the convoy near Ayungin.
PCG spokesperson Jay Tarriela said a CCG vessel performed “dangerous maneuvers” against M/V Lapu-Lapu that threatened a collision, prompting the mission’s suspension.
In response, the Chinese Embassy in Manila condemned the US Embassy’s pronouncement.
“We strongly condemn the US Embassy in the Philippines' disregard for right and wrong and its insistence on supporting the Philippines' provocative and unlawful actions at Ren'ai Reef in China's Nansha Qundao,” the Chinese Embassy in Manila said.
“China urges the US side to stop fanning the flames and refrain from actions that undermine regional peace and stability,” it added.
The West Philippine Sea encompasses the marine territories off the western coast of the Philippine archipelago, specifically the Luzon Sea, along with the waters surrounding the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, an arbitral tribunal at the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague invalidated Beijing's expansive South China Sea claims, ruling they were without legal foundation.
However, Beijing continues to reject the landmark international ruling.

items.title: Palace tells Sara Duterte to ‘level up’ defense over cash claims
items.summary: Malacañang called out Vice President Sara Duterte over her recent public statements, urging her to address the allegations raised against her with concrete evidence rather than resorting to personal attacks and rhetorical evasions.
items.body_text:
Palace tells Sara Duterte to ‘level up’ defense over cash claims
MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang called out Vice President Sara Duterte over her recent public statements, urging her to address the allegations raised against her with concrete evidence rather than resorting to personal attacks and rhetorical evasions.
This came after Duterte, in her statement, said she does not know former police officer Rodulfo Gracioso and accused the Marcos administration of being “desperate” to bring her down.
In a message to reporters, Palace Press Secretary Claire Castro advised her to familiarize herself with basic logical fallacies.
“Maturuan sana ang Bise Presidente na matuto siyang sumagot ng may ebidensiya sa mga inaakusa sa kanya bago magturo ng iba,” Castro said.
(Hopefully, the Vice President can learn to answer the accusations against her with evidence before pointing fingers at others.)
“Uulit-ulitin natin para tumimo sa isipan... She needs to level up her defending skills so she can appear credible, if only for once," she added.
(We will keep repeating this so it sinks in... She needs to level up her defending skills so she can appear credible, if only for once.)
Castro’s remarks came in response to Duterte, who had denied allegations that she knew or accepted money from Gracioso, a former security aide for then-House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco, while turning the accusations back against her critics.
“The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical,” Duterte said.
Gracioso previously alleged that he made more than 20 deliveries of cash-filled suitcases totaling more than P2 billion to Vice President Sara Duterte and over P1 billion to detained former President Rodrigo Duterte.
The National Bureau of Investigation said that it is currently probing Gracioso’s claims.
Meanwhile, Velasco’s lawyer dismissed Gracioso’s claims of alleged unlawful acts by Velasco and his wife, calling the claims fabricated, logically inconsistent, and contradicted by verifiable facts.

items.title: Philippine diplomats joined walkout on Netanyahu at UN, DFA confirms
items.summary: The Philippines was among delegates who walked out of the United Nations General Assembly hall during Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech on Friday, September 25, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs.
items.body_text:
Philippine diplomats joined walkout on Netanyahu at UN, DFA confirms
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines was among delegates who walked out of the United Nations General Assembly hall during Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech on Thursday, September 24, according to the Department of Foreign Affairs.
Clips of the session show dozens of delegates leaving their seats in protest and streaming out of the hall, just as Netanyahu stood at the podium to deliver his address.
Other delegates stayed seated, and some stood to applaud him amid repeated calls for order.
The available footage does not clearly show where the Philippine delegation was. With no official roll call, tallies compiled by news outlets and observers drew on video and photos of the hall, and some placed the Philippines among the delegations that stayed.
"The Philippines joined the walk out in global solidarity for peace in the Middle East and the call for all parties to desist from unilateral actions that erode the conditions of peace," DFA Spokesperson Analyn Ratonel told Philstar.com in a message.
The DFA spokesperson said such actions undermine the viability of a future Palestinian state.
"The Philippines is deeply concerned about the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and notes with alarm Israel's efforts to advance the E1 settlement plan, and the continued rise of settler violence in the West Bank," the DFA spokesperson said.
"These actions are detrimental to finding a just, lasting and comprehensive solution to the Middle East conflict," she added.
The Philippines "has always supported the two-state solution as the viable path to peace in the region," the DFA spokesperson said.
Before the speech by the Israeli leader, the Palestinian Mission to the UN had urged member states to fill the hall with staff and leave together once Netanyahu was introduced, according to reports.
The mission urged member states to show their objection to what it described as Israel's genocide, war crimes and illegal occupation.
Netanyahu, who visibly paused before he began his speech, reacted to the throngs of delegates leaving the hall by inviting "any other moral cowards who haven't yet left this hall" to go.
The Israeli leader's UN General Assembly speeches also drew walkouts in 2024 and 2025.
A week before Netanyahu's UN address, the DFA issued a similar statement protesting Israel's E1 settlement plan on September 17.
In that statement, the department said Israel's push to advance the E1 plan and the rise in settler violence "may contravene international law."
It also said Manila would continue to uphold the Palestinian people's right to self-determination.

items.title: Sneaker billionaire behind the biggest university gift in US history gives his alma mater $1B
items.summary: Nike co-founder Phil Knight and his wife, Penny, have pledged US$1 billion to the University of Oregon to create an engineering college, the largest known gift to a U.S. public flagship university.
items.body_text:
The university announced the gift on Sept. 23. Paid over 10 years, it will cover a new building on the Knight Campus in Eugene, faculty hiring and the college's running costs in perpetuity, Knight Campus executive director Robert Guldberg told reporters that day, local news site Lookout Eugene-Springfield reported.
The college will train engineers and applied scientists in bioengineering and other high-demand fields, recruit leading researchers and shorten the path from lab discoveries to marketable products, the university said.
The university currently offers only engineering minors and graduate programs. Officials told The New York Times that building a full undergraduate program will take about a decade.
Guldberg said the Knight Campus expects its faculty to grow from 17 to 42 and its roughly 500 students to more than double.
University President Karl Scholz told The New York Times the gift was tremendous news at a time when "we're all feeling a little bit under siege."
The pledge lands as the university prepares to cut about $65 million from its budget over the coming years, largely because fewer out-of-state students, who pay far higher tuition than Oregon residents, are enrolling, public radio station KLCC reported.
In a May campus message, Scholz traced the decline to factors ranging from demographic shifts and economic uncertainty to a political environment that is weighing on international enrollment.
In his Sept. 23 message announcing the gift, he noted that the money is earmarked for engineering and does not resolve the university's structural deficit.
Knight, 88, graduated from the university in 1959. The pledge brings his family's known giving to the school to more than $2 billion, The New York Times reported.
That total includes two $500 million gifts, in 2016 and 2021, that built and expanded the Knight Campus.
In a statement released by the university, Knight said he and Penny were "grateful for the chance to invest in our most promising young people's future."
Among the largest gifts to U.S. public universities before this one were an anonymous $550 million gift to Western Michigan University in 2021 and $500 million from the Simons Foundation to Stony Brook University in 2023, according to The Chronicle of Higher Education's list of major gifts.
The Knights' own $2 billion pledge in 2025 to the Knight Cancer Institute at Oregon Health & Science University, Oregon's public academic health center, remains the largest gift ever made to an American university. It surpassed Michael Bloomberg's $1.8 billion gift to Johns Hopkins University in 2018.

items.title: Thousands sleep in schools as floods hit 52,000 homes in Bangkok
items.summary: Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.
items.body_text:
Nearly 4,900 people have been evacuated to shelters, with around 52,000 households affected by the floods, which prompted a disaster declaration across the capital, according to the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA).
More than 330 mm (13 inches) of rain fell in some areas of the city between Thursday and Sunday, the weather agency said.
Thailand is used to wet weather and September is the peak of the rainy season, but several Bangkok residents said this year seemed worse.
"Our house was underwater for about 30 hours," office worker Kosin Nilset, who lives along the Premprachakorn canal on the outskirts of the capital, told AFP on Sunday morning.
"This time, the water level is higher than the 2011 flood," the 44-year-old said.
Widespread deluges across the Southeast Asian country in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.
Kosin and his family lifted their belongings once they saw the water level was higher than the canal retaining wall, but their ground floor was still left soaked.
"At least tap water and electricity are working," Kosin said, as he used a broom to sweep out water.
Pedestrians in plastic rain ponchos trudged through murky floodwaters in Bangkok's east -- knee-deep in some areas of a grocery store parking lot -- floating their belongings in plastic tubs alongside them, AFP journalists saw.
'Sleeping on the table'
Water levels in Bangkok's network of canals remained high on Sunday morning, with authorities working to speed up drainage, the BMA said.
More rain was forecast throughout Sunday for Bangkok and its surrounding provinces, but would begin to taper off on Monday, it said.
Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events will increase as the planet continues to heat up because of fossil fuel emissions.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said several roads were still flooded and warned Bangkok residents in a Facebook Live post to avoid unnecessary travel.
Bangkok was the world's most-visited city in 2025, with an estimated 30.3 million international arrivals, according to Euromonitor International's Top 100 City Destinations Index.
Chadchart visited a temporary shelter on Saturday night in a school in the Kheha Romklao area, where he said about 1,000 people were evacuated.
Some rested on cots and benches with their dogs in hallways, while others lay with blankets on the floors of classrooms where desks and chairs were pushed to the side.
Hundreds of city schools will be closed on Monday, according to the BMA.
Some convenience stores had empty shelves over the weekend as residents raced to buy essentials.
The prime minister's office asked the public to avoid panic-buying and warned that price gouging was a criminal offence.
Thidarat Silsuwan, 56, lives alone in her partially submerged house along the Premprachakorn canal.
"I have been sleeping on the table for two days now," she told AFP.
She did not want to go to a shelter as she worked to clean up and salvage her belongings.
"I tried to lift everything up, but I gave up on large electric appliances like the refrigerator and washing machine. I guess they are broken."

items.title: Wealthy Chinese parents turn to US surrogacy for American-born children
items.summary: A California surrogacy agency serving wealthy Chinese parents is under scrutiny after a surrogate learned that her baby is intended for a Chinese billionaire reported to have more than 100 U.S.-born children.
items.body_text:
The woman, identified only as Judy, said in a CBS News report aired Sept. 13 that she signed with Irvine-based surrogacy agency Patriot Conceptions after seeing an Instagram ad offering $120,000, and was told the intended parent was a single father hoping to expand his family.
Leaked documents obtained by CBS named the father as Xu Bo, a video game executive. Judy said the agency told her he had hired close to two dozen surrogates, and that she asked to meet him several times but never did. "I feel blindsided. I feel misled," she said.
A former partner of Xu has claimed he fathered as many as 300 children. His company, Duoyi Network, disputed that figure but told The Wall Street Journal in December 2025 that he has "only a little over 100" through U.S. surrogacy. Xu told a closed Los Angeles court hearing in 2023 that he wanted about 20 U.S.-born children to inherit his business, the Journal reported.
Patriot Conceptions said in a Sept. 17 statement that it facilitated Judy's surrogacy but was not Xu's only agency, and that her concerns deserve to be taken seriously. It also told CBS it had encouraged her to end the contract, which she denies.
The agency, founded in 2019 by Haotian Bai, a 37-year-old U.S. Army veteran born in China, charges intended parents a base price of $120,000 to $200,000, while surrogates receive $60,000 to $120,000, the New York Post reported on Sept. 21.
In a profile on the U.S. Chamber of Commerce website, Bai said the company had helped thousands of parents and that 40% of its clients were international. The Post's review of the company's promotional materials suggested those clients are almost entirely Chinese.
The company's website comes in Chinese and English and directs prospective clients to WeChat. It also maps 25 states it rates as broadly supportive for securing a child's U.S. citizenship, marking only Louisiana, which bans paid surrogacy, as restrictive.
Bai told the Post the company does not disclose client demographics but records intended parents' nationality at intake and shares it with surrogates during matching. A parent's foreign nationality, he said, "does not by itself establish that obtaining citizenship is the purpose of an arrangement."
Bai came to the U.S. around 2012 from China's Lanzhou University to study for a master's degree at Iowa State University, then joined the Army under a program that fast-tracked green cards for non-citizen recruits, sources told the Post. He later held a 2024-2025 veteran fellowship at Stanford University's Hoover Institution.
In 2018, while working as a real estate agent in Hawaii, Bai was hired by China-based placement firms to arrange internships at the state legislature for Chinese students whose families paid the firms $5,000 to $6,000 each, Hawaii News Now reported at the time. Then-House Speaker Scott Saiki shut the program down amid allegations that students were exploited. Bai denied selling the internships and faced no charges, according to the Post.
Such arrangements hinge on the 14th Amendment, which grants citizenship to nearly everyone born on U.S. soil. The Supreme Court reaffirmed that guarantee on June 30, striking down President Donald Trump's 2025 executive order restricting birthright citizenship.
Trump signed a new order on Aug. 6 that denies recognition of citizenship in several new categories, including, according to immigration lawyers, cases in which parents pay a surrogate to give birth in the U.S. A federal judge in Maryland blocked it on Sept. 2 for a class of children covered by an existing lawsuit, calling the order "almost certainly unconstitutional" as applied to them, The Hill reported.
Emory University researchers found in a 2024 study published in Fertility and Sterility that 32% of the 40,177 embryo transfers to U.S. surrogates from 2014 to 2020 were for foreign intended parents, a share that climbed from 22% in 2014 to nearly 40% in 2019. Chinese nationals accounted for 41.7% of those foreign clients.
Nathan Zha

items.title: Luggage chaos, flight delays at Suvarnabhumi airport
items.summary: Passengers arriving at Suvarnabhumi airport have been forced to wait five or six hours for their baggage and numerous flights have been delayed since Saturday because of problems with Thai Airways’ ground operations.
items.body_text:
Passengers arriving at Suvarnabhumi airport have been forced to wait five or six hours for their baggage and numerous flights have been delayed since Saturday because of problems with Thai Airways’ ground operations.
The disruptions began on Sept 26 and continued into Sunday, leaving many passengers and their luggage stranded at the airport.
Suvarnabhumi airport said on Sunday that it had received complaints from Thai Airways passengers about delayed departures, as well as from arriving passengers who had faced lengthy waits to collect their baggage.
An investigation found that flooding in several areas had affected the ability of ground-handling staff employed by Thai Airways International Plc to travel to work. As a result, the airline had insufficient ground staff to handle its operations.
The situation was compounded by malfunctions involving some of Thai Airways’ baggage carts, which further disrupted ground-handling operations for both departing flights and the unloading of baggage from arriving flights.
The problems resulted in delays to some departing flights, while passengers arriving at Suvarnabhumi had to wait significantly longer than usual for their luggage. Baggage from several flights was also left behind at the airport.
Suvarnabhumi airport said it was working urgently with Thai Airways to increase its ground-handling workforce, repair the faulty baggage carts and provide replacement equipment to speed up the handling and transportation of delayed baggage.
The airport has also coordinating with the airline to display baggage status information on airport screens and make regular announcements in baggage-claim areas so passengers could keep track of their luggage.
The airport said it had redirected staff to baggage-claim and service areas to assist passengers, provide information and coordinate with the airline to address the disruption.
It advise passengers requiring assistance to call the AOT 24-hour contact centre on 1722.

items.title: Bangkok floods force thousands into shelters
items.summary: BANGKOK - Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.
items.body_text:
BANGKOK - Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.
Nearly 4,900 people have been evacuated to shelters, with around 52,000 households affected by the floods, which prompted a disaster declaration across the capital, according to the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA).
More than 330 millimetres (13 inches) of rain fell in some areas of the city between Thursday and Sunday, the weather agency said.
Thailand is used to wet weather and September is the peak of the rainy season, but several Bangkok residents said this year seemed worse.
"Our house was underwater for about 30 hours," office worker Kosin Nilset, who lives along the Premprachakorn canal on the outskirts of the capital, told AFP on Sunday morning.
"This time, the water level is higher than the 2011 flood," the 44-year-old said.
Widespread deluges across the Southeast Asian country in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.
Kosin and his family lifted their belongings once they saw the water level was higher than the canal retaining wall, but their ground floor was still left soaked.
"At least tap water and electricity are working," Kosin said, as he used a broom to sweep out water.
Pedestrians in plastic rain ponchos trudged through murky floodwaters in Bangkok's east -- knee-deep in some areas of a grocery store parking lot -- floating their belongings in plastic tubs alongside them, AFP journalists saw.
- 'Sleeping on the table' -
Water levels in Bangkok's network of canals remained high on Sunday morning, with authorities working to speed up drainage, the BMA said.
More rain was forecast throughout Sunday for Bangkok and its surrounding provinces, but would begin to taper off on Monday, it said.
Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events will increase as the planet continues to heat up because of fossil fuel emissions.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said several roads were still flooded and warned Bangkok residents in a Facebook Live post to avoid unnecessary travel.
Chadchart visited a temporary shelter on Saturday night in a school in the Kheha Romklao area, where he said about 1,000 people were evacuated.
Some rested on cots and benches with their dogs in hallways, while others lay with blankets on the floors of classrooms where desks and chairs were pushed to the side.
Hundreds of city schools will be closed on Monday, according to the BMA.
Some convenience stores had empty shelves over the weekend as residents raced to buy essentials.
The prime minister's office asked the public to avoid panic-buying and warned that price gouging was a criminal offence.
Thidarat Silsuwan, 56, lives alone in her partially submerged house along the Premprachakorn canal.
"I have been sleeping on the table for two days now," she told AFP.
She did not want to go to a shelter as she worked to clean up and salvage her belongings.
"I tried to lift everything up, but I gave up on large electric appliances like the refrigerator and washing machine. I guess they are broken."

items.title: Schoolboy hailed for clearing rubbish from flooded city street
items.summary: Amid heavy flooding in Bangkok, a schoolboy's simple act of civic-mindedness has drawn widespread praise online after he was filmed wading through murky water to collect floating rubbish before it could clog the drains.
items.body_text:
Amid heavy flooding in Bangkok, a schoolboy's simple act of civic-mindedness has drawn widespread praise online after he was filmed wading through murky water to collect floating rubbish before it could clog the drains.
The clip, posted on TikTok by user Ndphk on Saturday, quickly drew attention on social media. The uploader accompanied the footage with a short caption expressing admiration for the boy's actions.
The video was recorded in flooded Soi On Nut 17 during rain on Saturday. The water level had risen nearly halfway up car wheels, and numerous rubbish bags could be seen drifting with the current.
Against that backdrop, the boy stopped beside the flooded road, set down his school bag and umbrella, and began picking up floating rubbish bags. He then carried the waste to a nearby bin, preventing it from being swept into drains and removing obstacles from the flooded roadway.
His simple action struck a chord with many viewers, who flooded the comments section with praise.
Many commended not only the boy but also his parents and teachers for instilling a sense of civic responsibility and concern for the wider community.
"His parents have raised him really well. Admirable," one commenter wrote, while also encouraging the youngster to take care of his health after wading through dirty floodwater.
Others said the fact that he acted without being prompted reflected strong public-minded values and consideration for others.
As the clip gained traction online, many commenters described the youngster as a "little hero" for his efforts during the flooding.

items.title: Bangkok and three neighbouring provinces get two‑day holiday as Thailand ramps up flood response
items.summary: BANGKOK, Sept 27 — Thailand has declared September 28 and 29 as special public holidays in Bangkok and three neigh...
items.body_text:
BANGKOK, Sept 27 — Thailand has declared September 28 and 29 as special public holidays in Bangkok and three neighbouring provinces as authorities step up flood response efforts following days of heavy rain that that inundated parts of the capital.
Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said the holidays would apply to Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani and Samut Prakan to ease the impact of the floods and facilitate public travel.
“The special holidays were approved at a special Cabinet meeting today to help ease the impact of the floods and facilitate public travel,” he told reporters after the meeting at Government House today.
Anutin said further rain was forecast in the Central and Eastern regions, while Bangkok was expected to receive light to moderate rain.
He instructed provincial governors to closely monitor affected areas and ensure personnel, machinery and vehicles were deployed promptly where needed.
The government was also preparing temporary shelters, food, relief supplies and medical facilities for flood-affected residents, he said.
Anutin also instructed governors to promptly declare disaster-affected areas where necessary and seek additional emergency funds through the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) if conditions worsened.
In Bangkok, rainfall has eased since Saturday night, but many areas remain inundated, with several major roads inaccessible, particularly in the eastern and northern parts of the capital towards Don Mueang Airport and along Phetchaburi Road in the city centre.
Several vehicles were also stranded on flooded roads. — Bernama

items.title: Bomb squad examines vehicles as UK counter‑terror police probe incident near RAF Fairford
items.summary: LONDON, Sept 27 — British counter-terrorism police today were reportedly probing a major incident near a base used...
items.body_text:
LONDON, Sept 27 — British counter-terrorism police today were reportedly probing a major incident near a base used by the US air force after several men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences.
Villagers were evacuated and army bomb disposal experts were “currently examining a number of vehicles”, police in the southwestern county of Gloucestershire said in a statement.
Several UK media including the BBC and Sky News reported that the counter-terrorism force was leading the investigation into the incident near RAF Fairford, but that was not immediately confirmed to AFP.
A cordon is in place and officers believed the incident had been “contained”.
In March, then prime minister Keir Starmer granted permission for “defensive” US action against Iranian missile sites from two UK bases including Fairford.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being kept updated on the incident, a government spokesperson said.
“We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe,” the spokesperson said.
“It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing.”
Defence Minister Wes Streeting thanked “emergency and specialist teams” deployed to the scene.
“We can be reassured that this is being dealt with,” he said on X.
Media reported a large emergency services presence in the area including a Hazardous Area Response Team.
“A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident,” Gloucestershire Police said.
Several men had been arrested “on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act”, the force added.
Villagers evacuated
Residents from the nearby village of Whelford had been evacuated to a nearby leisure centre, the BBC said.
The village of Whelford is located adjacent to the Royal Air Force Fairford base which is also used by the United States Air Force.
Fairford is the UK base of the 501st Combat Support Wing, a US air force administrative support wing.
It said in a statement that no US air force personnel had been involved in the incident.
“The 501st Combat Support Wing appreciates the swift response and continued support of our local law enforcement partners,” it said.
“We remain in close coordination with our UK partners to help ensure the safety and security of both our military and local communities,” it added.
The MP for the area, Roz Savage, described the situation as “worrying”.
“I have contacted the police for further updates and I’ve been told that it is believed the incident is contained,” she said on X.
The incident comes amid concerns about the actions of hostile foreign states.
Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood has accused Iran and Russia of using proxies to carry out criminal activities on their behalf on UK territory.
Earlier this month, reports said British military sites were targeted by drones more than 300 times over the past year.
Britain’s defence ministry did not disclose who was behind the drone activity, but the figures come as European countries warned of an increase in suspected Russian hybrid operations on their territory.
UK armed forces minister Louise Sandher-Jones told AFP in a statement that the government was “taking the threat posed by hostile drones to defence sites extremely seriously”. — AFP

items.title: Iran Guards claim capture of US underwater drone in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 27 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said today that they seized an American submarine drone in the...
items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 27 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said today that they seized an American submarine drone in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has blockaded in the months-long Middle East war.
“Through a coordinated, complex operation involving intelligence oversight and electronic warfare, IRGC naval forces’ personnel successfully captured an advanced unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) belonging to the terrorist US military,” the IRGC naval forces said in a statement, according to state TV.
They added that the drone was “operating in the Strait of Hormuz for espionage purposes”, identifying the model as a Remus 600 autonomous underwater vehicle that was “now in the hands of the force’s specialists for data recovery”.
Earlier this month, the Guards said they captured another US submarine drone in the strait that was crucial for oil and gas trade before the Middle East war started in late February and choked off shipping.
Iran has maintained a blockade of the Hormuz strait since the outbreak of the conflict, while the United States has imposed a counter-blockade of Iranian ports. — AFP

items.title: Games-Organisers fend off bed-size complaints in Nagoya
items.body_text:
Games-Organisers fend off bed-size complaints in Nagoya
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept 27 : It was never going to be a bed of roses when container-style blocks were used to house athletes, but Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games organisers said using ottomans as extensions could have brought more comfort to taller competitors.
Complaints about cramped rooms and small beds surfaced on social media from athletes staying in the modular units, adding to the woes of the organisers, who have drawn flak for not building a traditional Athletes' Village.
On Sunday, media were given a peek inside the container-style athletes' accommodation at the Garden Pier that looked like a minimalist Lego city.
The wood-lined rooms looked compact and the beds appeared short — especially for typically tall basketball players — though a separate, spacious dining hall and a shop selling basic necessities aimed to offset the squeeze.
South Korea have already moved their men's basketball team into standard hotels, but Yuta Matsuo, deputy director of the Games' athlete accommodation section, and his team braved rain to explain the "sustainable" rationale behind the setup.
"The most requests we have received was about the size of the bed, particularly from the basketball players and other athletes with larger physiques," Matsuo told reporters.
"When there were more beds and more people staying in the rooms, they felt the space was rather cramped.
"We had thought that the bed extension, ottomans, could be used effectively to make better use of the available space. However, we could have done a better job of explaining how these tools could be used, because they may not have been used as effectively as we had hoped.
"Going forward, we would like to improve the way we communicate what these items are for and how they can be used, so that we can provide the athletes with a more comfortable environment during their stay."
The organisers are also using a cruise ship and hotels to accommodate 17,000 athletes and officials who have descended on the port city.
"It is becoming increasingly difficult in Japan to develop entirely new facilities," Matsuo said, referring to the absence of a dedicated Athletes' Village.
"So in terms of how to make the most effective use of existing facilities while ensuring that they properly meet the needs of the athletes, we hope to continue making improvements in these areas."
Coach of the Mongolian women's basketball team Javier Garcia Alvarez has been critical of the accommodations.
"Especially for basketball players who are like 185, 190 centimetres, it's not easy," Alvarez told Reuters.
"When you are coming to these villages and they are like this, I mean, you have to adapt to this. It's almost like camping, it's like a camp."
India used similar units for some of their athletes to acclimatise for the continental showpiece.
(Editing by Christian Radnedge)

items.title: Australia hold on to beat South Africa with 11 men in Perth
items.body_text:
Australia hold on to beat South Africa with 11 men in Perth
SYDNEY, Sept 27 : Australia held on with 11 men in a dramatic finish to beat a second-string South Africa outfit 42-38 at Perth Stadium on Sunday and extend their unbeaten run to five games since new coach Les Kiss took over in late July.
Skipper Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan, Joseph Suaalii and Hunter Paisami were all shown yellow cards in the last 10 minutes as the world champions cut a 25-point deficit down to four at the final whistle.
Australia had looked to be cruising after centre Len Ikitau's double and tries from flyhalf Ben Donaldson, number eight Wilson and winger Max Jorgensen combined with 17 points from the boot of scrumhalf Ryan Lonergan gave them a 42-17 lead after 65 minutes.
The last 10 minutes threatened to undo all their earlier good work but the Wallabies will move on to back-to-back tests against the All Blacks in October without a loss in six games, their best unbeaten run since 2017.
"I'm so proud of the group," said Wilson. "We versed the world champions in our own backyard here. Jeez, that was a crazy last 10 minutes, but that first 70 minutes, the way we played, we implemented our game plan in exactly the way we wanted."
South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus had made 13 changes to his lineup from the team which completed the gruelling 3-1 series victory over New Zealand earlier this month but stacked his bench with first-choice players as an insurance policy.
It almost paid off in the frantic last 10 minutes, but scores from hooker Johan Grobbelaar, winger Edwill van der Merwe, scrumhalf Morne van den Berg, prop Ox Nche as well as a penalty try were not quite enough.
"Australia is always a hard team to beat, and such a good game to play," said Springboks captain Andre Esterhuizen.
"It was a pretty intense game and quite quick for a test match, but they capitalised on all our errors, and I think discipline let us down, especially in that first half."
The visitors scored the first try after Handre Pollard and Lonergan had exchanged early penalties with Grobbelaar rolling over the line on the back of a rolling maul.
Australia responded with two tries from Ikitau in three minutes, the first from close range and the second after winger Suaalii had disrupted the restart and the ball bounced back to the lurking centre.
The Springboks responded almost immediately to lock up the scores again at 17-17, flyhalf Pollard's long pass exposing a hole in the Australian backline defence and Van der Merwe showing his pace to finish the move.
A slanted crosskick from Wallabies fullback Tom Wright gave Jorgensen some space to run shortly before halftime, however, and Australia recycled patiently when the winger was held up shy of the line with Donaldson going over unopposed in the corner after 14 phases.
Lonergan extended Australia's lead with his second penalty eight minutes into the second half, prompting Erasmus to bring on all eight of his replacements, and added a third three-pointer after 54 minutes to make it 30-17.
The Wallabies were now taking the Springboks on up front and tapped a penalty close to the line just before the hour mark with Wilson forcing his way over and slapping the ball down for a try.
The Springboks stormed back to try and cut the 20-point deficit but when Canan Moodie spilled the ball, Jorgensen was on hand to scoop it up and sprint 60 metres for Australia's fifth try.

items.summary: "No credit card or bank account information is at risk," the telco said.
items.body_text:
More than 23,500 Simba customers affected in data breach involving IC numbers, birth dates
"No credit card or bank account information is at risk," the telco said.
SINGAPORE: Telecommunications company Simba has suffered a data breach affecting 23,549 customers, involving names, identity card numbers and dates of birth.
Based on the company's investigations so far, the data affected also included mobile numbers and email addresses of customers who had registered for Simba's services.
In a statement on Friday (Sep 25), Simba said it had discovered the incident a day earlier and had since resolved it.
No credit card or bank account information is "at risk", the company said.
The company added that there was currently no indication that any of the affected data had been "maliciously misused".
"Simba is treating this incident seriously and have swiftly resolved it.
"We have also taken immediate and appropriate actions to review existing security measures to protect core infrastructure and systems," it said, adding that it was working with the relevant authorities on the incident.
The company is also progressively notifying affected customers via email, with the process expected to be completed within the next week.
In response to CNA's queries, the Personal Data Protection Commission said it was aware of the incident and was investigating.
