items.title: Swiss voters reject bid to enshrine stricter neutrality by big margin
items.summary: Result allows the government to continue applying the doctrine pragmatically.
items.body_text:
Swiss voters reject bid to enshrine stricter neutrality by big margin
- Swiss voters rejected a proposal to enshrine stricter neutrality in the constitution, allowing the government to maintain flexible interpretation and sanctions against Russia.
- The initiative aimed to make neutrality "eternal and armed", ban military alliances, and block non-UN sanctions, but received only about 31% support.
- The vote preserves current policy favouring sanctions on Russia and pragmatic neutrality, reflecting public approval of government actions despite opposition from the Swiss People’s Party.
AI generated
Swiss voters rejected a bid to enshrine stricter neutrality in the constitution, preserving the government’s freedom to interpret the doctrine flexibly and maintain sanctions against Russia.
The initiative received about 31 per cent support, with 69 per cent voting against it, according to early government results on Sept 27 as ballots were still being counted. The outcome broadly matched final polls.
While Swiss neutrality has been internationally recognised since the end of the Napoleonic wars in 1815, how the government implements it is not spelt out.
The proposal would have declared Switzerland’s neutrality “eternal and armed”, barred the country from joining military alliances and prevented it from imposing sanctions not approved by the United Nations.
The initiative was a response to Switzerland’s decision to mirror European Union sanctions against Russia following its 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Supporters argued that the move breached the country’s neutrality – a view echoed by Moscow, which urged Swiss voters to back the proposal.
The government, Parliament and all major parties except the right-wing Swiss People’s Party (SVP), opposed the initiative. Former SVP leader Christoph Blocher spent 2 million francs (S$3.1 million) campaigning for it.
“Switzerland has not had a war for 200 years because it is permanently armed and neutral,” said the billionaire businessman.
“But neutrality has been followed less and less in recent years,” he said, with Russia now seeing Switzerland as a party to the conflict because of the sanctions.
The vote was not a verdict on neutrality itself, which remains widely supported. Instead, it preserves the government’s ability to apply the doctrine pragmatically rather than bind it via stricter constitutional rules.
Fabio Wasserfallen, a professor of European politics at the University of Bern, said: “Swiss voters like neutrality, but they approve of how the government is implementing it at present.
“They are also generally in favour of the sanctions on Russia over the war in Ukraine and don’t want that to change.”
It is the second SVP-backed initiative voters have rejected in 2026. In June, they turned down a proposal to cap Switzerland’s population at 10 million. Under the country’s system of direct democracy, voters can be called to the polls up to four times a year.
In a separate ballot on Sept 27, voters also rejected a plan to produce more food locally. The proposal, which would have indirectly reduced domestic meat production, received just 24 per cent support. BLOOMBERG, REUTERS

items.title: Deputy chair of Turkey's AK Party resigns after trading allegation amid funds crisis
items.summary: ANKARA, Sept 27 - A deputy chair of President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party stepped down after an opposition politician accused her of making a large profit on shares just before a funds crisis triggered a major selloff on the country's stock market.
items.body_text:
Deputy chair of Turkey's AK Party resigns after trading allegation amid funds crisis
ANKARA, Sept 27 - A deputy chair of President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party stepped down after an opposition politician accused her of making a large profit on shares just before a funds crisis triggered a major selloff on the country's stock market.
Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya, the AK Party's deputy chair responsible for social policies and who also served as family minister from 2016 to 2018, said late on Saturday she had asked Erdogan to relieve her of all her duties so the allegations could be investigated.
Main opposition Yeni Party spokesman Zeynel Emre alleged at a press conference on Saturday that Kaya and her husband, Ilyas Kaya, invested a combined 163 million lira ($3.3 million) in April this year mainly in shares of shipbuilder Ozata Denizcilik and later received about 2.17 billion lira ($44 million) from selling them.
Ozata Denizcilik shares traded at around 220 lira at the start of April and rose to 4,980 lira on September 15, before turmoil in Turkey's investment fund industry, as suspected share-price manipulation in thinly traded stocks triggered a liquidity crisis and sent share prices tumbling on September 16.
Emre alleged the timing of the transactions raised questions.
Kaya said on X that she considered it necessary to take political responsibility while the allegations were examined and asked Erdogan, to relieve her of all the posts she holds.
She did not comment further on the specifics of the allegation.
Turkish authorities took steps last week to support financial stability after some investment funds failed to meet withdrawals from almost half a million investors amid the selloff.
Ozata Denizcilik said in a regulatory filing on Friday that its chairman, Ozdemir Ataseven, and vice chairman, Gokhan Ataseven, had been jailed pending trial as part of an ongoing investigation into the funds crisis. REUTERS

items.title: British PM Burnham pledges to offer social care reform at next election
items.summary: He said it would be free at the point of use, with the cost spread across the population.
items.body_text:
British PM Burnham pledges to offer social care reform at next election
LONDON – British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged on Sept 27 to present his proposal to tackle Britain’s social care crisis at the next national election, saying it would be free at the point of use, with the cost spread across the population.
At the beginning of his first Labour Party conference as Prime Minister, Burnham used an interview with the BBC to set out his plans for social care, a pricey issue he said resonated for him after his father died earlier in September in a care home.
Yet, despite saying it was one of his priorities, the former Manchester mayor said he would not present his social care plans until the next national election, due by mid-2029, offering some relief to a government wanting to avoid the prospect of major tax rises.
Burnham promises to ‘rip the plaster off’
“I am going to go show leadership on this issue... I won’t dodge the difficult questions. I am going to rip the plaster off, if I can put it that way, because someone has to do it,” he said.
“I will put that plan to the public at a general election. That will be where the plan gets tested... I am prepared to put myself in that position recognising it may be difficult or unpopular with some.”
Several British prime ministers have tried, and failed, to reform social care, a system which often sees those being looked after in care homes having to sell their property or get into debt to cover sky-high costs.
Burnham was reticent over how he would exactly fund his plans, but by delaying social care reform until the next election, he has offered his finance minister, John Healey, a bit of room for manoeuvre before the budget on Oct 28.
Instead, Burnham wants the conference in the English city of Liverpool to inspire a sense of hope for a party, which under his predecessor Keir Starmer had seen its popularity plummet.
Emphasising what he described as the good news stories in Britain, with the cities of Liverpool and Manchester showing healthy economic growth rates, Burnham will know there are equally difficult decisions coming down the track.
The cost of borrowing is at high levels, the welfare Bill is ballooning, energy costs are rising and Burnham and Healey need to fill a £4.7 billion (S$7.96 billion) gap in the Defence Investment Plan, a blueprint that some defence experts say does not go far enough in meeting Britain’s promise to increase defence spending.
Burnham said his desire first is to ease the pressure on the country, where many are suffering with the cost of living.
“I want the job because of what I can do with the job, and people won’t be in any doubt about what I am trying to do,” he said. “I am here to end a decade of drift and division that we’ve had since Brexit.” REUTERS

items.title: US’ Taiwan policy unchanged: envoy
items.body_text:
- 
            US’ Taiwan policy unchanged: envoy‘STATUS QUO’: ‘There’s no change in the Taiwan policy here,’ the US ambassador to China said, adding that the US is not changing its language or position on the issue
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 US policy toward Taiwan has not changed following talks between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平), Washington’s top envoy to Beijing said on Friday, a day after the two leaders met at the White House. “There’s no change in the Taiwan policy here,” US Ambassador to China David Perdue told CNBC in an interview aired on Friday morning when asked about the possibility that Xi might have tried to persuade Trump to soften his stance on Taiwan. Trump is “fully committed to the one China policy,” Perdue said, adding that the US remains committed to the Taiwan Relations Act, the Three Joint Communiques and the Six Assurances. US Ambassador to China David Perdue speaks during CNBC’s Squawk Box aired yesterday.Photo: Screen grab from CNBC Television’s YouTube channel “Nothing has changed there,” he said. “We’re not changing the language. We’re not changing our position there. We want peace across the [Taiwan] Strait. We don’t want coercion. We don’t support independence.” Perdue said Washington believed Xi had received that message, adding that Trump had “shown respect and listened to their side of that argument.” Taiwan was among the closely watched issues during Thursday’s Trump-Xi meeting, and the two leaders did not respond to reporters’ questions afterward on whether the issue had been discussed. According to the White House fact sheet on Xi’s visit, issued on Friday, the two leaders discussed bilateral trade and investment, geopolitical flashpoints, including Russia, North Korea and Iran, as well as drug control. Taiwan is notably absent from the White House fact sheet, unlike the readout published by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. According to China’s readout, Xi stressed China’s “clear cut” position on safeguarding “national reunification” and “territorial integrity.” “It is hoped that the US side will adhere to the correct position of opposing Taiwan independence, and handle the Taiwan question with caution, so as to lay a solid foundation for China-US strategic cooperation and the development of bilateral relations,” the readout said. Trump has not publicly “opposed” Taiwanese independence, instead saying in May in an interview while visiting Beijing that he was not “looking to have somebody go independent” as he urged Beijing and Taipei to “cool down.” According to the White House fact sheet, the two leaders “recalled that United States and China were allies in World War II and fought side by side to win the war.” China’s readout does not mention the remark, but it was included in a report published by Xinhua on the same day. Taipei has rebuked that stance and accused Xi of distorting historical facts. The Mainland Affairs Council and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs have stressed that it was the Republic of China, whose government relocated from China to Taiwan in 1949 after the Chinese Civil War, that fought alongside US forces in World War II. However, Taipei has not publicly responded to the White House’s fact sheet. Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan (彭麗媛), on Friday concluded their three-day state visit to the US after having tea with Trump and US first lady Melania Trump at the White House and visiting the US National Archives. items.title: Allied nations call for Taiwan’s inclusion in UN
items.body_text:
- 
            Allied nations call for Taiwan’s inclusion in UNPLEA: How the UN addresses Taiwan’s security issue would be a test of its strength and relevance, Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine told the UN General Assembly
  - By Fion Khan / Staff writer, with CNA
 Only Taiwan’s elected government can represent the people of Taiwan, Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said on Friday at the UN General Assembly, calling for the nation’s inclusion in the UN. Taiwan and its 23 million people are a reality, and only its democratically elected government can represent it, Heine said when addressing the 81st session of the UN General Assembly General Debate. Appropriate ways must be found for Taiwan’s substantive participation in UN meetings if the UN is to be truly inclusive and effective in years to come, she said. Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine, bottom, addresses the 81st UN General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City on Friday.Photo: Reuters UN member states would experience pressure to accept a false narrative that UN Resolution 2758 serves as a legal pretext under the UN Charter for coercion or war, impairing freedom of navigation in one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, she said. Resolution 2758, passed in 1971, states that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) is the only legitimate representative of China at the UN, which enabled Beijing to replace the Republic of China (ROC), Taiwan’s official name, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council. “Every nation in this hall may be told that aggression or coercion upon Taiwan is an internal matter somehow justified by an ancient UN seating chart resolution, a resolution which doesn’t even reference Taiwan,” she said. Tuvaluan Prime Minister Feleti Teo speaks during the 81st UN General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York on Friday.Photo: AP Appeasement never satisfies an aggressor’s wider agenda, and one taste is never enough, she said. UN member states might be told that “might makes right,” and that it is futile for small nations to resist a larger one, she said. “We will be asked, politely and impolitely, to turn a blind eye and look away,” she said, adding that how the UN addresses this very real security dilemma would be a test of its strength and relevance. Tuvaluan Prime Minister Feleti Teo also called for arrangements that enable the meaningful participation of the 23.5 million Taiwanese in the UN and related agencies. Taiwan has consistently demonstrated that it is an able, trustworthy and constructive partner in addressing global challenges, and its exclusion undermines the spirit and effectiveness of multilateral cooperation, he said. Tuvalu is gravely concerned by the escalating military activities around Taiwan, which threaten stability across the Strait, disrupt international transportation and trade, and jeopardize peace and security in the Pacific and beyond, he said. Tuvalu commends Taiwan for its calm and principled adherence to the values of the UN Charter, he said, urging all UN member states to uphold the same principles. The 81st session of the UN General Assembly opened on Sept. 8, with the general debate running from Tuesday last week to tomorrow. Three of Taiwan’s diplomatic allies — Paraguay, Eswatini and Palau — on Wednesday made a push for Taiwan’s inclusion in the UN.

            US, China to open AI ‘communication channel’
  - AFP, WASHINGTON
 The US and China agreed to set up a “communication channel” for artificial intelligence (AI) incidents, the White House said on Friday, after a Washington summit short on breakthroughs. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) discussed matters ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year at international summits in China and the US. Xi’s visit to Washington was marked more by pomp than substance, but the White House said the nations agreed to establish a “bilateral communication channel” for AI incidents. US President Donald Trump, right, speaks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the steps of the US National Archives Museum in Washington on Friday.Photo: AP While billionaire Trump has repeatedly dismissed fears that AI could pose a threat to humanity, Xi took a more measured tone, saying that the technology must develop under human control. The White House also reported some deals from the visit, including China agreeing to import at least 10 million tonnes of coal from the US next year and in 2028. Additionally, the two countries agreed more favorable tariff treatment for US$30 billion of “non-sensitive goods” in each direction and two Chinese pandas were to arrive at a US zoo. Beijing did not immediately comment after the White House statements.

items.title: US, China buy time with trade truce as pressure builds
items.summary: By Beiyi Seow Washington and Beijing may have bought themselves breathing space with an extended trade truce, but analysts warn that time is running out for the world’s two biggest economies to resolve their strategic rivalry. President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping concluded a pomp-filled summit Friday, with the US leader confirming they […]
items.body_text:
By Beiyi Seow
Washington and Beijing may have bought themselves breathing space with an extended trade truce, but analysts warn that time is running out for the world’s two biggest economies to resolve their strategic rivalry.
President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping concluded a pomp-filled summit Friday, with the US leader confirming they would meet twice more this year.
But even as Trump and Xi “are making nice,” their countries “remain locked in a bitter competition over trade, tech, Taiwan, defense, rare earths and industrial policy,” said Daniel Russel of the Asia Society Policy Institute.
Daniel Kritenbrink, a former US official now with The Asia Group consultancy, said there’s “no doubt that both leaders would like to see stability in the relationship, at least through the end of the year.”
However, “you’d have to see further tangible outcomes for this truce to extend in the long run.”
Some feel Beijing has “largely not lived up to the commitments it made” at earlier meetings, he added, noting many US officials “have articulated their profound frustration with the Chinese.”
Xi and Trump agreed to a trade truce last year during a meeting in South Korea, after a bitter tit-for-tat fight that saw tariffs soar over 100 percent at one point.
As part of the agreement, Beijing agreed to buy more US soybeans and other agriculture products, and to suspend rare earths restrictions for a year.
The pact was originally due to expire in November but both sides agreed this week to extend it until January 10, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
‘Short leash’
Trump’s top trade official Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that Washington views such extensions as “compliance periods.”
“I think US officials would say China is doing just barely enough to maintain the agreement and no more,” Kritenbrink said.
“That’s unsustainable over the long run,” he added.
The brief extension “was the preferred position of the Americans,” Mary Lovely of the Peterson Institute for International Economics told AFP.
She added that while Beijing would have preferred a longer rollover, the current situation points to Washington’s anxiety about the delivery of rare earth magnets and how officials “want to keep this on a short leash.”
“It’s not clear anymore how much their threats of high tariffs actually move China,” she said.
‘Bitter competition’
For now, Greer said that both countries have made “progress” on other economic outcomes and expect to release more details Monday.
“We want to have some subset of goods that we can trade with the Chinese on a more preferential basis,” he said.
He added that both sides have agreed on products that can be left aside in future trade disputes.
Greer is set to host G20 trade ministers in Wisconsin next week, with US tariff threats and the issue of excess capacity — a key concern surrounding Chinese industry — expected to be discussed.
Washington and Beijing have also agreed to set up some kind of notification system for artificial intelligence threats between the two countries, Bessent said.
Peter Richardson of Counterpoint Research said the channel could be as simple as a hotline, but it will be tough to define what triggers it.
“It is often very difficult to tell quickly whether an AI incident was state-directed, a rogue actor or an accident,” he said.
“Given the rivalry we don’t expect this to lead to any comprehensive international framework for AI regulation, but it would be the first practical guardrail,” he added.
Kritenbrink, for his part, said the summit has done “nothing to curb the competitive instincts of both sides on AI.”
“I don’t think you’ll see any slowing down.”

items.title: Teen swimmer makes Games history as Thai, Chinese sprinters win gold
items.summary: Towering teenager Zhang Zhanshuo became the first swimmer in history to win seven golds at a single Asian Games on Friday, as young Thai and Chinese sprinters powered to victory on the track in the 100m in record times. China’s Zhang, 19, scorched to the men’s 400m freestyle title in the pool in Tokyo in […]
items.body_text:
Towering teenager Zhang Zhanshuo became the first swimmer in history to win seven golds at a single Asian Games on Friday, as young Thai and Chinese sprinters powered to victory on the track in the 100m in record times.
China’s Zhang, 19, scorched to the men’s 400m freestyle title in the pool in Tokyo in a Games-record 3min 41.28sec.
He sat on the lane divider after the race and slowly counted off on his fingers all seven gold medals he had won.
Zhang also won individual titles in the 200m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle events, as well as three relays.
He said after wrapping up a scintillating campaign that it had been the “perfect week”.
“I think the most important thing is to stay grounded and focused, because the Asian Games are not my ultimate goal,” said Zhang, who stands 198cm (6ft 6in).
With the Los Angeles Olympics less than two years away, China won 30 of the 42 golds in the pool this week.
Their 13-year-old phenomenon Yu Zidi was the undoubted superstar, taking home three individual golds and all in Games-record times.
Not be outdone, Japan’s 17-year-old Shin Ohashi shattered the men’s 200m breaststroke world record on Thursday.
Swimming, equestrian and diving are taking place in Tokyo, but the city of Nagoya and the wider Aichi prefecture are the main Games host.
The men’s and women’s 100m sprints, the blue riband events in track and field, took place in front of rows of empty seats in Nagoya.
China’s 17-year-old Chen Yujie streaked to a comfortable victory in the women’s final in a Games-record 11.06sec.
Chen turns 18 in December and said: “In China, it’s when we become adults.
“So this is the best present for my birthday, to be on the top of the Asian Games podium.”
The men’s was won by 20-year-old Puripol Boonson, who burst out of the pack in the final quarter of the race to win in 9.90sec, breaking his Games record from earlier in the evening.
It was Thailand’s first men’s 100m gold medal since Suchart Jairsuraparp on home soil at the 1978 Bangkok Games.
China had racked up 98 golds after day six, with Japan a distant second in the overall medals table with 28 gold.
South Korea were third with 13.
Yulo’s miracle
On the last evening of gymnastics, Carlos Yulo won the men’s vault for his second gold of the Games.
The double Olympic champion won floor gold on Thursday to complete his collection of major titles.
“I can’t believe it,” the Filipino said.
“In this whole Asian Games I felt really stressed, but at the same time I enjoyed what I did today. I really did my part.
“Today was really a miracle for me.”
There’s little time to celebrate, however, with the world championships next month.
South Korea edged China 85-80 in the semi-finals of the women’s basketball and will face hosts Japan for gold.
China had their giant centre Zhang Ziyu, 19, but it was not enough.
Zhang stands 223cm (7ft 4in) and scored 22 points.
“She was tough to guard,” said South Korea’s Kang Lee-seul.
“We couldn’t defend her, but we focused on fast breaks and shooting more three-pointers.”
North Korea’s women were again in record-setting form in weightlifting.
Oh Kwang Ok set three world records on her way to women’s 57kg bodyweight class gold.
Oh lifted 104kg in the snatch and 134kg in the clean and jerk for a 238kg total — all world records to add to the two golds North Korea’s women won in the 49kg and 53kg classes this week.
North Korea have won four gold medals and two silvers in the six weightlifting events contested so far.

items.title: Migrant domestic workers demand 21% wage hike to HK$6,172, reject calls for pay freeze
items.summary: Domestic workers called for an increase in their Minimum Allowable Wage from HK$5,100 to HK$6,172 at a rally outside the Labour Department on Friday. The Asian Migrants Coordinating Body (AMCB) also called for an increase in the monthly food allowance from HK$1,236 to HK$3,123. Employers must provide free meals or pay the food allowance set […]
items.body_text:
Domestic workers called for an increase in their Minimum Allowable Wage from HK$5,100 to HK$6,172 at a rally outside the Labour Department on Friday.
The Asian Migrants Coordinating Body (AMCB) also called for an increase in the monthly food allowance from HK$1,236 to HK$3,123. Employers must provide free meals or pay the food allowance set by the Labour Department for their domestic workers, which works out to around HK$41 per day.
“Increasing our wage will ensure we can cope with the unending inflation in Hong Kong, which heavily impacts the majority of [domestic workers] who are striving to live decently and with dignity,” spokesperson Sringatin said, according to a Friday press release. Some Indonesians go by only one name.
“Since 2000, the Minimum Allowable Wage has only increased from HK$3,670 per month to the current HK$5,100 – a cumulative increase of just 39% (HK$1,430) spanning 25 years. This is an incredibly low wage for a territory that proudly brands itself as ‘Asia’s World City,'” she added.
Long hours, job insecurity
The coalition, the city’s largest group of migrant worker unions and associations, said that domestic workers have provided “round-the-clock household and caregiving support for children and the elderly” for decades, enabling double-income households.
The group rejected claims from employer groups that wage hikes would trigger mass layoffs and pushed back on calls for a pay freeze. The AMCB said that the care services that domestic workers provide are “irreplaceable,” with some of their earnings recycled back into the local economy.
In August, a petition by the International Domestic Service Industry Development Federation and the Quadripartite Alliance for Harmonious Employment Practices (QAHEP) called for a domestic worker wage freeze. The QAHEP released a survey suggesting that 97 per cent of employers were “strongly opposed” to pay rises for their domestic workers.
The AMCB also cited “job insecurity, excessively long working hours, heightened vulnerability to abuse due to the mandatory live-in arrangement, and ongoing exploitation by erring recruitment agencies.”
By law, domestic workers must live with their employers – a situation advocacy groups argue can enable abuse.
Sringatin added: “We will continue the fight for a living wage, full legal protection, and decent working conditions until these deep-seated issues are resolved.”

Alex Lo has been an SCMP columnist since 2012, commenting on China and international affairs. 
Last week, the president of the United States stood at the podium of the United Nations General Assembly and asked aloud whether he should “annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly”. Donald Trump then turned to Venezuela’s oil and declared: “To the victor belong the spoils, you’ve all heard that …”
He spoke as the Iran war neared its eighth month, a week after the UN Human Rights Council found “reasonable grounds to believe” that the US had committed war crimes. In the same speech, Trump said the United States would not join global regulation of AI and urged countries to abandon the International Criminal Court.
Elsewhere this month, the picture looked very different. In Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, all 10 member states of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) gathered to mark its 25th anniversary. The bloc began in 2001 as a club of six. This year’s summit produced 27 documents alongside the Bishkek Declaration, which condemned the military strikes on Iranian territory by the US and Israel as violations of international law.

Washington’s proposed military bases and expanded defence presence in Greenland will be akin to a “keep out” sign against potential Arctic military cooperation between Beijing and Moscow, according to analysts.
The US, Denmark and Greenland signed a defence deal on Tuesday that allows Washington to build two new military bases on the world’s largest island, while reaffirming Denmark’s sovereignty over it.
The deal – which updates and amends a 1951 defence agreement between Denmark and the US – allows expansion and modernisation of the Pituffik US Space Force Base in northwestern Greenland and for additional military bases to be established in Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, though they will still require approval from Greenland and Denmark.
Narsarsuaq is a settlement located in southern Greenland with a former civilian airport and US airbase that was closed in 1958. Its population is only a few dozen people.

items.body_text:
白羊座滿月能量爆發 艾菲爾點名4生肖「卡關人生動起來」
和平島地質公園為最美日出觀測點之一。（資料照，北觀處提供）
〔娛樂頻道／綜合報導〕塔羅牌老師艾菲爾指出，白羊座滿月帶來強烈的「結束與釋放」能量，並點名生肖鼠、龍、馬、猴從27日起，有望逐漸擺脫過去的包袱與停滯狀態，迎接新的轉機。其中生肖鼠適合調整方向、重新啟動計畫，生肖龍可告別消耗自己的人事物，生肖馬行動力回升，適合勇敢跨出第一步，生肖猴則可能因轉換思維，意外發現新的可能。
艾菲爾今（27）日在臉書粉專發文指出，昨日白羊座滿月帶來強烈的「結束與釋放」氣氛，累積已久的情緒、停滯的計畫，或是一段讓人反覆糾結的關係，都可能在滿月後逐漸出現新的答案。
他表示，滿月過後不必急著證明自己究竟改變了多少，反而應該把注意力重新放回「接下來想往哪裡走」。有些事情告一段落並不代表失去，反而是在替新的選擇清出空間。
到了9月27日，鼠、龍、馬、猴4個生肖特別容易感受到周遭環境正在鬆動。艾菲爾提醒，只要願意放下過度執著的舊模式，就有機會重新找回行動力，讓原本卡住的人生逐步邁向下一個階段。
生肖鼠：舊計畫重新找到出口
艾菲爾表示，生肖鼠在滿月後最明顯的轉變，就是開始不再執著於「一定要照原本的方式完成」。之前可能因為太在意細節、別人的看法，或害怕重新來過，把自己困在原地，這幾天反而適合重新整理手上的事情，挑出真正值得留下的目標。
生肖鼠也可能突然發現，某個看似走不通的方向，其實只是需要換一條路。工作上適合重新調整安排，生活中也可能出現改變想法的人或消息。艾菲爾提醒，別再把過去的失誤當成限制，因為它們早已成為經驗值，接下來真正重要的是重新相信自己的判斷，勇敢啟動下一步。
生肖龍：告別消耗你的人事物
生肖龍這段時間容易出現「突然想通了」的感覺。過去那些讓自己反覆煩惱的人、事與承諾，到了滿月之後，可能開始覺得不值得繼續投入過多時間與情緒，也會逐漸明白，真正適合自己的選擇，不需要一直努力說服自己。
工作上可能重新接觸曾經擱置的任務，但這一次會有更成熟的方法處理。人際方面適合與過度消耗自己的人保持一些距離，財務上也適合重新檢視不必要的支出。
艾菲爾表示，當生肖龍願意把注意力從「已經失去什麼」轉向「接下來能擁有什麼」，整體運勢就有機會逐漸鬆開，新的機會往往就在停止留戀之後出現。
生肖馬：行動力重新被點燃
滿月過後，生肖馬很適合把「想了很久」的事情真正付諸行動。前陣子可能有些提不起勁，明明知道方向在哪裡，卻總覺得還少了一個契機，如今這個契機正逐漸形成。
尤其在工作、學習及生活規劃方面，生肖馬適合先跨出第一步，再一邊行動、一邊調整。艾菲爾提醒，不需要一次把未來全部想清楚，只要先讓自己動起來，答案自然會越來越明朗。
感情與人際方面，也可能重新遇見熟悉的人，或再次開啟某段對話。不過這一次不用急著回到從前，而是觀察彼此能否用新的方式相處。真正需要的不是把所有事情重新開始，而是重新找回對生活的主導感。
生肖猴：換個角度出現新可能
艾菲爾表示，滿月後生肖猴最大的好運來自「改變思考方式」。原本可能認定某件事情只能二選一，近期卻有機會意外發現第三條路，不只重新燃起期待，也容易遇見願意提供資訊、資源或實際幫助的人。
工作上適合重新提案、調整方法，甚至把原本認為做不到的事情拆成較小的步驟。感情方面則適合放下過度揣測，不要因為害怕受傷，就提前替結果下結論。
生活中如果有一直拖著沒有處理的小事，也適合趁機一次清掉，讓空間與心情一起變輕。艾菲爾認為，當生肖猴願意接受「事情不一定要照原計畫發生」，反而更容易走進真正適合自己的新局面。

items.body_text:
鐵幕！中國20名大學生、研究生用VPN翻牆 遭校方祭出處分
中國哈爾濱工程大學20名學生使用VPN翻牆，被校方警告處分。（路透）
首次上稿 14:10
更新時間 20:42
中國哈爾濱工程大學（下稱哈工程）數學科學學院20名學生，在本月18日至19日使用VPN翻牆連接到國外網路，被學院祭出警告處分，無疑是中國「網路長城」治理下的新一批受害者。
從哈工程數學院蓋有單位公章的通報可以看到，該院大學生祖X豪、王X宇、李X澤、李X洋、關X、郭X揚、劉X熙；研究生毛X、李X隆、胡X飛、安X權、龔X威、黃X宇、李X成、高X隆、姜X、李X謀、張X康、蔡X杰、趙X婷等20人，9月18日至19日以校園網路帳號翻牆訪問境外網路。
通報指出，這20名學生違反國家、校方有關網路管理的規定，考慮到屬於初犯且沒有傳播危害訊息，因此做出警告處分，未來若再度觸犯將嚴格處理，並要求上述學生深刻反省。
哈工程的處分公告被中國知名律師蔡雅奇等人轉發微博後，受到大量網友的討論，一度傳出是1名女生想要升上研究所，但被其他人卡住位置，因此一氣之下舉報同學翻牆，結果就抓了一大串，後來又被認為不合理，可能只是流言。
不過，中國網友透露，學生在被校方警告處分後，該年的獎學金或保送研究所資格都會被取消，而且「翻牆」的資料可能會被登記在個人檔案裡，若未來想進入公家機關工作恐會因此被刷掉。

items.title: North Korean province launches student tracking app, but glitches pile up
items.summary: North Korean education officials in South Hamgyong province have launched a student tracking app for high schools. Students can now borrow library books and join after-school clubs on their own mobile phones. Since the September 2026 rollout, however, unstable networks and incompatible devices have caused widespread confusion. A source in the province told Daily NK […]
items.body_text:
North Korean education officials in South Hamgyong province have launched a student tracking app for high schools. Students can now borrow library books and join after-school clubs on their own mobile phones. Since the September 2026 rollout, however, unstable networks and incompatible devices have caused widespread confusion.
A source in the province told Daily NK on Monday that the system took effect on Sept. 10. The education department of the provincial people’s committee introduced it at senior middle schools as part of a modernization push for the new term. People’s committees are North Korea’s regional administrative bodies and oversee local schools, housing and public services. Senior middle schools are the North Korean equivalent of high schools.
Once students install the app, they receive a QR code to scan at library terminals when borrowing or reserving books. The app also scraps the longstanding rule that limited each student to a single after-school club. Students can now register for up to three or four clubs in academic, arts, sports and technical fields. These clubs are a fixture of North Korean school life, where students build skills in areas from science to music.
The education department plans to log each student’s reading history and club activity on a provincial server in real time. It will then use that data in academic evaluations and future career placements. In North Korea, the state largely decides whether graduates head to university, military service or assigned workplaces. That gives these digital records real weight in shaping a young person’s future.
Student tracking app hit by network failures and device gaps
Problems surfaced even before launch, when city and county education departments ran simulated login tests across the province. Unreliable networks frequently prevented the app from syncing student data with the central server, according to the source.
“In some areas, the data synchronization failure rate topped 40%,” the source said. “The confusion comes from rushing a phone-based management system while network conditions remain unstable.”
Teachers complain that compatibility problems across different phone models have only added to their administrative workload. The rollout has also sparked a debate over fairness and equal access to school services. Students without phones, or with older handsets that cannot run current software, could be shut out of borrowing and club sign-ups entirely.
Mobile phone use has grown rapidly in North Korea over the past decade. Yet smartphone ownership remains uneven, and network coverage outside major cities is often unreliable.
A senior middle school teacher in Hamhung, the provincial capital, called the rollout “a textbook case of armchair administration.” The teacher said officials launched the system without first checking student phone ownership, school networks or the local power supply.
Schools also differ widely in their IT infrastructure, which has deepened the problem. Rural schools on the outskirts of Hamhung lack adequate network connections and equipment. Some of them suffered login delays and outages on club registration day, throwing the process into disarray.
Schools and parents must also cover part of the cost of the QR code scanners installed in libraries. That expense has prompted complaints from families already stretched by informal payments to their children’s schools. North Korean parents are routinely expected to contribute cash or goods toward school supplies, repairs and state projects.
“Authorities are introducing a new management system in the name of education modernization, but basic conditions like network coverage and phone distribution aren’t in place,” the source said. “Because access depends on each student’s and school’s IT environment, many worry the education gap will grow even wider.”

items.title: Will the New Yalu River Bridge finally open? Border traders point to early October
items.summary: Talk of a New Yalu River Bridge opening in early October 2026 is spreading rapidly along the China-North Korea border. Rising vehicle traffic and final work on North Korean customs facilities have convinced many local traders that the long-stalled crossing may finally begin operating. Traders in Dandong who do business with North Korea increasingly believe […]
items.body_text:
Talk of a New Yalu River Bridge opening in early October 2026 is spreading rapidly along the China-North Korea border. Rising vehicle traffic and final work on North Korean customs facilities have convinced many local traders that the long-stalled crossing may finally begin operating.
Traders in Dandong who do business with North Korea increasingly believe the bridge will officially open early next month, a Daily NK source in China said on Tuesday. The same view is circulating among businesspeople who operate near the bridge.
The New Yalu River Bridge spans the Yalu River between Dandong, in China’s Liaoning province, and Sinuiju, in North Pyongan province. The roughly three-kilometer cable-stayed bridge was built largely with Chinese funding and structurally completed in 2014. It has sat idle ever since, leaving cross-border trade dependent on the aging Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge.
The date mentioned most often is Oct. 6, the 77th anniversary of diplomatic relations between North Korea and China. Some locals believe the two countries could choose that date to highlight the symbolic importance of their ties. Others expect the ceremony on Oct. 8 or 9, however, since China’s National Day holiday runs from Oct. 1 through Oct. 7.
“China usually shuts down or scales back customs operations during major national holidays, so it may be difficult in practice to hold the ceremony on the 6th,” the source said. “Some people think it will be held on the 8th or 9th, after the holiday ends.”
A noticeable increase in vehicles crossing the bridge has lent further credibility to the rumors. In the past, vehicles crossed only occasionally for construction work or facility inspections. Since August, however, they have made regular trips about three times a week, mostly at night, according to the source.
On the North Korean side, construction of the customs complex and surrounding roads is nearly complete, the source added. Work to prepare customs clearance and logistics facilities is also picking up speed. North Korean authorities have ordered all logistics facilities connected to the bridge finished before Oct. 10, and crews are now carrying out the final stages of work.
Daily NK previously reported that torrential rains in late August flooded low-lying areas around the North Korean customs complex. Satellite imagery showed, however, that the main customs building and the bridge access road escaped direct damage.
What the New Yalu River Bridge opening date could signal
With preparations apparently in their final stages, trade insiders are watching closely for two things. The first is the exact date of the ceremony, and the second is the seniority of the officials each side sends.
Some people in the area have even suggested that China could dispatch an official at the vice premier level. “The fact that people are even talking about a vice premier coming leads some to believe China considers this quite important,” the source said. He added that many expect “it will be no small event for either country.”
Still, neither the official opening date nor the list of officials attending the ceremony has been confirmed.
Local trade insiders believe an Oct. 6 ceremony would carry strong diplomatic symbolism tied to the anniversary of bilateral ties. A ceremony on Oct. 8 or 9, by contrast, would fit the resumption of normal customs work after the Chinese holiday. It would also fall just before Oct. 10, the founding anniversary of the Workers’ Party of Korea (WPK). Party Foundation Day is one of North Korea’s most important political holidays, and the regime typically showcases economic achievements in the weeks leading up to it.
“If it happens on the 6th, many people will see it as an event focused on Korea-China (North Korea-China) relations,” the source said. “The 8th or 9th would be a good moment for North Korea to present it as an achievement ahead of Party Foundation Day, which is why people are paying close attention to the specific date.”

items.title: North Korea revises science and technology law, adds unpaid labor penalties
items.summary: North Korea revised its science and technology law this year. The changes sharpen the criteria for choosing which new technologies enter production, and they add unpaid labor punishments for officials who miss targets or falsify progress reports, Daily NK has confirmed. Daily NK obtained a copy of the amended Law on the Introduction of Scientific […]
items.body_text:
North Korea revised its science and technology law this year. The changes sharpen the criteria for choosing which new technologies enter production, and they add unpaid labor punishments for officials who miss targets or falsify progress reports, Daily NK has confirmed.
Daily NK obtained a copy of the amended Law on the Introduction of Scientific and Technological Achievements. It was revised through Presidium of the Supreme People’s Assembly Decree No. 1938 on June 10, 2025, and its structure grew from five chapters and 47 articles to six chapters and 50 articles. Chapter 5 of the 2020 version, titled “guidance and control over the introduction of scientific and technology achievements,” was replaced with a chapter on “legal responsibility.” A new sixth chapter setting the law’s effective date was added as an addendum.
The revision does not overhaul the system for introducing scientific and technology achievements. North Korea kept the older law’s basic framework, which centers on drafting and issuing plans, signing and carrying out contracts, and offering incentives. What changed is more specific: the amended law spells out which technologies count as genuine achievements, and it details who bears responsibility when a plan falls short.
The revision arrives as North Korea has strengthened legal and institutional control across society since the COVID-19 pandemic. Economic and industrial laws in particular have increasingly carved out separate legal responsibility sections that specify punishments by violation type, and the science and technology law revision fits squarely within that trend.
Selection criteria shift toward measurable results
The first notable change concerns the criteria for selecting which science and technology achievements to introduce. The old law’s Article 12, titled “principles for selecting science and technology achievements to introduce,” listed five criteria. The revised Article 12, retitled “requirements to observe in selection,” now lists six.
Two of the old criteria disappeared: “saving labor, energy and costs” and being “advanced, practical and suited to actual conditions.” In their place, the amended law newly requires that a technology “contribute to updating technical-economic indicators.” It must also “contribute to expanding the variety of products manufactured.”
The change favors measurable outcomes, such as productivity, efficiency and product diversification, over relatively abstract language like “advanced” or “practical.” Rather than simply crediting the development of a new technology, the law now appears designed to evaluate what changes that technology actually produced on the factory floor.
The amended law also changed how achievements move through the approval process. Where the old law said the central science and technology administrative guidance agency “selects” achievements, the revised version says the agency “applies for” them. Article 13, which governs how introduction plans are drafted, similarly shifted from “selected” achievements to “applied” achievements.
A similar emphasis has shown up elsewhere in North Korea’s recent economic policymaking. Daily NK reported in March that a joint directive from the ruling Workers’ Party’s Central Economic Department and the Cabinet called for industrializing new energy sources and artificial intelligence. The South Pyongan Provincial People’s Committee, which received the directive, stressed that factories would need to demonstrate modernized processes and improved efficiency, not simply meet output quotas.
The upshot is that North Korean authorities are now evaluating performance by more than output alone. They are also judging how much a factory’s newly introduced technology improved its production structure.

items.title: Matty Johns breaks down in tears after Knights end NRL grand final drought
items.summary: Matty Johns fights through tears to praise the Knights and the Newcastle fans after a gripping and gritty preliminary final win over Penrith.
items.body_text:
Former Knights star Matty Johns has praised the Knights and their fans after Newcastle reached the NRL grand final for the first time in 25 years.
Johns became emotional as he hailed the supporters for sticking by the team.
What's next?
The Knights will face the Roosters in the NRL grand final on Sunday, October 4 from 7:30pm AEDT.
Former Knights star Matty Johns has broken down in tears as he heaped praise on the Newcastle team and its fans after a gripping and gritty NRL preliminary final win over Penrith.
The Knights played more than half the game with 12 men on the field after Phoenix Crossland was sent off for a hip drop that graphically broke Nathan Cleary's leg.
Penrith scored shortly after to take a 14-6 lead into half-time, but Justin Holbrook's Knights defended resolutely against a scrappy Panthers side and managed to score three second-half tries to progress to the grand final against the Roosters.
The women's team won back-to-back NRLW premierships in 2022 and 2023, but Newcastle has not played in a men's grand final since Andrew Johns led the Knights to victory over the Eels in the 2001 grand final.
A quarter of a century and five wooden spoons later, the team will return to the final day of the season next week after a similarly remarkable upset win over the most dominant team in NRL history.
So it is hardly surprising that Hunter native and former Knights star Matty Johns was incredibly emotional straight after full-time.
"To be honest, I don't know what to say," he said on Fox Sports.
"It was unbelievable. Incredible effort in that second half. I just feel so happy for all the fans."
It became increasingly hard to find the words as tears started to flow and emotion took over.
"They've had to put up with a lot of shit for a lot of years to get back to where they are now," Johns said.
Even getting to the game on Sunday was tough as an issue with a freight train caused delays and cancellations on the Central Coast and Newcastle train line, forcing fans to find alternate routes and replacement services to get down to Sydney, which led to traffic jams on the M1 motorway on a sodden afternoon.
"But it just didn't stop them in the wet," Johns said of the crowd at Homebush, which was hugely in favour of the visiting Novocastrians.
"When you run onto a field like that and you look up and you see all those Newcastle fans, you don't leave the field defeated.
"If not for the fans they don't win today."
Holbrook sprinted around the field to pay tribute to the fans who turned up, and who have continued to turn up even when the team was struggling, including last year when they finished last for the fifth time in 21 seasons.
"We want to make our community proud, our Hunter region, and for the boys to deliver that performance, it was so good to see them all hang around," he said.
"We went down to 12 [when Crossland was sent off] and then 30,000 make you feel like you've got 14 out there."
Captain Kalyn Ponga agreed the supporters helped the team get over the line.
"They're a big reason why we won today," he said.
"They're loud, they're passionate, they're vocal and we're gonna need them next week."

items.title: Freo finds joy in AFLW win, Pies finally off the mark
items.summary: Fremantle's AFLW side restores some joy to the Dockers' weekend with victory over Adelaide, while Collingwood claims its first win of the season over GWS.
items.body_text:
Fremantle's women have lifted their club as they surged into the AFLW top eight, while Collingwood broke through for its first win of the season.
The fast-starting Dockers outscored Adelaide 28-0 in the first quarter and led by as much as 45 on their way to a comfortable 9.6 (60) to 5.5 (35) victory over Adelaide at Unley Oval. 
Adelaide (3-4) kicked three straight goals either side of three-quarter time, but never got the deficit below 25, as Fremantle (4-3) defended its advantage, unlike its male counterparts in Saturday's AFL grand final.
It was the Dockers' first win in their past seven AFLW encounters with Adelaide, who had a 9-1 record in the fixture before Sunday.
In the other early game on Sunday, Collingwood (1-6) outlasted GWS 4.10 (34) to 3.7 (25) in a low-scoring arm wrestle at Victoria Park.
The Giants (1-6) led by margins of one, four and seven at the end of the first three quarters respectively, but Collingwood dominated the final term.
They finished with 18 more inside 50s and 16 more contested possessions.
In Sydney, the Lions fell short of a stirring comeback of their own in a 5.7 (37) to 3.5 (23) defeat to the Swans.
The victory held Sydney's position in the top four and saw Brisbane's record fall to a disappointing 2-5.
The Lions were second best for most of the afternoon but managed to stay in touch through three quarters, and were only a point behind at the final term.
But after Cynthia Hamilton goaled inside the first minute of the last quarter, the Swans didn't look back, running out comfortable 12-point winners.
In the final game of round seven, Gold Coast took St Kilda another step closer to the wooden spoon by running out 10.9 (69) to 6.3 (39) winners.
The Saints led by 15 points at half-time but were gunned down by the home side after the break, conceding eight goals to one as the Suns moved to sixth place on the AFLW ladder.
ABC/AAP

items.title: Dynasties and destinies swing on Cleary's horror ankle injury
items.summary: Penrith and Newcastle were going hammer and tongs when Nathan Cleary's horror ankle injury turned the NRL preliminary final on its head.
items.body_text:
Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
analysis
Knights earn date with destiny as Nathan Cleary's injury puts Panthers dynasty on the brink
Mark the 35th minute of Sunday's NRL preliminary final as the hinge on which a storied dynasty and a potential premiership destiny swung.
Penrith and Newcastle had fought a first-half that made both look like worthy foes for the Roosters in next week's grand final.
The Knights faithful turned Stadium Australia into a little piece of the Hunter, proving yet again they would follow their team into hell itself if Sid Fogg's would charter a bus there.
Francis Manuleleua's long-range try, the latest scorching adventure of the screaming Knights, gave the beast inside the 55,000-strong crowd a smell of blood and it turned the Panthers into strangers in their own country.
The Penrith half of the crowd rose for Blaize Talagi's score off a clever Jack Cogger kick, but never has Nathan Cleary, benched before kick-off, copped such treatment on his home turf as he did before he entered the game in the 20th minute.
Just 10 minutes later came the tackle that ended his season as he suffered an graphic fracture to his ankle, also ending Phoenix Crossland's afternoon after he was sent off, and putting this game on the raggedy edge.
In the end, it was the Knights who pushed the Panthers over the side to write their names in history, with a 22-14 win that sends Newcastle to their first grand final in 25 years.
The two sides provided a fascinating contrast from the start as they left the field following the warm-up.
Penrith, the ultimate professionals and avatars of pure ruthlessness, had eyes of steel, a picture of focus.
Newcastle, by contrast, waved to friends and family, faces beaming that they were here together on the verge of a dream.
Rage and joy proved to be equally potent fuels, with rare courage on both sides amid the furious desperation you only see when the stakes are highest.
The Knights finished with 12 on the field after Crossland's dismissal but, somehow, rarely looked shorthanded.
There is a temptation to call that a miracle, but Newcastle didn't need divine intervention to flat-out-play the Panthers in a second half.
They bent occasionally but never broke as Penrith fought hard, denied only by a series of last-gasp efforts from the Knights.
Kalyn Ponga pulled off a tackle on Moses Leota that any footy hit man would have been proud of. Mat Croker dived on loose balls like they were live grenades.
Dane Gagai played like his Newcastle life depended on it, and given he has earned one last day as a Knight, it kind of did.
They were able to take advantage of the Panthers not quite being their razor-sharp selves, as best typified by Smith's first try off a quick tap that caught Penrith on the hop.
The Panthers missed Cleary, their edges blunted, but Casey McLean came agonisingly close to scoring.
It is a mark of the steel in the Panthers that they weren't out of it until Sandon Smith's late intercept try, even with injuries mounting.
Aside from Cleary — already carrying a broken foot into the game — Blaize Talagi did his Achilles, Dylan Edwards hurt his PCL and Isaah Yeo defied belief to play through a torn pec.
They regrouped well in the moments after Cleary's injury, scoring through Lindsay Smith while the game was still in something of a punch-drunk stupor.
But they did not trouble the scorers again as Newcastle ran in three tries in the second half, all of which began from their own side of halfway.
That ability to strike fast and from anywhere on the field is the Knights' greatest gift — it has happened too many times to call this a charmed run or a triumph of abstract, random brilliance.
It has taken them through a high-octane South Sydney, to the heart of Auckland and back and now, a man down and all, through the greatest dynasty many will ever know.
That dynasty is not at its end, but preliminary final losses in each of the past two years show how thin the margins have

items.title: Melbourne man’s mysterious disappearance on popular Peru hiking trail prompts widespread search
items.summary: Loved ones describe Jordan Yap, 30, as an experienced hiker who set out for a 10-day solo trek Peru before falling silentGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastLoved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and
items.body_text:
Loved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.
A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.
He was last seen near the beginning of his trek across the Cordillera Huayhuash circuit, which is regarded as a challenging, high-altitude trek through the remote Andes mountains.
Regarded as a very experienced hiker by friends and family, the Melbourne man failed to make contact on Wednesday, his estimated return date.
He also failed to check back into the Krusty Hostel in Huaraz, where his luggage remains stored, and missed a scheduled flight from Lima to Cusco on Thursday.
“It’s really uncharacteristic of him to not have communicated at any point in his journey if he had the chance to,” longtime friend Kevin Nguyen said.
“It is a very popular trek, where you might have 200 to 300 hikers and guides per week during the busy season, so it is very uncharacteristic that no one’s seen him since day one or day two.”
The avid trekker misplaced a satellite beacon he was travelling with days before he set off on the 120km hike, raising further concerns.
Local mountain rescue organisation Socorro Andino Peruano has been hired by Yap’s family to help with the search.
His loved ones are holding out hope the rescue group, which recently rescued a Canadian trekker from the same trail, will be able to find him safe.
“Time is of the essence … because ultimately, as much as we were saying he’s been missing since the 23rd, he’s had no contact with anyone since the 14th,” Nguyen said.
Rescue crews completed their biggest day of search operations so far on Saturday (Sunday morning AEST), scouring various trails on the circuit to no avail.
“I know Jordan likes to orienteer and navigate and he’s quite an adventurer himself, so I wouldn’t be surprised if he tried an alternative route,” Nguyen said.
Yap had been planning the trek for more than a year and had recently bought a GPS watch to allow for offline maps to guide him on the hike.
“He was telling everyone about how he was ready to go on a big hike like this, (he was) really excited,” Nguyen said.
He was last known to be wearing a white jacket, green sunshade sweater and grey pants.
The experienced trekker was believed to be carrying a 40-litre hiking bag, Durston dome tent and hiking poles.
Family and friends are urging the Australian government to work with Peruvian officials and local authorities to mobilise further resources in and around the rugged region.
The Australian embassy in Peru is helping his family.
The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has been contacted for comment.

items.title: ‘Cash grab’: One Nation demands up to $630,000 from Victorian election candidates
items.summary: Exclusive: Many applicants left feeling ‘used, lied to, misled and gaslit’, complaint letter seen by Guardian Australia saysListen to the Guardian podcast The Populist hereGet our new political email, free app or daily news podcastOne Nation could collect as much as $633,000 from people who have put their hand up to run in the Victorian state election, with potential candidates questioning whether the party is staging a “cash grab”.Guardian Australia has spoken to multiple former councillors, ma
items.body_text:
One Nation could collect as much as $633,000 from people who have put their hand up to run in the Victorian state election, with potential candidates questioning whether the party is staging a “cash grab”.
Guardian Australia has spoken to multiple former councillors, mayors and deputy mayors who expressed an interest in running for the party. They claim they went through what one called a “pay-to-play” application process, after which they were rejected.
Those who applied to be considered were required to pay $150 as a “non refundable application fee”, invoices seen by the Guardian show.
One Nation told the Guardian that 1,209 people put in an expression of interest to run in the November state election, and approximately 220 proceeded to the final stage, resulting in an estimated $33,000 flowing into party coffers if all final stage candidates paid this amount.
Applicants were also expected to be party members, with this translating to an additional $72,000 based on the minimum membership fee of $60 a year.
In addition, candidates were advised in interviews that they would be required to pay $5,500 of their own money to run if preselected, even though the vast majority of lower house electorates are not deemed winnable.
While it is not uncommon for the major parties to require candidates to pay an application fee, they do not levy campaign fees on candidates like those being charged by One Nation.
The candidate fee will bring $528,000 into the party’s coffers, based on running 88 lower house candidates and eight for the upper house. In total, the amount paid by candidates could be as much as $633,000.
Aidan McLindon, a political consultant who worked with One Nation in Victoria last year, said many potential candidates had been left frustrated by what appeared to be a “money-spinning exercise”.
One Nation was “disproportionately focusing on profits over policy”. McLindon said in an interview for episode three of The Populist, out on Monday.
Based on the party’s polling numbers, One Nation is also in line to receive as much as $10m through Victoria’s public electoral funding scheme.
Applicants who spoke to the Guardian have questioned whether the application process was genuine, saying the party had conducted 15-minute video interviews with each candidate before a decision was made. Potential candidates were all required to sign non-disclosure agreements about the process on application.
There is also concern that the upper house candidates were “captain’s picks” selected by the party’s state leader, Warren Pickering, with One Nation overlooking candidates with significant local government and professional experience.
A complaint letter sent to the party by one former Victorian mayor says the process has left many candidates feeling “that we were used, lied to, misled and gaslit”.
“The issue is that the process increasingly looks as though it was used as cover to conceal decisions that had already been substantially made, while creating the public appearance of an open, merit-based candidate search,” the letter seen by the Guardian states.
“Applicants should not have been encouraged to invest their time, energy, reputations and personal information in an elaborate exercise merely to provide legitimacy, numbers or political cover for what now appears to have been a biased and self-serving leadership process.”
Another local government member who had applied questioned whether the process was a “cash grab”.
“They are asking everyday folk, hard-working mums and dads, for $5,500 which is a lot of money,” one said.
“I just think it is a cash grab for the federal election. My feeling is they are just using all of the states to fundraise for the federal election where they want to take power.”
Another said they believed that under the party’s constitution, all funds would be transferred to One Nation’s Brisbane headquarters.
“They will get $800,000 in the kitty for doing absolutely nothing,” one said.

items.title: U.K. police evacuate homes near U.S. airbase and detain men on suspected explosives offensives
items.summary: British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offences and army bomb disposal experts were examining a number of vehicles in a "major incident" near an airbase used by the U.S. in southwest England.
items.body_text:
U.K. police evacuate homes near U.S. airbase and detain men on suspected explosives offensives
Police say several men have been detained on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act
British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offences and army bomb disposal experts were examining a number of vehicles in a "major incident" near an airbase used by the U.S. in southwest England.
Police said nearby residents had been evacuated from their homes.
The British government gave authorization to the U.S. to use RAF Fairford to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that are attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guard warned in July that any base used in strikes would be a legitimate target.
A Reuters eyewitness said armed police had blocked access to the main gate of the base, while equipment had been positioned in front of access points and residents of a nearby village were evacuated to a leisure centre.
Around 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, were stationed in the village of Fairford near the base.
"A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident. It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act," Gloucestershire police said in a statement, referring to a village near the air base.
"The army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles."
Police said they believed the incident was now contained.
A spokesperson for the U.S. air force declined to discuss specific force protection measures.
"The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow U.K.-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our U.S. service members, civilians, contractors and their families," the spokesperson said.
"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families."
Britain said in July its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack after Iran's Revolutionary Guard warned the U.K. not to allow U.S. bombers to fly from Fairford.
British ministers have also briefed providers of critical infrastructure on the threat posed by Russia, with the government increasingly concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks. Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.

items.title: Putin appears to be eyeing NATO. The question is, will he actually attack?
items.summary: European military experts warn that Russia is actively planning targeted aggression against NATO to test alliance solidarity. Recent high-alert incidents include a foiled explosive drone plot at a German airport and a strike near the Ukraine-Poland border targeting European VIPs. However, officials are deeply split on the immediacy of a conventional threat.

Putin appears to be eyeing NATO. The question is, will he actually attack?
European countries on high alert amid mounting signs of danger from Moscow
European military experts are tracking urgent danger signs that suggest Vladimir Putin may be preparing for a direct escalation against the NATO alliance.
What analysts are split over is whether the Russian president is merely weighing his options or has already decided to pull the trigger.
"What's pretty clear from public intelligence briefings by … a number of heads of state and defence secretaries across different member states is that Russia is planning [some] sort of aggression, probably with multiple potential forms," said Justin Bronk, senior research fellow for airpower and technology at the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based military think-tank.
"That doesn't mean they've decided to do it — but it does mean it's probably under active planning and therefore the risk of it has risen significantly."
Moscow is "cooking up something big this year," warned Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski during a panel discussion as part of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Friday, without elaborating.
The concerns have been fuelled by a threat assessment from Denmark's government that this week raised the prospect of a Russian missile attack on NATO infrastructure used to support Ukraine. The report said such an attack could happen within weeks.
A wave of incidents over the last month have put governments and security services on high alert.
Germany's government has directly blamed Putin for an attempted drone strike on Leipzig's airport that appeared to target aircraft carrying supplies to Kyiv.
A Russian drone then attacked a Ukrainian passenger train on the border with Poland, a NATO ally, just as it unloaded a carriage full of European VIPs, including former British prime minister Boris Johnson. Russia confirmed the strike but denied it was trying to assassinate European diplomats.
Meanwhile, Polish authorities stated they strongly suspect Kremlin agents were behind an arson attack earlier this week on a satellite communications ground station serving as a critical link with Ukraine's armed forces.
Going forward, analysts suggest Moscow's goals are highly calculated.
"The Russians aren't going to do something that they think leads to a long, difficult war. That's not their objective," said Bronk.
"The objective would be to do something small enough that it still definitively violates NATO territory to test the alliance visibly, but keep it small enough that it becomes very difficult to get the political will to respond directly and militarily kick them out."
Putin has denied all allegations of aggression and instead framed Russia as the victim of warmongering by the Western military alliance as he has for much of 27 years at the top of Russia's power pyramid.
"NATO is swelling up and expanding," he told a Kremlin meeting on Sept. 18, claiming European leaders are "simply trying to salvage their sagging ratings, and cover up mistakes" with accusations of Russian aggression.
Putin has repeatedly justified his February 2022 invasion of Ukraine as self-defence, falsely claiming that NATO was building up troops and weapons there in preparation for invading Russia.
'Rat in the corner'
Now, after four and half years of full-scale war, Russia is believed to have suffered as many as 1.4 million people killed or wounded and its economy is under severe strain.
One senior Estonian commander on Friday likened Putin to a "rat in the corner," suggesting that because the war is going badly he may see aggression against Ukraine's European allies as a the best means to break Western support.

items.title: At least 27 people dead after two separate mass shootings in South Africa
items.summary: The two shootings come just days after a mass shooting at a house party near the east coast city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.
items.body_text:
At least 27 people dead after two separate mass shootings in South Africa
Preliminary reports indicate authorities were searching for multiple gunmen in both cases
Two separate mass shootings near South Africa's two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, police said Sunday.
The South African Police Service said 17 people were killed Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, southwest of Johannesburg. At least 15 others sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.
In a separate statement, police said 10 people were killed in a mass shooting at a store in Lwandle, near Cape Town, around 1 a.m. local time on Sunday. Another 11 were wounded in that shooting. Police said they were searching for multiple suspects in that case also, though they didn't give an exact number.
The two shootings come just days after a mass shooting at a house party near the east coast city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.
No arrests had been made in the two latest mass shootings, police said.

items.title: In French wine country, climate change, tariffs and dwindling demand are a recipe for trouble
items.summary: Growers of Bordeaux, threatened by nature and economics, look for ways to weather future seasons
items.body_text:
On clear sunny days, Guillaume Duluc likes to stand on top of one of his giant stainless steel fermentation vats and look out over the rows of vineyards that stretch to the horizon in this picturesque region north of Bordeaux in southwestern France.
Mr. Duluc has noticed something troubling lately when he gazes at the greenery. There are more patches of vacant land where growers have pulled up their vines and given up. Many of them are families like the Dulucs who have been here for centuries making world-renowned cognac and wine.
A summer of drought, searing heat and plummeting sales have taken their toll. And Mr. Duluc fears the worst is yet to come. “It’s just the beginning of the crisis,” he said, shaking his head. “But the crisis, I think, will stay a long time.”
His family has been making cognac here since the French Revolution. He’s the eighth generation of Dulucs in charge of the farm, which includes 90 hectares of vines, 20 fermentation vats, a copper distillation system and a shed full of barrels aging some of his finest products.
On a recent morning, Mr. Duluc, 38, was up before sunrise directing the final days of harvesting. His wife, Gwenaelle, wielded a plastic rake as she helped unload a truck filled with freshly picked grapes. His father, Pierre, fixed a broken harvester while his mother, Christine, made lunch for the farm’s six workers who have been with the family for decades.
It’s been an uphill battle. Mr. Duluc said they’ve lost roughly half their crop because of the extreme weather this summer, the hottest on record for France and much of Europe.
Nearly all of their cognac goes to the big players – Rémy Martin and Hennessy – and the buyers haven’t budged on price.
Meanwhile, the cost of fuel and other farm supplies has doubled in the past couple of years.
They have a decent reserve of cognac they can draw on to fulfill their contracts. But a few more summers like this and there’s no telling where they’ll be. “I’m worried about it,” said Mr. Duluc.
This is more than a business for the family. “We love to make cognac,” he said. “We love to talk about it. We love to taste it, and we want other people all around the world to taste it if they want.”
That passion for turning grapes into something almost magical has been at the heart of the broader Bordeaux region for nearly 2,000 years, ever since Romans planted the first vines in the estuary of the Garonne and Dordogne rivers. The region’s mild climate and the estuary’s gravelly soil proved ideal for growing grapes. Today there are nearly 8,000 chateaux making some of the best-known brands of Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot and sweet white wines, in addition to a couple of hundred cognac houses north of the rivers.
Winemaking has long dominated Bordeaux and for decades wineries have had to adjust to changing tastes, most notably in the 1970s when they switched from making mostly white wines to reds.
But the changes many are seeing now – to the climate and the market – are the most serious yet. Summer temperatures of 40C are becoming commonplace and drought has ravaged vineyards. French agriculture officials expect this year’s grape harvest to be one of the lowest in 30 years and the country’s overall wine production is forecast to be 60 per cent lower than its peak in 1979.
The market trends are even more disheartening.
Wine consumption has fallen by 14 per cent since 2018, largely because of shifting social habits, according to the International Organisation of Vine and Wine. In France, where drinking wine was once considered a daily ritual, annual consumption has fallen from more than 100 litres per adult in 1960 to less than 20 litres today.
“We know people who are just saying no to alcohol,” said Manbeen Riar, a 35-year-old Canadian who was on a recent wine-tasting tour in Bordeaux with her husband and her brother. They’ve taken up wine as a hobby, but they don’t drink much at home or when they go out.

“Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that “we’re not supposed to develop nuclear weapons”.
Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on Feb. 28 with US and Israeli attacks.

items.title: Corrections Canada to distribute items for ‘safe snorting’ in federal prisons
items.summary: Paper straws are being introduced for 'safer snorting' and 'intended for inhaling substances in powdered form or inhaling vapour'
items.body_text:
Corrections Canada to distribute items for 'safe snorting' in federal prisons
Paper straws are being introduced for 'safer snorting' and 'intended for inhaling substances in powdered form or inhaling vapour'
The Correctional Service of Canada has confirmed that paper straws will soon be distributed in federal prisons to facilitate safe snorting of drugs.
This week a social media post included photos of a memo distributed to Corrections staff stating that paper straws were being newly “introduced” for “safer snorting” and “intended for inhaling substances in powdered form or inhaling vapour from heated substances.”
The explanation provided was that paper straws will “reduce harm” by lessening the risk of internal nose cuts that could occur from homemade or plastic straws and reduce infections from diseases such as hepatitis B and C, while “recognizing that overdose and toxicity risk remain.”
Meanwhile, according to the memo, foil strips are to be distributed “for safer smoking.” So were drug-testing strips for fentanyl, benzodiazepine and xylazine.
The memo states that these items are being introduced “in response to increased inhalation, smoking and snorting substances among federal inmates” adding that “harm reduction must adapt to reduce overdose risks, prevent the transmission of infectious diseases and align with current evidence-based practices.”
The new harm reduction items if found on their own, should not result in criminal charges, but the memo states that if they are “found alongside illicit substances or unauthorized paraphernalia, standard operational procedures … must be followed.”
In a statement emailed to National Post by Correctional Service Canada communications officer Laurence Côté, the CSC confirmed that the document shown in the social media post is genuine and “was developed … to provide information to all employees regarding the expansion of harm reduction products.”
The CSC stated that its health services include “harm reduction measures” designed to prevent and minimize “harms related to substance use.”
It says its National Drugs and Substances Strategy recognizes substance use as a health issue, and therefore approved harm reduction supplies are not considered contraband.
However, the counterbalance to provide these “safe snorting” items seems to be that the CSC says it “maintains robust measures” to address “introduction, trafficking, financing, and distribution of unauthorized substances … within its institutions, and holds those involved accountable.”
Finally, the CSC stated that harm reduction interventions “are widely recognized as cost-effective because they help prevent the transmission of infectious diseases such as HIV and Hepatitis C, reducing the need for significantly more expensive medical treatment and long-term health care costs associated with these conditions.”
Training for Health Services staff responsible for distributing the supplies to inmates is set to begin on Oct, 1, ahead of planned implementation on Oct. 13. At that time, says the CSC, “Health Services staff will provide education and guidance to support informed and appropriate use of these supplies.”
