items.title: Pope to pilgrims in Lourdes: ‘You will leave as missionaries of hope'
items.summary: In Lourdes, Pope Leo XIV calls pilgrims to conversion and penance, urges the Church to conversion, and invites the sick to see their suffering as part of Christ’s redemptive action. Read all
items.body_text:
Pope to pilgrims in Lourdes: âYou will leave as missionaries of hope'
Vatican News
Celebrating Mass at the Shrine of Our Lady of Lourdes on Sunday, the third day of his apostolic journey to France, Pope Leo XIV said the gathering of pilgrims from France and around the world revealed âthe universal face of the Church,â and he encouraged them to bring âthe consolation of Lourdesâ back to their homes and communities.
Reflecting on the Sunday readings and the message entrusted by the Virgin Mary to Saint Bernadette, the Pope placed conversion at the heart of his homily.
READ THE FULL TEXT OF THE POPE'S HOMILY
Call to conversion
âToday, not tomorrow, that we must repent,â he said, explaining that God desires people to âopen our eyes and return to him.â Conversion, he explained, means leaving behind paths on which we have lost our way and choosing âthe way of life.â
Pope Leo recalled Maryâs words to Saint Bernadette: âI do not promise to make you happy in this world but in the next.â In a society focused on progress and material wellbeing, he said, Lourdes recalls the dignity of every human life and the hope of eternal life.
âIn the face of current trends that seek to redefine the value of human life in illness, suffering and old age, the grotto of Massabielle stands as a place of Christian hope,â he said. At Lourdes, he added, crutches, wheelchairs and âhidden tearsâ are not obstacles but places where people can encounter Godâs love.
âPenance! Penance! Penance!â
The Pope also recalled Maryâs repeated call at Lourdes: âPenance! Penance! Penance!â, noting that Mary asked Bernadette to undertake acts of penance not only for herself but also âfor sinners.â
Linking this appeal to the conflicts and suffering present in the world today, he asked: âHow can our hearts not be moved by the conflicts that are spreading and destroying so many innocent lives?â
Yet, he continued, the roots of evil are found in the human heart. âIt is therefore human hearts that must change, beginning with our own.â
âIt is therefore human hearts that must change, beginning with our own,â he said, stressing that penance is âan act of love, carried out in solidarity with the human family.â
A call to the Church to recognise its faults
That call to conversion, Pope Leo said, applies to the Church herself.
âShe must have the courage to begin with herself,â he said, calling for humility in confronting the Churchâs âdeep wounds, infidelities and painful errors.â Recognising faults, he added, is essential to spiritual growth.
And citing Saint Augustine, he said, âDo not be content with what you are, if you want to become what you are not yet.â
The suffering of the sick at the heart of the Church
The Pope then turned particularly to those who are sick, telling them that their suffering can become a participation in Christâs redemptive work.
âDear friends who are sick, so many of you here in Lourdes are familiar with suffering,â he said. Their trials and pains, when lived in a spirit of offering, can contribute to âthe redemptive work that the world so greatly needs.â
âIn this way,â Pope Leo added, âyou are truly at the heart of the Church, and your role is irreplaceable.â
Pope Leo concluded by telling pilgrims that they would leave Lourdes changed by their encounter with Mary and with one another.
âYou will not leave Lourdes as you arrived. You will leave as missionaries of hope,â he said, adding that âThe miracle of Lourdesâ is that it can âawaken the joy of hope in the very midst of suffering and hardship.â

items.title: Pope to French Bishops: Church bears prophetic authority in public square
items.summary: Meeting with the Bishops of France in Lourdes, Pope Leo XIV upholds the Church’s voice in French society and encourages them to support the spiritual life of families. Read all
items.body_text:
Pope to French Bishops: Church bears prophetic authority in public square
By Devin Watkins
Pope Leo XIV met with the Bishops of France on Sunday in Lourdes, just a short distance from where Our Lady appeared to St. Bernadette Soubirous in 1858.
Thanking them for placing their ministry under the Virgin Maryâs protection, he said there is âno better way to come to Jesus than through Mary.â
Recalling Franceâs deep historical devotion to Our Lady, Pope Leo said the French people bear a living faith, which the Bishops must help grow and deepen.
He encouraged them to show courage and missionary creativity, despite todayâs challenges and human errors.
âAlways have the courage to acknowledge failings with a love of the truth and a determination to bind up wounds with the charity of the Good Shepherd,â he said.
The Church has contributed greatly to building French society, noted Pope Leo, adding that the Churchâs voice has âevery right to be heard in the public square.â
âBy its nature, it possesses a prophetic authority,â he said. âEven if it is not always understood, her voice is nonetheless needed.â
The French Church lives under a particular form of secularity (laïcité), which endured a turbulent history but now enjoys a more peaceful and hard-won balance, which is âgradually being called into question.â
âI urge you to remain vigilant in defending the freedom and rights of the Church to evangelize, to educate about true freedom, and to worship publicly, so that charity may be exercised visibly in the name of Jesus Christ,â he said.
Pope Leo joined the late Pope Francis in urging French Catholics to âreclaim their heritage of faith,â which finds expression in awareness of the inalienable worth of the human person and the flourishing of the arts.
As France and the world faces polarization, a decline in fraternity, and a rise in violence, the Church must remain a prophetic sign of renewal, so that society may hear the hope-filled message of the Gospel.
He encouraged the Bishops to show young people the âsure wayâ of the Gospel in doctrinal clarity and to work with them for all that is âbeautiful, true, and good.â
âTo renew hope and give fresh impetus to the Churchâs mission in France, which I earnestly desire, there is only one âroadmap,â which is always the same: to make Jesus Christ known and loved, authentically, passionately, again and again,â he said.
Pope Leo then pointed to several major challenges facing the Church in France, including Catholic education, which he said must always welcome all people while offering them an opportunity to encounter Christ.
He thanked the Bishops of France for taking âcourageous measuresâ to confront the âpainful scourge of abuse of minors committed by members of the clergy or in an ecclesial context.â
âYou must continue along the path you have begun, maintaining the greatest vigilance,â he said. âAt the same time, your clergy need to be supported and encouraged.â
Pope Leo said priests must be âeagerly wanted, welcomed, and lovedâ and that their identity as men configured to Christ should be understood by the faithful.
He noted the decline in religious vocations, especially to contemplative life, and lamented the closure of âancient and renowned monastic communities,â which have left a deep impact on France.
The Pope encouraged the Bishops to offer their full support for families of French Catholics, so that they may live their faith in Christ fully and help young people dedicate their lives to Him.
âTo give oneâs life to following Jesus along such a demanding path requires, alongside the work of grace, a special generosity, a deep-rooted faith, a sustained interior life, and a privileged closeness to him,â he said.
In conclusion, Pope Leo XIV urged the Bishops of France to remain united in charity and never descend into ideological division, which he said would render their witness in vain.
